blocks.original_text:
- name: customer360__customer_activity_metrics
      description: Customer activity and engagement metrics across marketing, sales, and support with recency, velocity, depth, risk, and intervention signals
      grain: One row per primary_email
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: 'Overview - Start from behavior_analysis (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis, one row per customer) and left join lifecycle_metrics (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics) on primary_email. - Enrich with platform data via left joins on platform IDs: - Marketo: intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on lead_id - Stripe: intermediate.int_customer360__stripe on customer_id - Zendesk: intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk on user_id - Filter: exclude rows where primary_email is NULL; no de-duplication beyond joins. - Time anchors: current_date for recency calculations and current_timestamp for activity_analysis_timestamp; results vary by execution time. - Ordering: rows are sorted by activity_priority_score (desc), then weighted_engagement_score (desc), then active_channel_count (desc). Activity recency and counts - days/weeks/months_since_last_activity: difference between customer_last_activity and current_date by unit; returns NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL. - active_channel_count: integer sum (in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk); if any flag is NULL the sum becomes NULL; expected domain is 0–3 from 0/1 flags. Estimated and adjusted activity (stochastic components) - estimated_monthly_activities: simulated with random() per run based on composite_engagement_score: - >=4.0 → 15 + floor(random()*10) ∈ [15,24] - >=3.0 → 8 + floor(random()*7) ∈ [8,14] - >=2.0 → 3 + floor(random()*5) ∈ [3,7] - >=1.0 → 1 + floor(random()*3) ∈ [1,3] - else → floor(random()*2) ∈ [0,1] - Note: random() yields different results each execution; this column is non-deterministic by design. - seasonally_adjusted_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a month factor (Nov/Dec/Jan ×1.2; Jun/Jul/Aug ×0.8; else ×1.0); no rounding. - predicted_next_month_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a factor from engagement_velocity category (Accelerating ×1.3; Steady High ×1.1; Steady Medium ×1.0; Declining ×0.7; Slow ×0.4; Stagnant ×0.2); no rounding. Engagement velocity, momentum, maturity (rule-based categories) - engagement_velocity (uses activity recency and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.0 → Accelerating - <=14 days and score>=2.5 → Steady High - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Steady Medium - <=60 days → Declining - <=90 days → Slow - else → Stagnant - activity_momentum (uses days_since_last_activity and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.5 → High Momentum - <=14 days and score>=3.0 → Medium Momentum - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Low Momentum - <=60 days → Losing Momentum - else → No Momentum - engagement_maturity (uses account_age_days and active_channel_count): - age>=365 and channels>=3 → Mature Multi-channel - age>=180 and channels>=2 → Developing Multi-channel - age>=90 and channels>=1 → Single Channel Engaged - age<90 → Early Stage - else → Minimal Engagement Channel scores and depths - marketing_engagement_score: if in_marketo=1 and is_unsubscribed=false and is_email_invalid=false then round(marketo_engagement × (1 − days since last Marketo update / 90), 2); else 0; may be negative; if the last update timestamp is NULL the result is NULL in the true branch. - sales_engagement_score: if in_stripe=1 and is_deleted=false and is_delinquent=false then round(stripe_engagement × (1 − days since last Stripe update / 60), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - support_engagement_score: if in_zendesk=1 and is_active=true and is_suspended=false and is_deleted=false then round(zendesk_engagement × (1 − days since last Zendesk update / 120), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - primary_engagement_channel: choose the channel with the highest raw engagement; ties break in order Marketing Driven > Sales Driven > Support Driven; if comparisons do not resolve (e.g., NULL inputs) fallback is Balanced. - marketing_depth/sales_depth/support_depth (per channel): if in_* = 1: engagement>=4 → Deep; engagement>=2 → Medium; else → Shallow; if in_*=0 → None. Cross-platform and composite scores - cross_platform_consistency: round( average of raw engagement across platforms where in_*=1, 2 decimals ); returns NULL if no active platforms or if any included operand (flags or raw engagements) is NULL. - activity_efficiency: round(composite_engagement_score divided by active_channel_count, 2); NULL if active_channel_count is 0 or NULL. - weighted_engagement_score: round(0.3×marketing_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.5×sales_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.2×support_engagement_score (NULL→0), 2); can be negative. - activity_grade: from weighted_engagement_score and active_channel_count: >=4.0 & channels>=3 → A+; >=3.5 & channels>=2 → A; >=3.0 → B+; >=2.5 → B; >=2.0 → C+; >=1.5 → C; >=1.0 → D; else → F. - activity_priority_score: round(0.4×weighted_engagement_score + 0.3×active_channel_count + 0.3×priority_component, 2) where priority_component is 5/4/3/2/1 by recency+composite rules (<=7 days & score>=3.5 → 5; <=14 & score>=3.0 → 4; <=30 & score>=2.0 → 3; <=60 → 2; else → 1). Risk and interventions - activity_risk_level: if days_since_last_activity>90 and customer_health_score<3.0 → High Activity Risk; else if days_since_last_activity>60 or active_channel_count=1 → Medium Activity Risk; else if days_since_last_activity>30 → Low Activity Risk; else → No Activity Risk. - recommended_activity_intervention (evaluated top-to-bottom): Declining/Slow/Stagnant with health>=3.0 → Re-engagement Campaign; else single channel (count=1) with composite>=2.5 → Channel Expansion; else Marketing Driven with in_stripe=0 → Sales Conversion Focus; else Sales Driven with in_zendesk=0 → Success Onboarding; else recent (<=7 days) with composite>=3.5 → Upsell Opportunity; else Standard Engagement.'
      columns:
      - name: marketo_lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Marketo lead identifier sourced from behavior_analysis; may be NULL if not matched
      - name: stripe_customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stripe customer identifier sourced from behavior_analysis; may be NULL if not matched
      - name: zendesk_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Zendesk user identifier sourced from behavior_analysis; may be NULL if not matched
      - name: primary_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer email key; rows with NULL are excluded from output; grain is one row per primary_email
      - name: primary_organization
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer organization from behavior_analysis; passthrough value
      - name: customer_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer segment from behavior_analysis; passthrough value
      - name: customer_journey_pattern
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Journey pattern label from behavior_analysis; passthrough value
      - name: lifecycle_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Lifecycle stage from lifecycle_metrics joined on primary_email; may be NULL
      - name: composite_engagement_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(14,1)
        description: Base composite engagement score from behavior_analysis; used by multiple downstream rules without further rounding
      - name: weighted_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 0.3*marketing_engagement_score + 0.5*sales_engagement_score + 0.2*support_engagement_score rounded to 2 decimals; NULL channel scores treated as 0; may be negative
      - name: customer_health_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(15,2)
        description: Health score from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough value used in risk and intervention logic
      - name: activity_grade
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Letter grade from weighted_engagement_score and active_channel_count with thresholds: A+, A, B+, B, C+, C, D, F as defined in Business Logic'
      - name: activity_priority_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Priority score rounded to 2 decimals: 0.4*weighted_engagement_score + 0.3*active_channel_count + 0.3*recency_component (5–1) per rules'
      - name: days_since_last_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of days between customer_last_activity and current_date; NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL
      - name: weeks_since_last_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of weeks between customer_last_activity and current_date; NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL
      - name: months_since_last_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of months between customer_last_activity and current_date; NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL
      - name: account_age_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Account age in days from behavior_analysis; passthrough value used in maturity logic
      - name: active_channel_count
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Sum of in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk (expected 0–3); NULL if any flag is NULL
      - name: primary_engagement_channel
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Channel with highest raw engagement; ties break Marketing Driven > Sales Driven > Support Driven; fallback Balanced when comparisons cannot be resolved (e.g., NULL inputs)
      - name: marketing_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If in_marketo=1 and not unsubscribed/invalid then mark_engagement×(1 − days since last update/90) rounded to 2 decimals; else 0; may be negative or NULL if updated_at is NULL in the true branch
      - name: sales_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If in_stripe=1 and not deleted and not delinquent then stripe_engagement×(1 − days since last update/60) rounded to 2 decimals; else 0; may be negative or NULL if updated_at is NULL in the true branch
      - name: support_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: If in_zendesk=1 and active and not suspended/deleted then zendesk_engagement×(1 − days since last update/120) rounded to 2 decimals; else 0; may be negative or NULL if updated_at is NULL in the true branch
      - name: marketing_depth
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Depth within Marketo: if in_marketo=1 then engagement>=4 Deep, >=2 Medium, else Shallow; if in_marketo=0 then None'
      - name: sales_depth
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Depth within Stripe: if in_stripe=1 then engagement>=4 Deep, >=2 Medium, else Shallow; if in_stripe=0 then None'
      - name: support_depth
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Depth within Zendesk: if in_zendesk=1 then engagement>=4 Deep, >=2 Medium, else Shallow; if in_zendesk=0 then None'
      - name: engagement_velocity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Velocity category from recency and composite_engagement_score: Accelerating, Steady High, Steady Medium, Declining, Slow, or Stagnant per thresholds'
      - name: activity_momentum
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Momentum category from days_since_last_activity and composite_engagement_score: High/Medium/Low Momentum, Losing Momentum, or No Momentum per thresholds'
      - name: engagement_maturity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Maturity category from account_age_days and active_channel_count: Mature Multi-channel, Developing Multi-channel, Single Channel Engaged, Early Stage, or Minimal Engagement'
      - name: estimated_monthly_activities
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Simulated integer in defined ranges using random() and composite_engagement_score; stochastic and varies each run
      - name: predicted_next_month_activity
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Estimated future activity = estimated_monthly_activities × factor from engagement_velocity (1.3/1.1/1.0/0.7/0.4/0.2); not rounded
      - name: seasonally_adjusted_activity
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Estimated_monthly_activities adjusted by month: Nov–Jan ×1.2, Jun–Aug ×0.8, else ×1.0; not rounded'
      - name: active_30_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 30 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_60_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 60 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_90_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 90 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_180_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 180 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: active_365_days
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Activity metric for last 365 days from lifecycle_metrics; passthrough
      - name: activity_risk_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk category from days_since_last_activity, customer_health_score, and active_channel_count: High/Medium/Low/No Activity Risk per rules'
      - name: cross_platform_consistency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of raw engagement across active platforms (in_*=1) rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if no active platforms or any included operand is NULL
      - name: activity_efficiency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Composite_engagement_score divided by active_channel_count rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if denominator is 0 or NULL
      - name: recommended_activity_intervention
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Intervention label evaluated in order: Re-engagement Campaign, Channel Expansion, Sales Conversion Focus, Success Onboarding, Upsell Opportunity, else Standard Engagement'
      - name: in_marketo
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Channel presence flag from behavior_analysis (expected 0/1); used in counts and conditional logic; may be NULL
      - name: in_stripe
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Channel presence flag from behavior_analysis (expected 0/1); used in counts and conditional logic; may be NULL
      - name: in_zendesk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Channel presence flag from behavior_analysis (expected 0/1); used in counts and conditional logic; may be NULL
      - name: is_unsubscribed
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Marketo unsubscribe flag from platform data; influences marketing_engagement_score
      - name: is_email_invalid
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Marketo invalid email flag from platform data; influences marketing_engagement_score
      - name: do_not_call
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Marketo do-not-call flag from platform data; passthrough
      - name: is_delinquent
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Stripe delinquency flag from platform data; influences sales_engagement_score
      - name: stripe_deleted
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Stripe deletion flag from platform data; influences sales_engagement_score
      - name: zendesk_active
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Zendesk active flag from platform data; required true for support_engagement_score to be computed
      - name: zendesk_suspended
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Zendesk suspended flag from platform data; must be false for support_engagement_score to be computed
      - name: zendesk_deleted
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Zendesk deletion flag from platform data; must be false for support_engagement_score to be computed
      - name: customer_first_touchpoint
        data_type: TIMESTAMP

      - name: customer_last_activity

      - name: activity_analysis_timestamp
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE

CASE WHEN customer_last_activity IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(DATE_DIFF('WEEK', customer_last_activity, CURRENT_DATE) AS BIGINT) END
CASE WHEN customer_last_activity IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(DATE_DIFF('MONTH', customer_last_activity, CURRENT_DATE) AS BIGINT) END

CASE WHEN marketing_engagement_score >= sales_engagement_score AND marketing_engagement_score >= support_engagement_score THEN 'Marketing Driven' WHEN sales_engagement_score >= support_engagement_score THEN 'Sales Driven' WHEN NOT support_engagement_score IS NULL THEN 'Support Driven' ELSE 'Balanced' END
CASE WHEN in_marketo = 1 AND is_unsubscribed = FALSE AND is_email_invalid = FALSE THEN ROUND(marketo_engagement * (1 - DATE_DIFF('DAY', m_updated, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) / 90.0), 2) ELSE 0 END
CASE WHEN in_stripe = 1 AND stripe_deleted = FALSE AND is_delinquent = FALSE THEN ROUND(stripe_engagement * (1 - DATE_DIFF('DAY', s_updated, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) / 60.0), 2) ELSE 0 END

CASE WHEN in_zendesk = 1 AND zendesk_active = TRUE AND zendesk_suspended = FALSE AND zendesk_deleted = FALSE THEN ROUND(zendesk_engagement * (1 - DATE_DIFF('DAY', z_updated, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) / 120.0), 2) ELSE 0 END
CASE WHEN in_marketo = 1 THEN CASE WHEN marketo_engagement >= 4 THEN 'Deep' WHEN marketo_engagement >= 2 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Shallow' END ELSE 'None' END
CASE WHEN in_stripe = 1 THEN CASE WHEN stripe_engagement >= 4 THEN 'Deep' WHEN stripe_engagement >= 2 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Shallow' END ELSE 'None' END
CASE WHEN in_zendesk = 1 THEN CASE WHEN zendesk_engagement >= 4 THEN 'Deep' WHEN zendesk_engagement >= 2 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Shallow' END ELSE 'None' END

CASE WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 7 AND composite_engagement_score >= 3 THEN 'Accelerating' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 14 AND composite_engagement_score >= 2.5 THEN 'Steady High' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 30 AND composite_engagement_score >= 2 THEN 'Steady Medium' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 60 THEN 'Declining' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 90 THEN 'Slow' ELSE 'Stagnant' END

CASE WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 7 AND composite_engagement_score >= 3.5 THEN 'High Momentum' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 14 AND composite_engagement_score >= 3 THEN 'Medium Momentum' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 30 AND composite_engagement_score >= 2 THEN 'Low Momentum' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 60 THEN 'Losing Momentum' ELSE 'No Momentum' END

CASE WHEN account_age_days >= 365 AND active_channel_count >= 3 THEN 'Mature Multi-channel' WHEN account_age_days >= 180 AND active_channel_count >= 2 THEN 'Developing Multi-channel' WHEN account_age_days >= 90 AND active_channel_count >= 1 THEN 'Single Channel Engaged' WHEN account_age_days < 90 THEN 'Early Stage' ELSE 'Minimal Engagement' END

CASE WHEN composite_engagement_score >= 4 THEN 15 + FLOOR(RANDOM() * 10) WHEN composite_engagement_score >= 3 THEN 8 + FLOOR(RANDOM() * 7) WHEN composite_engagement_score >= 2 THEN 3 + FLOOR(RANDOM() * 5) WHEN composite_engagement_score >= 1 THEN 1 + FLOOR(RANDOM() * 3) ELSE FLOOR(RANDOM() * 2) END

estimated_monthly_activities * CASE engagement_velocity WHEN 'Accelerating' THEN 1.3 WHEN 'Steady High' THEN 1.1 WHEN 'Steady Medium' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'Declining' THEN 0.7 WHEN 'Slow' THEN 0.4 ELSE 0.2 END
estimated_monthly_activities * CASE WHEN MONTH(CURRENT_DATE) IN (11, 12, 1) THEN 1.2 WHEN MONTH(CURRENT_DATE) IN (6, 7, 8) THEN 0.8 ELSE 1 END

CASE WHEN days_since_last_activity > 90 AND customer_health_score < 3 THEN 'High Activity Risk' WHEN days_since_last_activity > 60 OR active_channel_count = 1 THEN 'Medium Activity Risk' WHEN days_since_last_activity > 30 THEN 'Low Activity Risk' ELSE 'No Activity Risk' END
ROUND(CASE WHEN in_marketo = 1 THEN marketo_engagement ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN in_stripe = 1 THEN stripe_engagement ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN in_zendesk = 1 THEN zendesk_engagement ELSE 0 END, 2)

CASE WHEN engagement_velocity IN ('Declining', 'Slow', 'Stagnant') AND customer_health_score >= 3 THEN 'Re-engagement Campaign' WHEN active_channel_count = 1 AND composite_engagement_score >= 2.5 THEN 'Channel Expansion' WHEN primary_engagement_channel = 'Marketing Driven' AND in_stripe = 0 THEN 'Sales Conversion Focus' WHEN primary_engagement_channel = 'Sales Driven' AND in_zendesk = 0 THEN 'Success Onboarding' WHEN days_since_last_activity <= 7 AND composite_engagement_score >= 3.5 THEN 'Upsell Opportunity' ELSE 'Standard Engagement' END

references.name: intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
references.line_text: business_logic: 'Overview - Start from behavior_analysis (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis, one row per customer) and left join lifecycle_metrics (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics) on primary_email. - Enrich with platform data via left joins on platform IDs: - Marketo: intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on lead_id - Stripe: intermediate.int_customer360__stripe on customer_id - Zendesk: intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk on user_id - Filter: exclude rows where primary_email is NULL; no de-duplication beyond joins. - Time anchors: current_date for recency calculations and current_timestamp for activity_analysis_timestamp; results vary by execution time. - Ordering: rows are sorted by activity_priority_score (desc), then weighted_engagement_score (desc), then active_channel_count (desc). Activity recency and counts - days/weeks/months_since_last_activity: difference between customer_last_activity and current_date by unit; returns NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL. - active_channel_count: integer sum (in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk); if any flag is NULL the sum becomes NULL; expected domain is 0–3 from 0/1 flags. Estimated and adjusted activity (stochastic components) - estimated_monthly_activities: simulated with random() per run based on composite_engagement_score: - >=4.0 → 15 + floor(random()*10) ∈ [15,24] - >=3.0 → 8 + floor(random()*7) ∈ [8,14] - >=2.0 → 3 + floor(random()*5) ∈ [3,7] - >=1.0 → 1 + floor(random()*3) ∈ [1,3] - else → floor(random()*2) ∈ [0,1] - Note: random() yields different results each execution; this column is non-deterministic by design. - seasonally_adjusted_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a month factor (Nov/Dec/Jan ×1.2; Jun/Jul/Aug ×0.8; else ×1.0); no rounding. - predicted_next_month_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a factor from engagement_velocity category (Accelerating ×1.3; Steady High ×1.1; Steady Medium ×1.0; Declining ×0.7; Slow ×0.4; Stagnant ×0.2); no rounding. Engagement velocity, momentum, maturity (rule-based categories) - engagement_velocity (uses activity recency and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.0 → Accelerating - <=14 days and score>=2.5 → Steady High - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Steady Medium - <=60 days → Declining - <=90 days → Slow - else → Stagnant - activity_momentum (uses days_since_last_activity and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.5 → High Momentum - <=14 days and score>=3.0 → Medium Momentum - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Low Momentum - <=60 days → Losing Momentum - else → No Momentum - engagement_maturity (uses account_age_days and active_channel_count): - age>=365 and channels>=3 → Mature Multi-channel - age>=180 and channels>=2 → Developing Multi-channel - age>=90 and channels>=1 → Single Channel Engaged - age<90 → Early Stage - else → Minimal Engagement Channel scores and depths - marketing_engagement_score: if in_marketo=1 and is_unsubscribed=false and is_email_invalid=false then round(marketo_engagement × (1 − days since last Marketo update / 90), 2); else 0; may be negative; if the last update timestamp is NULL the result is NULL in the true branch. - sales_engagement_score: if in_stripe=1 and is_deleted=false and is_delinquent=false then round(stripe_engagement × (1 − days since last Stripe update / 60), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - support_engagement_score: if in_zendesk=1 and is_active=true and is_suspended=false and is_deleted=false then round(zendesk_engagement × (1 − days since last Zendesk update / 120), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - primary_engagement_channel: choose the channel with the highest raw engagement; ties break in order Marketing Driven > Sales Driven > Support Driven; if comparisons do not resolve (e.g., NULL inputs) fallback is Balanced. - marketing_depth/sales_depth/support_depth (per channel): if in_* = 1: engagement>=4 → Deep; engagement>=2 → Medium; else → Shallow; if in_*=0 → None. business_logic: 'Overview - Start from behavior_analysis (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis, one row per customer) and left join lifecycle_metrics (intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics) on primary_email. - Enrich with platform data via left joins on platform IDs: - Marketo: intermediate.int_customer360__marketo on lead_id - Stripe: intermediate.int_customer360__stripe on customer_id - Zendesk: intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk on user_id - Filter: exclude rows where primary_email is NULL; no de-duplication beyond joins. - Time anchors: current_date for recency calculations and current_timestamp for activity_analysis_timestamp; results vary by execution time. - Ordering: rows are sorted by activity_priority_score (desc), then weighted_engagement_score (desc), then active_channel_count (desc). Activity recency and counts - days/weeks/months_since_last_activity: difference between customer_last_activity and current_date by unit; returns NULL if customer_last_activity is NULL. - active_channel_count: integer sum (in_marketo + in_stripe + in_zendesk); if any flag is NULL the sum becomes NULL; expected domain is 0–3 from 0/1 flags. Estimated and adjusted activity (stochastic components) - estimated_monthly_activities: simulated with random() per run based on composite_engagement_score: - >=4.0 → 15 + floor(random()*10) ∈ [15,24] - >=3.0 → 8 + floor(random()*7) ∈ [8,14] - >=2.0 → 3 + floor(random()*5) ∈ [3,7] - >=1.0 → 1 + floor(random()*3) ∈ [1,3] - else → floor(random()*2) ∈ [0,1] - Note: random() yields different results each execution; this column is non-deterministic by design. - seasonally_adjusted_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a month factor (Nov/Dec/Jan ×1.2; Jun/Jul/Aug ×0.8; else ×1.0); no rounding. - predicted_next_month_activity: estimated_monthly_activities multiplied by a factor from engagement_velocity category (Accelerating ×1.3; Steady High ×1.1; Steady Medium ×1.0; Declining ×0.7; Slow ×0.4; Stagnant ×0.2); no rounding. Engagement velocity, momentum, maturity (rule-based categories) - engagement_velocity (uses activity recency and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.0 → Accelerating - <=14 days and score>=2.5 → Steady High - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Steady Medium - <=60 days → Declining - <=90 days → Slow - else → Stagnant - activity_momentum (uses days_since_last_activity and composite_engagement_score): - <=7 days and score>=3.5 → High Momentum - <=14 days and score>=3.0 → Medium Momentum - <=30 days and score>=2.0 → Low Momentum - <=60 days → Losing Momentum - else → No Momentum - engagement_maturity (uses account_age_days and active_channel_count): - age>=365 and channels>=3 → Mature Multi-channel - age>=180 and channels>=2 → Developing Multi-channel - age>=90 and channels>=1 → Single Channel Engaged - age<90 → Early Stage - else → Minimal Engagement Channel scores and depths - marketing_engagement_score: if in_marketo=1 and is_unsubscribed=false and is_email_invalid=false then round(marketo_engagement × (1 − days since last Marketo update / 90), 2); else 0; may be negative; if the last update timestamp is NULL the result is NULL in the true branch. - sales_engagement_score: if in_stripe=1 and is_deleted=false and is_delinquent=false then round(stripe_engagement × (1 − days since last Stripe update / 60), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - support_engagement_score: if in_zendesk=1 and is_active=true and is_suspended=false and is_deleted=false then round(zendesk_engagement × (1 − days since last Zendesk update / 120), 2); else 0; may be negative; NULL if the last update timestamp is NULL in the true branch. - primary_engagement_channel: choose the channel with the highest raw engagement; ties break in order Marketing Driven > Sales Driven > Support Driven; if comparisons do not resolve (e.g., NULL inputs) fallback is Balanced. - marketing_depth/sales_depth/support_depth (per channel): if in_* = 1: engagement>=4 → Deep; engagement>=2 → Medium; else → Shallow; if in_*=0 → None. Cross-platform and composite scores - cross_platform_consistency: round( average of raw engagement across platforms where in_*=1, 2 decimals ); returns NULL if no active platforms or if any included operand (flags or raw engagements) is NULL. - activity_efficiency: round(composite_engagement_score divided by active_channel_count, 2); NULL if active_channel_count is 0 or NULL. - weighted_engagement_score: round(0.3×marketing_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.5×sales_engagement_score (NULL→0) + 0.2×support_engagement_score (NULL→0), 2); can be negative. - activity_grade: from weighted_engagement_score and active_channel_count: >=4.0 & channels>=3 → A+; >=3.5 & channels>=2 → A; >=3.0 → B+; >=2.5 → B; >=2.0 → C+; >=1.5 → C; >=1.0 → D; else → F. - activity_priority_score: round(0.4×weighted_engagement_score + 0.3×active_channel_count + 0.3×priority_component, 2) where priority_component is 5/4/3/2/1 by recency+composite rules (<=7 days & score>=3.5 → 5; <=14 & score>=3.0 → 4; <=30 & score>=2.0 → 3; <=60 → 2; else → 1). Risk and interventions - activity_risk_level: if days_since_last_activity>90 and customer_health_score<3.0 → High Activity Risk; else if days_since_last_activity>60 or active_channel_count=1 → Medium Activity Risk; else if days_since_last_activity>30 → Low Activity Risk; else → No Activity Risk. - recommended_activity_intervention (evaluated top-to-bottom): Declining/Slow/Stagnant with health>=3.0 → Re-engagement Campaign; else single channel (count=1) with composite>=2.5 → Channel Expansion; else Marketing Driven with in_stripe=0 → Sales Conversion Focus; else Sales Driven with in_zendesk=0 → Success Onboarding; else recent (<=7 days) with composite>=3.5 → Upsell Opportunity; else Standard Engagement.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: customer360__customer_value_analysis
      description: Customer value analysis with RFM, adjusted LTV, portfolio metrics, risk and engagement recommendations
      grain: One row per customer (from int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics) with non-null primary_email
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      business_logic: 'Starting from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics (aliased lm), compute RFM metrics and value segments, then portfolio and recommendation metrics; finally filter to rows where primary_email is not NULL and sort for presentation (sorting does not affect metric values). - Monetary score: bucket lm.estimated_customer_value into {>=5000→5, >=3000→4, >=1500→3, >=800→2, else 1}. - RFM score string: concatenate recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score with no delimiter in R-F-M order; if any component is NULL the result is NULL. - RFM average: average of recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score, rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if any component is NULL. - RFM segment: apply deterministic rules in this order: rfm_avg_score≥4.5→Champions; rfm_avg_score≥4.0 and recency_score≥4→Loyal Customers; rfm_avg_score≥3.5 and monetary_score≥4→Potential Loyalists; recency_score≥4 and frequency_score≤2→New Customers; recency_score≥3 and frequency_score≤2 and monetary_score≤2→Promising; recency_score≥3 and monetary_score≥3→Customers Needing Attention; recency_score≤2 and frequency_score≥3→At Risk; recency_score≤2 and frequency_score≤2 and monetary_score≥4→Cannot Lose Them; recency_score≤1 and frequency_score≥2→Hibernating; else Lost. - Adjusted LTV: estimated_customer_ltv multiplied by lifecycle_stage multiplier {Acquisition 0.3, Activation 0.6, Growth 1.2, Maturity 1.0, Retention 0.8, else 0.5}; not explicitly rounded; stored with 3-decimal precision. - Revenue tier: by estimated_customer_ltv thresholds {≥10000 Tier 1 - Strategic; ≥5000 Tier 2 - High Value; ≥2500 Tier 3 - Core; ≥1000 Tier 4 - Developing; else Tier 5 - Basic}. - Value stability: by customer_health_score and churn_probability {≥4.0 and ≤0.20→High Stability; ≥3.0 and ≤0.40→Medium Stability; ≥2.0 and ≤0.60→Low Stability; else Unstable}. - Upsell potential: {rfm_avg_score≥4.0 and frequency_score≥4→High Upsell; rfm_avg_score≥3.5 and monetary_score≥3→Medium Upsell; recency_score≥4 and frequency_score≤2→Cross-sell Focus; else Retention Focus}. - Expected annual revenue: compute adjusted_ltv × (1 − churn_probability) divided by the age denominator (account_age_days/365.0 when account_age_days≥365, otherwise 1); round to 2 decimals; returns NULL if adjusted_ltv or churn_probability is NULL. - Portfolio contribution pct: adjusted_ltv divided by the total adjusted_ltv across all customers in the portfolio (computed before the final email filter), multiplied by 100 and rounded to 4 decimals; NULL when the portfolio total is 0 or NULL. - Concentration risk: by adjusted_ltv {≥50000→High Concentration Risk; ≥20000→Medium Concentration Risk; else Low Concentration Risk}. - Investment priority score: weighted composite of rfm_segment (40%), revenue_tier (30%), and churn risk (30%), rounded to 2 decimals; segment weights {Champions 5; Loyal Customers 4.5; Potential Loyalists 4; New Customers 3.5; Promising 3; Customers Needing Attention 4.5; At Risk 5; Cannot Lose Them 5; Hibernating 2; else 1}; revenue tier weights {Tier 1 - Strategic 5; Tier 2 - High Value 4; Tier 3 - Core 3; Tier 4 - Developing 2; else 1}; churn risk weights by churn_probability {≥0.70→5; ≥0.50→4; ≥0.30→3; ≥0.10→2; else 1}. - Acquisition ROI assessment: by expected_annual_revenue {≥5000→Excellent ROI; ≥2000→Good ROI; ≥1000→Acceptable ROI; ≥500→Marginal ROI; else→Poor ROI}. - Strategic classification: combine rfm_segment and revenue_tier: {(Champions, Cannot Lose Them)∧(Tier 1, Tier 2)→Strategic Account; (Loyal Customers, Potential Loyalists)∧(Tier 2, Tier 3)→Key Account; (New Customers, Promising)∧(Tier 3, Tier 4)→Growth Account; (At Risk, Hibernating)∧(Tier 1, Tier 2)→Recovery Account; else→Standard Account}. - Recommended engagement model: map strategic_classification {Strategic→Executive Relationship Management; Key→Dedicated Account Management; Growth→Expansion Programs; Recovery→Retention & Recovery Initiatives; else→Standard Engagement}. - Investment recommendation: by investment_priority_score {≥4.5→High Investment; ≥3.5→Medium Investment; ≥2.5→Standard Investment; else→Minimal Investment}. - Success target: by rfm_segment {Champions/Loyal Customers→Maintain Excellence; Potential Loyalists/Customers Needing Attention→Drive Engagement; New Customers/Promising→Accelerate Onboarding; At Risk/Cannot Lose Them→Immediate Intervention; else→Reactivation Required}. - Revenue risk percentage: churn_probability expressed as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if adjusted_ltv is NULL or zero. - Development opportunity: by upsell_potential and value_stability {High Upsell∧High Stability→Premium Growth; High/Medium Upsell→Expansion Ready; Cross-sell Focus→Product Adoption; else→Value Preservation}. - Analysis timestamp: set at query execution time (time zone preserved). - Final filter and ordering: keep only rows with primary_email IS NOT NULL; order by investment_priority_score desc, adjusted_ltv desc, customer_health_score desc.'
      columns:
      - name: marketo_lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Marketo lead identifier from lifecycle metrics; may be NULL if not available
      - name: stripe_customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stripe customer identifier from lifecycle metrics; opaque string; may be NULL
      - name: zendesk_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Zendesk user identifier from lifecycle metrics; may be NULL
      - name: primary_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary customer email; final result filters to non-NULL values
      - name: primary_organization
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer organization name from lifecycle metrics; free text; may be NULL
      - name: customer_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Upstream segment label from lifecycle metrics; not recomputed here
      - name: customer_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Upstream customer tier from lifecycle metrics; not recomputed here
      - name: rfm_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic RFM segment per case rules using rfm_avg_score, recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score
      - name: rfm_score
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Three-digit string formed by concatenating recency, frequency, and monetary scores in R-F-M order with no delimiter; NULL if any component is NULL
      - name: rfm_avg_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if any component is NULL
      - name: recency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Recency score from lifecycle metrics (expected 1–5); higher is more recent; may be NULL
      - name: frequency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Frequency score from lifecycle metrics (expected 1–5); higher is more frequent; may be NULL
      - name: monetary_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Derived spend score (1–5) bucketed from estimated_customer_value using thresholds: >=5000, >=3000, >=1500, >=800, else 1'
      - name: estimated_customer_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,2)
        description: Upstream estimated customer lifetime value in source currency with 2-decimal precision; may be NULL
      - name: adjusted_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,3)
        description: 'Lifecycle-stage-adjusted LTV (multipliers: Acquisition 0.3, Activation 0.6, Growth 1.2, Maturity 1.0, Retention 0.8, else 0.5) stored with 3-decimal precision; not explicitly rounded in SQL'
      - name: expected_annual_revenue
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Adjusted LTV × (1 − churn_probability) divided by account_age_days/365.0 when age≥365, otherwise by 1; rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if adjusted_ltv or churn_probability is NULL
      - name: revenue_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier based on estimated_customer_ltv: >=10000 Tier 1 - Strategic; >=5000 Tier 2 - High Value; >=2500 Tier 3 - Core; >=1000 Tier 4 - Developing; else Tier 5 - Basic'
      - name: strategic_classification
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Account class from rfm_segment and revenue_tier: Strategic, Key, Growth, Recovery, or Standard per deterministic mapping'

CONCAT(CAST(recency_score AS TEXT), CAST(frequency_score AS TEXT), CAST(monetary_score AS TEXT))
CASE WHEN estimated_customer_value >= 5000 THEN 5 WHEN estimated_customer_value >= 3000 THEN 4 WHEN estimated_customer_value >= 1500 THEN 3 WHEN estimated_customer_value >= 800 THEN 2 ELSE 1 END
estimated_customer_ltv * CASE lifecycle_stage WHEN 'Acquisition' THEN 0.3 WHEN 'Activation' THEN 0.6 WHEN 'Growth' THEN 1.2 WHEN 'Maturity' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'Retention' THEN 0.8 ELSE 0.5 END
ROUND(adjusted_ltv * (1 - churn_probability) / CASE WHEN account_age_days >= 365 THEN account_age_days / 365.0 ELSE 1 END, 2)

CASE WHEN estimated_customer_ltv >= 10000 THEN 'Tier 1 - Strategic' WHEN estimated_customer_ltv >= 5000 THEN 'Tier 2 - High Value' WHEN estimated_customer_ltv >= 2500 THEN 'Tier 3 - Core' WHEN estimated_customer_ltv >= 1000 THEN 'Tier 4 - Developing' ELSE 'Tier 5 - Basic' END

CASE WHEN customer_health_score >= 4 AND churn_probability <= 0.2 THEN 'High Stability' WHEN customer_health_score >= 3 AND churn_probability <= 0.4 THEN 'Medium Stability' WHEN customer_health_score >= 2 AND churn_probability <= 0.6 THEN 'Low Stability' ELSE 'Unstable' END

CASE WHEN recency_score >= 4 AND frequency_score >= 4 THEN 'High Upsell' WHEN rfm_avg_score >= 3.5 AND monetary_score >= 3 THEN 'Medium Upsell' WHEN recency_score >= 4 AND frequency_score <= 2 THEN 'Cross-sell Focus' ELSE 'Retention Focus' END
CASE WHEN adjusted_ltv IS NULL OR adjusted_ltv = 0 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(churn_probability * 100, 2) END
CASE WHEN portfolio_ltv = 0 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(adjusted_ltv / portfolio_ltv * 100, 4) END
CASE WHEN adjusted_ltv >= 50000 THEN 'High Concentration Risk' WHEN adjusted_ltv >= 20000 THEN 'Medium Concentration Risk' ELSE 'Low Concentration Risk' END

ROUND((CASE rfm_segment WHEN 'Champions' THEN 5 WHEN 'Loyal Customers' THEN 4.5 WHEN 'Potential Loyalists' THEN 4 WHEN 'New Customers' THEN 3.5 WHEN 'Promising' THEN 3 WHEN 'Customers Needing Attention' THEN 4.5 WHEN 'At Risk' THEN 5 WHEN 'Cannot Lose Them' THEN 5 WHEN 'Hibernating' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END * 0.4 + CASE revenue_tier WHEN 'Tier 1 - Strategic' THEN 5 WHEN 'Tier 2 - High Value' THEN 4 WHEN 'Tier 3 - Core' THEN 3 WHEN 'Tier 4 - Developing' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END * 0.3 + churn_weight * 0.3), 2)

CASE WHEN expected_annual_revenue >= 5000 THEN 'Excellent ROI' WHEN expected_annual_revenue >= 2000 THEN 'Good ROI' WHEN expected_annual_revenue >= 1000 THEN 'Acceptable ROI' WHEN expected_annual_revenue >= 500 THEN 'Marginal ROI' ELSE 'Poor ROI' END

CASE strategic_classification WHEN 'Strategic Account' THEN 'Executive Relationship Management' WHEN 'Key Account' THEN 'Dedicated Account Management' WHEN 'Growth Account' THEN 'Expansion Programs' WHEN 'Recovery Account' THEN 'Retention & Recovery Initiatives' ELSE 'Standard Engagement' END

CASE WHEN investment_priority_score >= 4.5 THEN 'High Investment' WHEN investment_priority_score >= 3.5 THEN 'Medium Investment' WHEN investment_priority_score >= 2.5 THEN 'Standard Investment' ELSE 'Minimal Investment' END

CASE WHEN rfm_segment IN ('Champions', 'Loyal Customers') THEN 'Maintain Excellence' WHEN rfm_segment IN ('Potential Loyalists', 'Customers Needing Attention') THEN 'Drive Engagement' WHEN rfm_segment IN ('New Customers', 'Promising') THEN 'Accelerate Onboarding' WHEN rfm_segment IN ('At Risk', 'Cannot Lose Them') THEN 'Immediate Intervention' ELSE 'Reactivation Required' END

CASE WHEN upsell_potential = 'High Upsell' AND value_stability = 'High Stability' THEN 'Premium Growth' WHEN upsell_potential IN ('High Upsell', 'Medium Upsell') THEN 'Expansion Ready' WHEN upsell_potential = 'Cross-sell Focus' THEN 'Product Adoption' ELSE 'Value Preservation' END
CASE WHEN churn_probability >= 0.7 THEN 'High Risk' WHEN churn_probability >= 0.5 THEN 'Medium Risk' WHEN churn_probability >= 0.3 THEN 'Low Risk' ELSE 'Minimal Risk' END

references.line_text: business_logic: 'Starting from intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics (aliased lm), compute RFM metrics and value segments, then portfolio and recommendation metrics; finally filter to rows where primary_email is not NULL and sort for presentation (sorting does not affect metric values). - Monetary score: bucket lm.estimated_customer_value into {>=5000→5, >=3000→4, >=1500→3, >=800→2, else 1}. - RFM score string: concatenate recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score with no delimiter in R-F-M order; if any component is NULL the result is NULL. - RFM average: average of recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score, rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if any component is NULL. - RFM segment: apply deterministic rules in this order: rfm_avg_score≥4.5→Champions; rfm_avg_score≥4.0 and recency_score≥4→Loyal Customers; rfm_avg_score≥3.5 and monetary_score≥4→Potential Loyalists; recency_score≥4 and frequency_score≤2→New Customers; recency_score≥3 and frequency_score≤2 and monetary_score≤2→Promising; recency_score≥3 and monetary_score≥3→Customers Needing Attention; recency_score≤2 and frequency_score≥3→At Risk; recency_score≤2 and frequency_score≤2 and monetary_score≥4→Cannot Lose Them; recency_score≤1 and frequency_score≥2→Hibernating; else Lost. - Adjusted LTV: estimated_customer_ltv multiplied by lifecycle_stage multiplier {Acquisition 0.3, Activation 0.6, Growth 1.2, Maturity 1.0, Retention 0.8, else 0.5}; not explicitly rounded; stored with 3-decimal precision. - Revenue tier: by estimated_customer_ltv thresholds {≥10000 Tier 1 - Strategic; ≥5000 Tier 2 - High Value; ≥2500 Tier 3 - Core; ≥1000 Tier 4 - Developing; else Tier 5 - Basic}. - Value stability: by customer_health_score and churn_probability {≥4.0 and ≤0.20→High Stability; ≥3.0 and ≤0.40→Medium Stability; ≥2.0 and ≤0.60→Low Stability; else Unstable}. - Upsell potential: {rfm_avg_score≥4.0 and frequency_score≥4→High Upsell; rfm_avg_score≥3.5 and monetary_score≥3→Medium Upsell; recency_score≥4 and frequency_score≤2→Cross-sell Focus; else Retention Focus}. - Expected annual revenue: compute adjusted_ltv × (1 − churn_probability) divided by the age denominator (account_age_days/365.0 when account_age_days≥365, otherwise 1); round to 2 decimals; returns NULL if adjusted_ltv or churn_probability is NULL. - Portfolio contribution pct: adjusted_ltv divided by the total adjusted_ltv across all customers in the portfolio (computed before the final email filter), multiplied by 100 and rounded to 4 decimals; NULL when the portfolio total is 0 or NULL. - Concentration risk: by adjusted_ltv {≥50000→High Concentration Risk; ≥20000→Medium Concentration Risk; else Low Concentration Risk}. - Investment priority score: weighted composite of rfm_segment (40%), revenue_tier (30%), and churn risk (30%), rounded to 2 decimals; segment weights {Champions 5; Loyal Customers 4.5; Potential Loyalists 4; New Customers 3.5; Promising 3; Customers Needing Attention 4.5; At Risk 5; Cannot Lose Them 5; Hibernating 2; else 1}; revenue tier weights {Tier 1 - Strategic 5; Tier 2 - High Value 4; Tier 3 - Core 3; Tier 4 - Developing 2; else 1}; churn risk weights by churn_probability {≥0.70→5; ≥0.50→4; ≥0.30→3; ≥0.10→2; else 1}. - Acquisition ROI assessment: by expected_annual_revenue {≥5000→Excellent ROI; ≥2000→Good ROI; ≥1000→Acceptable ROI; ≥500→Marginal ROI; else→Poor ROI}. - Strategic classification: combine rfm_segment and revenue_tier: {(Champions, Cannot Lose Them)∧(Tier 1, Tier 2)→Strategic Account; (Loyal Customers, Potential Loyalists)∧(Tier 2, Tier 3)→Key Account; (New Customers, Promising)∧(Tier 3, Tier 4)→Growth Account; (At Risk, Hibernating)∧(Tier 1, Tier 2)→Recovery Account; else→Standard Account}. - Recommended engagement model: map strategic_classification {Strategic→Executive Relationship Management; Key→Dedicated Account Management; Growth→Expansion Programs; Recovery→Retention & Recovery Initiatives; else→Standard Engagement}. - Investment recommendation: by investment_priority_score {≥4.5→High Investment; ≥3.5→Medium Investment; ≥2.5→Standard Investment; else→Minimal Investment}. - Success target: by rfm_segment {Champions/Loyal Customers→Maintain Excellence; Potential Loyalists/Customers Needing Attention→Drive Engagement; New Customers/Promising→Accelerate Onboarding; At Risk/Cannot Lose Them→Immediate Intervention; else→Reactivation Required}. - Revenue risk percentage: churn_probability expressed as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals; NULL if adjusted_ltv is NULL or zero. - Development opportunity: by upsell_potential and value_stability {High Upsell∧High Stability→Premium Growth; High/Medium Upsell→Expansion Ready; Cross-sell Focus→Product Adoption; else→Value Preservation}. - Analysis timestamp: set at query execution time (time zone preserved). - Final filter and ordering: keep only rows with primary_email IS NOT NULL; order by investment_priority_score desc, adjusted_ltv desc, customer_health_score desc.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: customer360__email
      description: Unique customer emails per customer360_id with a deterministic 1-based index ordered by email ascending
      grain: One row per unique (customer360_id, email)
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '- Read customer-to-system ID links from marts.customer360__mapping (uses: customer360_id, marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id). - Collect emails from each source via inner joins to mapping: - Marketo: mapping.marketo_lead_id = marketo.lead_id - Stripe: mapping.stripe_customer_id = stripe.customer_id - Zendesk: mapping.zendesk_user_id = zendesk.user_id - Exclude rows where the source email is NULL; preserve original casing and spacing; do not trim or normalize. - Union all collected rows across sources. - De-duplicate to a unique set of (customer360_id, email) using exact string equality. - For each customer360_id, sort emails ascending by their literal value (default lexicographic order) and assign a contiguous 1-based sequential index; output customer360_id, email, and index. - If a customer has no non-NULL emails in any source, no row is emitted for that customer.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer360 ID from mapping; groups emails and defines the partition for indexing; no explicit NULL filtering
      - name: email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Email from Marketo/Stripe/Zendesk via mapping joins; NULLs excluded; duplicates removed by exact string equality; casing and whitespace preserved without normalization
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Contiguous 1-based sequential index within each customer360_id after sorting emails ascending; stable given the same deduplicated email set

      grain: One row per customer360_id
      source_models:

      - name: source_system
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Constant 'marketo' for all rows
      - name: last_seen
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: updated_at from the chosen Marketo row (the most recent per customer360_id; tie and NULL ordering follow the database default)

blocks.original_text:
- name: customer360__mapping
      description: Customer identity mapping linking unified and organizational hashes to source system records and an organization-level header row with aggregated metadata
      grain: 'Mixed: individual rows per combined source record (is_organization_header=false) and one header row per customer360_organization_id (is_organization_header=true)'
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches
      - intermediate.int_customer360__marketo
      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk
      business_logic: '1) Load four inputs: source_matches, marketo, stripe, zendesk. 2) Build combine_all_results: - Chain full outer joins: source_matches to marketo on lead_id, then to stripe on customer_id from source_matches, then to zendesk on user_id from source_matches, retaining all records from every source. - For IDs, prefer the value from source_matches when present; otherwise use the corresponding source table value. - Per-row timestamps: - marketo_updated_at = the most recent non-null updated_at among marketo/stripe/zendesk for that row, taking source_matches timestamps when available, else the source table’s. - marketo_created_at = the earliest non-null created_at among marketo/stripe/zendesk for that row, taking source_matches timestamps when available, else the source table’s. - stripe_updated_at / stripe_created_at = the stripe timestamp from source_matches when present, otherwise from stripe. - zendesk_updated_at / zendesk_created_at = the zendesk timestamp from source_matches when present, otherwise from zendesk. - zendesk_organization_* = the zendesk organization timestamps from source_matches when present, otherwise from zendesk.organization_*. - Union in three additional sets to also include any marketo/stripe/zendesk records whose IDs are not present in source_matches; these rows carry only their own system fields, others null. This can yield duplicates relative to the full outer joins. 3) For each row, derive customer360_organization_id by hashing the pipe-joined values (marketo org name without suffix, marketo inferred org name without suffix, stripe customer org name without suffix, stripe shipping org name without suffix, zendesk organization_id), treating nulls as empty strings. 4) Emit two row types: - Individual rows (is_organization_header=false): include the three source IDs; source_ids is a compact JSON-like object {"marketo":"...","stripe":"...","zendesk":"..."} where null IDs are rendered as empty strings; timestamps are the per-row values from step 2. - One organization header row per customer360_organization_id (is_organization_header=true): source IDs are null; source_ids is a JSON-like object with arrays per system containing distinct quoted IDs for that organization (comma-delimited, no spaces), with nulls rendered as empty strings; timestamps aggregated per organization as latest updated_at and earliest created_at for each system; zendesk organization timestamps use latest for updated and earliest for created. 5) Assign customer360_id by hashing the pipe-joined values (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id, is_organization_header, customer360_organization_id), treating nulls as empty strings and using the engine’s string form of the boolean.'
      columns:
      - name: customer360_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic 32-character hex md5 of marketo_lead_id|stripe_customer_id|zendesk_user_id|is_organization_header|customer360_organization_id with nulls as empty strings and the engine’s string form of the boolean.
      - name: customer360_organization_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic 32-character hex md5 of marketo_org_name_no_suffix|marketo_inferred_org_name_no_suffix|stripe_customer_org_name_no_suffix|stripe_shipping_org_name_no_suffix|zendesk_organization_id with nulls as empty strings.
      - name: marketo_lead_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Marketo lead ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else marketo; null on organization header rows.
      - name: stripe_customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stripe customer ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else stripe; null on organization header rows.
      - name: zendesk_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Zendesk user ID; on individual rows prefer source_matches, else zendesk; null on organization header rows.
      - name: is_organization_header
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: 'Row type flag: false for individual rows; true for the single aggregated header row per customer360_organization_id.'
      - name: source_ids
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'JSON-like string; individual rows: {"marketo":"...","stripe":"...","zendesk":"..."} with nulls as empty strings; header rows: arrays per system of distinct quoted IDs joined by commas (no spaces), nulls as empty strings, order not enforced.'
      - name: marketo_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: latest non-null updated_at across marketo, stripe, and zendesk after preferring source_matches timestamps; header rows: latest marketo_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: marketo_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: earliest non-null created_at across marketo, stripe, and zendesk after preferring source_matches timestamps; header rows: earliest marketo_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: stripe_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: stripe updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from stripe; header rows: latest stripe_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: stripe_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: stripe created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from stripe; header rows: earliest stripe_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: latest zendesk_updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_organization_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk organization_updated_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: latest org updated_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: earliest zendesk_created_at in the organization; null if none.'
      - name: zendesk_organization_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Individual rows: zendesk organization_created_at from source_matches when available, otherwise from zendesk; header rows: earliest org created_at in the organization; null if none.'

- name: customer360__name
      description: Deduplicated customer full names from Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk with lexicographic variant indexing per customer360_id
      grain: One row per unique full_name per customer360_id
      source_models:
      - marts.customer360__mapping

      - intermediate.int_customer360__stripe
      - intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk

      columns:

        description: Customer key; one row per unique full_name within each customer360_id.
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name taken as-is from upstream cleaned fields; NULLs are excluded, empty strings may appear; deduplicated per customer360_id; the exact string determines ordering for index.
      - name: index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Sequential position within each customer360_id after deduplication, starting at 1 and ordered by full_name ascending; consecutive integers with no gaps; not based on source priority.

- name: customer360__organization_network
      description: Organization-level network, value, health, engagement, risk, ranking, and strategy metrics grouped by standardized_org_name + email_domain (INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER excluded)
      grain: One row per (standardized_org_name, email_domain, organization_type, estimated_org_size)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_behavior_analysis
      - intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics
      - marts.customer360__customer_value_analysis
      business_logic: '- Build organization_entities: - Join behavior_analysis to lifecycle_metrics on primary_email; join behavior_analysis to value_analysis on primary_email. - Retain ids (marketo_lead_id, stripe_customer_id, zendesk_user_id), journey/segment fields, LTV/health/engagement fields. - Standardize fields: - standardized_org_name: uppercase and trim primary_organization; if null/blank set "INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER". - email_domain: take the substring after "@" in primary_email; if missing set "unknown.domain". - organization_type by primary_organization text patterns: - null/blank → Individual - contains inc/corp/llc/ltd → Corporation - contains university/college/school → Education - contains government/dept/agency → Government - contains nonprofit/foundation/charity → Non-Profit - otherwise → Business - estimated_org_size: - domain in {gmail.com,yahoo.com,hotmail.com,outlook.com} → Personal - domain in {microsoft.com,google.com,amazon.com,apple.com,facebook.com} → Enterprise - else if name length > 20 → Large Business; > 10 → Medium Business; > 0 → Small Business; otherwise → Individual - Aggregate to organization_aggregates at (standardized_org_name, email_domain, organization_type, estimated_org_size): - Counts (distinct primary_email): total_contacts; marketing_contacts when marketo_lead_id present; sales_contacts when stripe_customer_id present; support_contacts when zendesk_user_id present. - Journey distribution: full_journey_contacts when journey pattern = "Full Journey"; also compute marketing_to_sales_contacts and sales_to_support_contacts (used downstream). - Value metrics: total_organization_ltv (sum of estimated_customer_ltv), avg_customer_ltv, highest_customer_ltv (max), total_adjusted_ltv (sum). - Engagement/health: avg_engagement_score (average composite_engagement_score), max_engagement_score (max), avg_health_score (average customer_health_score). - Strategic classification: strategic_accounts, key_accounts, growth_accounts, recovery_accounts from strategic_classification. - Revenue tiers: tier1_contacts, tier2_contacts, tier3_contacts from revenue_tier. - Customer segments: champions, loyal_customers, at_risk_customers from customer_segment. - Lifecycle stages (for health calc): growth_stage_contacts when stage = "Growth"; maturity_stage_contacts when stage = "Maturity"; dormant_contacts when stage = "Dormant". - Diversity: email_domains_count = distinct email_domain within the group (will be 1); customer_tiers_represented = distinct customer_tier. - Compute organization_scoring: - organization_value_score: weighted sum of three 1–5 tiers, rounded to two decimals (stored with one-decimal precision): - LTV tier: ≥50000→5; ≥25000→4; ≥10000→3; ≥5000→2; else→1 (weight 0.4). - Contacts tier: ≥10→5; ≥5→4; ≥3→3; ≥2→2; else→1 (weight 0.3). - Avg engagement tier: ≥4.0→5; ≥3.0→4; ≥2.5→3; ≥2.0→2; else→1 (weight 0.3). - organization_health_score: 0.4×avg_health_score + 0.3×(champions+loyal_customers)/total_contacts×5 + 0.3×(growth_stage_contacts+maturity_stage_contacts)/total_contacts×5; if total_contacts=0, both ratios are 0; round to two decimals. - account_penetration_score: share of contacts linked across marketing, sales, and support out of three touchpoints, scaled to a 0–5 score and rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0. - organization_maturity: - if total_contacts≥10 and full_journey_contacts≥3 → Mature Enterprise - else if total_contacts≥5 and (strategic_accounts+key_accounts)≥2 → Developing Enterprise - else if total_contacts≥3 and total_organization_ltv≥10000 → Mid-Market - else if total_contacts≥2 → Small Business - else → Individual/Micro - growth_potential: - if growth_accounts≥2 and avg_engagement_score≥3.0 → High Growth Potential - else if growth_accounts≥1 or avg_engagement_score≥3.5 → Medium Growth Potential - else if total_contacts≥2 and avg_health_score≥3.0 → Stable Growth Potential - else → Limited Growth Potential - organization_risk_level: - if at_risk_customers ≥ 50% of total_contacts → High Risk - else if dormant_contacts ≥ 30% of total_contacts → Medium Risk - else if recovery_accounts ≥ 1 → Attention Needed - else → Stable - strategic_value_tier: - if strategic_accounts≥2 or total_organization_ltv≥100000 → Strategic Enterprise - else if key_accounts≥2 or total_organization_ltv≥50000 → Key Enterprise - else if total_contacts≥5 or total_organization_ltv≥25000 → Important Account - else if total_contacts≥2 or total_organization_ltv≥10000 → Standard Account - else → Small Account - engagement_breadth_percentage: weighted coverage across marketing (30%), sales (40%), and support (30%) among contacts, expressed as a percentage and rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0. - concentration_risk: - if total_contacts=1 → High Concentration Risk - else if total_contacts≤3 → Medium Concentration Risk - else if email_domains_count=1 and total_contacts≥5 → Domain Concentration Risk - else → Low Concentration Risk - Perform network_analysis: - market_share_within_type: percent share of total_organization_ltv within the same organization_type, rounded to four decimals; null when the type total is zero. - Rankings within organization_type: ltv_rank_within_type by total_organization_ltv descending; contacts_rank_within_type by total_contacts descending; value_score_rank_within_type by organization_value_score descending; ties break arbitrarily. - cross_sell_opportunity_score (integer 0–7): sum of three components, then rounded (remains integer): - Channel gap: if total_contacts≥5 and marketing_contacts=0 →3; else if total_contacts≥3 and sales_contacts=0 →3; else if total_contacts≥2 and support_contacts=0 →2; else →0. - Growth: High Growth Potential →2; Medium Growth Potential →1; else →0. - Engagement: avg_engagement_score≥3.5 →2; ≥3.0 →1; else →0. - expansion_priority: - if strategic_value_tier in {Strategic Enterprise, Key Enterprise} and growth_potential=High Growth Potential → Immediate Expansion - else if organization_value_score≥4.0 and organization_health_score≥4.0 → High Priority Expansion - else if total_contacts≥3 and avg_engagement_score≥3.0 → Medium Priority Expansion - else if total_contacts≥2 and organization_risk_level=Stable → Low Priority Expansion - else → Maintenance Mode - recommended_strategy: - if organization_risk_level=High Risk → Risk Mitigation & Recovery - else if strategic_value_tier=Strategic Enterprise → White Glove Account Management - else if strategic_value_tier=Key Enterprise → Dedicated Account Management - else if growth_potential=High Growth Potential → Growth & Expansion Focus - else if total_contacts=1 → Relationship Expansion - else → Standard Account Management - Finalization: - organization_influence_score: weighted score rounded to two decimals = 0.3×organization_value_score + 0.3×contacts tier (≥10→5; ≥5→4; ≥3→3; ≥2→2; else→1) + 0.2×breadth tier (≥80→5; ≥60→4; ≥40→3; ≥20→2; else→1) + 0.2×market-share tier (≥10→5; ≥5→4; ≥2→3; ≥1→2; else→1). - risk_adjusted_organization_value: total_adjusted_ltv multiplied by expansion priority multiplier (Immediate 1.5; High 1.3; Medium 1.1; else 1.0), then reduced by risk penalty (High Risk 40%; Medium Risk 20%; Attention Needed 10%; else 0%), rounded to two decimals. - network_analysis_timestamp: set to the current timestamp at computation time. - Exclude rows where standardized_org_name = "INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER". - Order output by organization_influence_score (desc), then total_organization_ltv (desc), then total_contacts (desc).'
      columns:
      - name: standardized_org_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Uppercased, trimmed organization name from behavior_analysis; null/blank becomes 'INDIVIDUAL_CUSTOMER' and is excluded from final output
      - name: email_domain
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Substring after '@' in primary_email; if missing set to 'unknown.domain'
      - name: organization_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Derived from primary_organization patterns: Individual, Corporation, Education, Government, Non-Profit, or Business'
      - name: estimated_org_size
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Size class from email_domain and name length: Personal, Enterprise, Large/Medium/Small Business, or Individual'
      - name: organization_maturity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Mature Enterprise if contacts≥10 and full_journey≥3; Developing Enterprise if contacts≥5 and strategic+key≥2; Mid-Market if contacts≥3 and org LTV≥10000; Small Business if contacts≥2; else Individual/Micro
      - name: strategic_value_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Strategic Enterprise if strategic≥2 or org LTV≥100000; Key Enterprise if key≥2 or org LTV≥50000; Important if contacts≥5 or org LTV≥25000; Standard if contacts≥2 or org LTV≥10000; else Small
      - name: total_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of primary_email within the group
      - name: marketing_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count with a marketo_lead_id present
      - name: sales_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count with a stripe_customer_id present
      - name: support_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count with a zendesk_user_id present
      - name: email_domains_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of email_domain within the group; equals 1 due to grouping by email_domain
      - name: customer_tiers_represented
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of customer_tier values within the group
      - name: total_organization_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of estimated_customer_ltv over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: total_adjusted_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,3)
        description: Sum of adjusted_ltv over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: avg_customer_ltv
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of estimated_customer_ltv over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: highest_customer_ltv
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,2)
        description: Maximum estimated_customer_ltv over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: risk_adjusted_organization_value
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Total_adjusted_ltv scaled by expansion priority multiplier and reduced by risk penalty; rounded to two decimals
      - name: organization_value_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(14,1)
        description: Weighted score from LTV tier (40%), contacts tier (30%), and avg engagement tier (30%); rounded and stored with one-decimal precision
      - name: organization_influence_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,2)
        description: Weighted score from value score, contacts tier, engagement breadth tier, and market share tier; rounded to two decimals
      - name: avg_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average composite_engagement_score over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: max_engagement_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(14,1)
        description: Maximum composite_engagement_score over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: avg_health_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average customer_health_score over grouped rows; null if all values are null
      - name: organization_health_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Weighted composite of avg_health_score and stage/segment ratios using total_contacts as denominator; rounded to two decimals
      - name: account_penetration_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Scaled 0–5 score of contact presence across marketing, sales, and support relative to all contacts; rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0
      - name: engagement_breadth_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Weighted coverage across marketing (30%), sales (40%), and support (30%) as a percentage; rounded to two decimals; 0 when total_contacts=0
      - name: full_journey_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_journey_pattern is 'Full Journey'
      - name: strategic_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Strategic Account'
      - name: key_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Key Account'
      - name: growth_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Growth Account'
      - name: recovery_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where strategic_classification is 'Recovery Account'
      - name: champions
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_segment is 'Champion'
      - name: loyal_customers
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_segment is 'Loyal Customer'
      - name: at_risk_customers
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where customer_segment is 'At Risk'
      - name: tier1_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where revenue_tier is 'Tier 1 - Strategic'
      - name: tier2_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where revenue_tier is 'Tier 2 - High Value'
      - name: tier3_contacts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct primary_email count where revenue_tier is 'Tier 3 - Core'
      - name: organization_risk_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Risk label based on at-risk share, dormant share, and recovery_accounts presence
      - name: concentration_risk
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact concentration label from total_contacts and email_domains_count, with a domain concentration flag when only one domain and contacts≥5
      - name: growth_potential
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Growth label from growth_accounts and avg_engagement_score, with stable or limited when thresholds not met
      - name: cross_sell_opportunity_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Integer 0–7 from the sum of channel gap, growth, and engagement components; rounding does not change the integer value
      - name: expansion_priority
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Priority label from strategic tier and growth potential, then value/health scores, then engagement and stability
      - name: recommended_strategy
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Strategy label based on risk level, strategic tier, growth potential, and contact count
      - name: market_share_within_type
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent share of total_organization_ltv within the same organization_type; rounded to four decimals; null when the type total is zero
      - name: ltv_rank_within_type
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Position within organization_type when sorted by total_organization_ltv descending; ties break arbitrarily
      - name: contacts_rank_within_type
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Position within organization_type when sorted by total_contacts descending; ties break arbitrarily
      - name: value_score_rank_within_type
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Position within organization_type when sorted by organization_value_score descending; ties break arbitrarily
      - name: network_analysis_timestamp
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Current timestamp captured at computation time
