blocks.original_text:
- name: hubspot__sales_rep_performance
      schema: sales
      description: Sales representative performance analytics with rankings, segment metrics, trends, and derived classifications
      grain: One row per owner_id (only reps with total_deals > 0)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_hubspot__owner_performance_metrics
      - intermediate.int_hubspot__deal_performance_metrics
      business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_hubspot__owner_performance_metrics and retain only owners where total_deals > 0. - Build monthly deal performance per owner from intermediate.int_hubspot__deal_performance_metrics: - Group by owner_id and the year/month of created_date; exclude rows where created_date is NULL. - monthly_deals_created: count distinct deal_id per month. - monthly_deals_won: count distinct deal_id where deal_status = ''Won''. - monthly_revenue: sum deal_amount where deal_status = ''Won'' (0 otherwise). - monthly_pipeline_added: sum deal_amount where deal_status = ''Open'' (0 otherwise). - monthly_win_rate: if decided deals (Won or Lost) exist, compute 100 × (won / decided); otherwise 0. - monthly_avg_cycle_time: average deal_cycle_time_days for won deals; NULL if none. - Aggregate per-owner trends over monthly data: - Use month_index = performance_year*12 + performance_month and current_month_index from current_date. - recent_6m_avg_revenue: average monthly_revenue where month_index >= current_month_index - 6 (inclusive). - prior_6m_avg_revenue: average monthly_revenue where month_index between current_month_index - 12 and current_month_index - 7 (inclusive). - recent_6m_avg_win_rate / prior_6m_avg_win_rate: analogous averages over monthly_win_rate (percent values). - revenue_volatility: standard deviation of monthly_revenue; activity_consistency: standard deviation of monthly_deals_created. - recent_active_months: count of monthly rows in the last 3 calendar months (relative to current_date), inclusive. - Territory and segment analysis per owner from all deals: - primary_deal_segment: most frequent deal_size_category; ties break by ascending category label. - segments_covered: count distinct deal_size_category. - enterprise/large/medium/small_revenue: sum won deal_amount within each named deal_size_category. - enterprise_win_rate / large_deal_win_rate: if decided deals in the segment exist, compute 100 × (won / decided); otherwise 0. - Rankings and percentiles from owner metrics: - revenue_rank: best-to-worst by total_won_revenue; win_rate_rank: best-to-worst by win_rate_percentage; volume_rank: best-to-worst by won_deals. - efficiency_rank: best-to-worst by avg_won_cycle_time, treating NULL as 999. - revenue_percentile / win_rate_percentile / volume_percentile: percentile position (0–100) across all reps using ascending order of each metric; peers share the same percentile. - efficiency_percentile: percentile position (0–100) using descending order of avg_won_cycle_time, treating NULL as 999 (longer cycles → higher percentile). - overall_performance_score: weighted sum of these percentiles (revenue 40%, win rate 25%, volume 20%, efficiency 15%), then scaled by ×100 to a 0–10,000 range. - Ties in ranks are resolved by the database’s implicit peer order. - Join rankings to trends and territory by owner_id (cast trend/territory owner_id to VARCHAR); unmatched trend/territory values remain NULL. - Derivations: - revenue_trend_percentage: if prior_6m_avg_revenue > 0 and recent_6m_avg_revenue is not NULL, compute 100 × (recent - prior) / prior; else NULL. - win_rate_trend_points: if prior_6m_avg_win_rate > 0 and recent_6m_avg_win_rate is not NULL, compute recent - prior; else NULL. - performance_tier: >=80 Top Performer; >=60 High Performer; >=40 Core Performer; >=20 Developing Performer; else Needs Improvement. - performance_trend: >=20 Strong Growth; >=5 Steady Growth; >=-5 Stable; >=-20 Declining; else Significant Decline (NULLs map to the else). - sales_specialization: Enterprise Specialist if enterprise_revenue strictly exceeds (large + medium + small); Large Deal Specialist if large_revenue strictly exceeds (enterprise + medium + small); else if segments_covered >= 3 then Generalist; otherwise Focused Seller. - development_focus (first-match order): low win rate + long cycle → Focus on Qualification and Process; low win rate → Improve Win Rate; very long cycle → Accelerate Sales Cycle; few wins → Increase Activity Volume; declining revenue trend → Address Performance Decline; else Maintain Current Performance. - activity_level (first-match): Highly Active (recent_active_months >= 3 and total_deals >= 10); Active (recent_active_months >= 2 and total_deals >= 5); Moderately Active (recent_active_months >= 1); else Low Activity. - pipeline_health_status: compare current_pipeline_value to total_won_revenue thresholds: >=2× Strong Pipeline; >=1× Healthy Pipeline; >=0.5× Adequate Pipeline; else Weak Pipeline. - Output rows are ordered by overall_performance_score descending.'
      columns:
      - name: owner_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Sales rep identifier; grouping key; exactly one output row per owner_id with total_deals > 0
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: owner_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Sales rep name from owner metrics; passed through from source (may be NULL)
      - name: owner_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Sales rep email from owner metrics; passed through from source (may be NULL)
      - name: total_deals
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total number of deals attributed to the rep from owner metrics; used for filters and activity_level thresholds
      - name: won_deals
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of won deals from owner metrics; used for volume_rank and development_focus
      - name: total_won_revenue
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of deal_amount for won deals from owner metrics; basis for revenue_rank, revenue_percentile, and pipeline health thresholds
      - name: win_rate_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Overall win rate percentage (0–100) from owner metrics; used for win_rate_rank and percentiles
      - name: avg_won_cycle_time
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days to close for won deals from owner metrics; NULL permitted; for ranking, NULL treated as 999
      - name: current_pipeline_value
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Current open pipeline value from owner metrics (alias of pipeline_value); used for pipeline_health_status thresholds
      - name: enterprise_win_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Enterprise (100K+) segment win rate in percent; if no decided enterprise deals then 0; computed as 100×won/decided
      - name: large_deal_win_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Large (50K-100K) segment win rate in percent; if no decided large deals then 0; computed as 100×won/decided
      - name: enterprise_revenue
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of won deal_amount in Enterprise (100K+) segment; NULL if no territory data joined
      - name: large_revenue
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of won deal_amount in Large (50K-100K) segment; NULL if no territory data joined
      - name: medium_revenue
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of won deal_amount in Medium (10K-50K) segment; NULL if no territory data joined
      - name: small_revenue
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of won deal_amount in Small (<10K) segment; NULL if no territory data joined
      - name: revenue_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Integer rank by total_won_revenue descending across all reps; 1 is highest revenue; ties resolved by peer order
      - name: win_rate_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Integer rank by win_rate_percentage descending across all reps; 1 is highest win rate; ties resolved by peer order
      - name: volume_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Integer rank by won_deals descending across all reps; 1 is most wins; ties resolved by peer order
      - name: efficiency_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Integer rank by avg_won_cycle_time ascending, treating NULL as 999; 1 is shortest cycle; ties resolved by peer order
      - name: revenue_percentile
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentile (0–100) using ascending order of total_won_revenue; peers share the same percentile
      - name: win_rate_percentile
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentile (0–100) using ascending order of win_rate_percentage; peers share the same percentile
      - name: volume_percentile
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentile (0–100) using ascending order of won_deals; peers share the same percentile
      - name: efficiency_percentile
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percentile (0–100) using descending order of avg_won_cycle_time with NULL treated as 999; higher values indicate longer cycles
      - name: overall_performance_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Weighted sum of percentiles (revenue 40%, win rate 25%, volume 20%, efficiency 15%) scaled by ×100; range 0–10,000
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier by overall_performance_score: >=80 Top, >=60 High, >=40 Core, >=20 Developing, else Needs Improvement'
      - name: sales_specialization
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Enterprise Specialist if enterprise_revenue > (large + medium + small), Large Deal Specialist if large_revenue > (enterprise + medium + small), else Generalist if segments_covered >= 3, otherwise Focused Seller
      - name: development_focus
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'First-match guidance: low win rate + long cycle → process; low win rate → improve; very long cycle → accelerate; few wins → increase volume; declining trend → address; else maintain'
      - name: pipeline_health_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Pipeline health by current_pipeline_value versus total_won_revenue: >=2x Strong, >=1x Healthy, >=0.5x Adequate, else Weak'
      - name: primary_deal_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Most frequent deal_size_category with tie-break by ascending label; NULL if no deal data
      - name: segments_covered
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of distinct deal_size_category values across the rep’s deals; NULL if no deal data
      - name: activity_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Activity classification by recent_active_months and total_deals with ordered thresholds: Highly Active, Active, Moderately Active, or Low Activity'
      - name: activity_consistency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Standard deviation of monthly_deals_created; higher implies more variability; may be NULL with limited data
      - name: recent_active_months
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of months in the last 3-month window with any monthly activity row (based on created_date); integer >= 0
      - name: performance_trend
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Trend label from revenue_trend_percentage: >=20 Strong Growth, >=5 Steady Growth, >=-5 Stable, >=-20 Declining, else Significant Decline (NULLs map to else)'
      - name: revenue_trend_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent change between recent_6m_avg_revenue and prior_6m_avg_revenue; NULL if prior <= 0 or recent is NULL
      - name: win_rate_trend_points
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Difference in percentage points between recent_6m_avg_win_rate and prior_6m_avg_win_rate; NULL if prior <= 0 or recent is NULL
      - name: revenue_volatility
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Standard deviation of monthly_revenue; may be NULL with limited data
      - name: recent_6m_avg_revenue
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average monthly_revenue where month_index >= current_month_index - 6; includes months with zero revenue if present; NULL if no months
      - name: prior_6m_avg_revenue
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average monthly_revenue where month_index is between current_month_index - 12 and current_month_index - 7; NULL if no months
      - name: recent_6m_avg_win_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average monthly_win_rate (percent) where month_index >= current_month_index - 6; NULL if no months
      - name: prior_6m_avg_win_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average monthly_win_rate (percent) where month_index is between current_month_index - 12 and current_month_index - 7; NULL if no months

alternatives.expression_sql: CASE WHEN overall_performance_score >= 80 THEN 'Top Performer' WHEN overall_performance_score >= 60 THEN 'High Performer' WHEN overall_performance_score >= 40 THEN 'Core Performer' WHEN overall_performance_score >= 20 THEN 'Developing Performer' ELSE 'Needs Improvement' END

CASE WHEN enterprise_revenue > COALESCE(large_revenue, 0) + COALESCE(medium_revenue, 0) + COALESCE(small_revenue, 0) THEN 'Enterprise Specialist' WHEN large_revenue > COALESCE(enterprise_revenue, 0) + COALESCE(medium_revenue, 0) + COALESCE(small_revenue, 0) THEN 'Large Deal Specialist' WHEN segments_covered >= 3 THEN 'Generalist' ELSE 'Focused Seller' END

CASE WHEN win_rate_percentage < 15 AND avg_won_cycle_time > 90 THEN 'Focus on Qualification and Process' WHEN win_rate_percentage < 15 THEN 'Improve Win Rate' WHEN avg_won_cycle_time > 120 THEN 'Accelerate Sales Cycle' WHEN won_deals < 5 THEN 'Increase Activity Volume' WHEN revenue_trend_percentage < -5 THEN 'Address Performance Decline' ELSE 'Maintain Current Performance' END

CASE WHEN pipeline_value >= 2 * total_won_revenue THEN 'Strong Pipeline' WHEN pipeline_value >= total_won_revenue THEN 'Healthy Pipeline' WHEN pipeline_value >= 0.5 * total_won_revenue THEN 'Adequate Pipeline' ELSE 'Weak Pipeline' END

CASE WHEN recent_active_months >= 3 AND total_deals >= 10 THEN 'Highly Active' WHEN recent_active_months >= 2 AND total_deals >= 5 THEN 'Active' WHEN recent_active_months >= 1 THEN 'Moderately Active' ELSE 'Low Activity' END

CASE WHEN revenue_trend_percentage >= 20 THEN 'Strong Growth' WHEN revenue_trend_percentage >= 5 THEN 'Steady Growth' WHEN revenue_trend_percentage >= -5 THEN 'Stable' WHEN revenue_trend_percentage >= -20 THEN 'Declining' ELSE 'Significant Decline' END
CASE WHEN t.prior_6m_avg_revenue > 0 THEN 100 * (t.recent_6m_avg_revenue - t.prior_6m_avg_revenue) / t.prior_6m_avg_revenue END
CASE WHEN t.prior_6m_avg_win_rate > 0 THEN t.recent_6m_avg_win_rate - t.prior_6m_avg_win_rate END
AVG(monthly_revenue) FILTER(WHERE month_index BETWEEN YEAR(CURRENT_DATE) * 12 + MONTH(CURRENT_DATE) - 12 AND YEAR(CURRENT_DATE) * 12 + MONTH(CURRENT_DATE) - 7)
AVG(monthly_win_rate) FILTER(WHERE month_index BETWEEN YEAR(CURRENT_DATE) * 12 + MONTH(CURRENT_DATE) - 12 AND YEAR(CURRENT_DATE) * 12 + MONTH(CURRENT_DATE) - 7)

references.name: intermediate.int_hubspot__owner_performance_metrics
references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_hubspot__owner_performance_metrics and retain only owners where total_deals > 0. - Build monthly deal performance per owner from intermediate.int_hubspot__deal_performance_metrics: - Group by owner_id and the year/month of created_date; exclude rows where created_date is NULL. - monthly_deals_created: count distinct deal_id per month. - monthly_deals_won: count distinct deal_id where deal_status = ''Won''. - monthly_revenue: sum deal_amount where deal_status = ''Won'' (0 otherwise). - monthly_pipeline_added: sum deal_amount where deal_status = ''Open'' (0 otherwise). - monthly_win_rate: if decided deals (Won or Lost) exist, compute 100 × (won / decided); otherwise 0. - monthly_avg_cycle_time: average deal_cycle_time_days for won deals; NULL if none. - Aggregate per-owner trends over monthly data: - Use month_index = performance_year*12 + performance_month and current_month_index from current_date. - recent_6m_avg_revenue: average monthly_revenue where month_index >= current_month_index - 6 (inclusive). - prior_6m_avg_revenue: average monthly_revenue where month_index between current_month_index - 12 and current_month_index - 7 (inclusive). - recent_6m_avg_win_rate / prior_6m_avg_win_rate: analogous averages over monthly_win_rate (percent values). - revenue_volatility: standard deviation of monthly_revenue; activity_consistency: standard deviation of monthly_deals_created. - recent_active_months: count of monthly rows in the last 3 calendar months (relative to current_date), inclusive. - Territory and segment analysis per owner from all deals: - primary_deal_segment: most frequent deal_size_category; ties break by ascending category label. - segments_covered: count distinct deal_size_category. - enterprise/large/medium/small_revenue: sum won deal_amount within each named deal_size_category. - enterprise_win_rate / large_deal_win_rate: if decided deals in the segment exist, compute 100 × (won / decided); otherwise 0. - Rankings and percentiles from owner metrics: - revenue_rank: best-to-worst by total_won_revenue; win_rate_rank: best-to-worst by win_rate_percentage; volume_rank: best-to-worst by won_deals. - efficiency_rank: best-to-worst by avg_won_cycle_time, treating NULL as 999. - revenue_percentile / win_rate_percentile / volume_percentile: percentile position (0–100) across all reps using ascending order of each metric; peers share the same percentile. - efficiency_percentile: percentile position (0–100) using descending order of avg_won_cycle_time, treating NULL as 999 (longer cycles → higher percentile). - overall_performance_score: weighted sum of these percentiles (revenue 40%, win rate 25%, volume 20%, efficiency 15%), then scaled by ×100 to a 0–10,000 range. - Ties in ranks are resolved by the database’s implicit peer order. - Join rankings to trends and territory by owner_id (cast trend/territory owner_id to VARCHAR); unmatched trend/territory values remain NULL. - Derivations: - revenue_trend_percentage: if prior_6m_avg_revenue > 0 and recent_6m_avg_revenue is not NULL, compute 100 × (recent - prior) / prior; else NULL. - win_rate_trend_points: if prior_6m_avg_win_rate > 0 and recent_6m_avg_win_rate is not NULL, compute recent - prior; else NULL. - performance_tier: >=80 Top Performer; >=60 High Performer; >=40 Core Performer; >=20 Developing Performer; else Needs Improvement. - performance_trend: >=20 Strong Growth; >=5 Steady Growth; >=-5 Stable; >=-20 Declining; else Significant Decline (NULLs map to the else). - sales_specialization: Enterprise Specialist if enterprise_revenue strictly exceeds (large + medium + small); Large Deal Specialist if large_revenue strictly exceeds (enterprise + medium + small); else if segments_covered >= 3 then Generalist; otherwise Focused Seller. - development_focus (first-match order): low win rate + long cycle → Focus on Qualification and Process; low win rate → Improve Win Rate; very long cycle → Accelerate Sales Cycle; few wins → Increase Activity Volume; declining revenue trend → Address Performance Decline; else Maintain Current Performance. - activity_level (first-match): Highly Active (recent_active_months >= 3 and total_deals >= 10); Active (recent_active_months >= 2 and total_deals >= 5); Moderately Active (recent_active_months >= 1); else Low Activity. - pipeline_health_status: compare current_pipeline_value to total_won_revenue thresholds: >=2× Strong Pipeline; >=1× Healthy Pipeline; >=0.5× Adequate Pipeline; else Weak Pipeline. - Output rows are ordered by overall_performance_score descending.'

business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_hubspot__owner_performance_metrics and retain only owners where total_deals > 0. - Build monthly deal performance per owner from intermediate.int_hubspot__deal_performance_metrics: - Group by owner_id and the year/month of created_date; exclude rows where created_date is NULL. - monthly_deals_created: count distinct deal_id per month. - monthly_deals_won: count distinct deal_id where deal_status = ''Won''. - monthly_revenue: sum deal_amount where deal_status = ''Won'' (0 otherwise). - monthly_pipeline_added: sum deal_amount where deal_status = ''Open'' (0 otherwise). - monthly_win_rate: if decided deals (Won or Lost) exist, compute 100 × (won / decided); otherwise 0. - monthly_avg_cycle_time: average deal_cycle_time_days for won deals; NULL if none. - Aggregate per-owner trends over monthly data: - Use month_index = performance_year*12 + performance_month and current_month_index from current_date. - recent_6m_avg_revenue: average monthly_revenue where month_index >= current_month_index - 6 (inclusive). - prior_6m_avg_revenue: average monthly_revenue where month_index between current_month_index - 12 and current_month_index - 7 (inclusive). - recent_6m_avg_win_rate / prior_6m_avg_win_rate: analogous averages over monthly_win_rate (percent values). - revenue_volatility: standard deviation of monthly_revenue; activity_consistency: standard deviation of monthly_deals_created. - recent_active_months: count of monthly rows in the last 3 calendar months (relative to current_date), inclusive. - Territory and segment analysis per owner from all deals: - primary_deal_segment: most frequent deal_size_category; ties break by ascending category label. - segments_covered: count distinct deal_size_category. - enterprise/large/medium/small_revenue: sum won deal_amount within each named deal_size_category. - enterprise_win_rate / large_deal_win_rate: if decided deals in the segment exist, compute 100 × (won / decided); otherwise 0. - Rankings and percentiles from owner metrics: - revenue_rank: best-to-worst by total_won_revenue; win_rate_rank: best-to-worst by win_rate_percentage; volume_rank: best-to-worst by won_deals. - efficiency_rank: best-to-worst by avg_won_cycle_time, treating NULL as 999. - revenue_percentile / win_rate_percentile / volume_percentile: percentile position (0–100) across all reps using ascending order of each metric; peers share the same percentile. - efficiency_percentile: percentile position (0–100) using descending order of avg_won_cycle_time, treating NULL as 999 (longer cycles → higher percentile). - overall_performance_score: weighted sum of these percentiles (revenue 40%, win rate 25%, volume 20%, efficiency 15%), then scaled by ×100 to a 0–10,000 range. - Ties in ranks are resolved by the database’s implicit peer order. - Join rankings to trends and territory by owner_id (cast trend/territory owner_id to VARCHAR); unmatched trend/territory values remain NULL. - Derivations: - revenue_trend_percentage: if prior_6m_avg_revenue > 0 and recent_6m_avg_revenue is not NULL, compute 100 × (recent - prior) / prior; else NULL. - win_rate_trend_points: if prior_6m_avg_win_rate > 0 and recent_6m_avg_win_rate is not NULL, compute recent - prior; else NULL. - performance_tier: >=80 Top Performer; >=60 High Performer; >=40 Core Performer; >=20 Developing Performer; else Needs Improvement. - performance_trend: >=20 Strong Growth; >=5 Steady Growth; >=-5 Stable; >=-20 Declining; else Significant Decline (NULLs map to the else). - sales_specialization: Enterprise Specialist if enterprise_revenue strictly exceeds (large + medium + small); Large Deal Specialist if large_revenue strictly exceeds (enterprise + medium + small); else if segments_covered >= 3 then Generalist; otherwise Focused Seller. - development_focus (first-match order): low win rate + long cycle → Focus on Qualification and Process; low win rate → Improve Win Rate; very long cycle → Accelerate Sales Cycle; few wins → Increase Activity Volume; declining revenue trend → Address Performance Decline; else Maintain Current Performance. - activity_level (first-match): Highly Active (recent_active_months >= 3 and total_deals >= 10); Active (recent_active_months >= 2 and total_deals >= 5); Moderately Active (recent_active_months >= 1); else Low Activity. - pipeline_health_status: compare current_pipeline_value to total_won_revenue thresholds: >=2× Strong Pipeline; >=1× Healthy Pipeline; >=0.5× Adequate Pipeline; else Weak Pipeline. - Output rows are ordered by overall_performance_score descending.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: hubspot__customer_support_analytics
      schema: service
      description: Customer support analytics with SLA compliance, urgency scoring, and risk/service classifications; timestamps are set at execution time.
      grain: Rows per ticket_id; duplicates may occur due to left joins to contact/company mappings (no de-duplication).
      source_models:
      - raw.ticket_data
      - raw.ticket_contact_data
      - staging.stg_hubspot__contact
      - raw.ticket_company_data
      - raw.company_data
      - raw.owner_data
      business_logic: '- Start from raw.ticket_data t and keep tickets where t.is_deleted != ''true''. - Set created_date = current_timestamp (execution time); set closed_date = current_timestamp only if t.property_closed_date is not null and not empty, else NULL. - Derive resolution_time_hours: 24 if t.property_closed_date is not null, else 8. - Derive ticket_status: ''Closed'' if t.property_closed_date is not null; else if t.property_hs_pipeline_stage LIKE ''%waiting%'' then ''Waiting for Customer''; else if LIKE ''%progress%'' then ''In Progress''; else ''Open''. - Derive priority_level from t.property_hs_ticket_priority: 1→High, 2→Medium, 3→Low, others→Medium. - Derive sla_target_hours by priority_level: High→4, Medium→24, Low→48, default→24. - Enrich using left joins: - Join raw.ticket_contact_data tc on cast(regexp_extract(t.id, ''ID(\d+)'', 1) as bigint) = tc.ticket_id; then staging.stg_hubspot__contact c on cast(tc.contact_id as varchar) = c.contact_id. - Join raw.ticket_company_data tco on cast(regexp_extract(t.id, ''ID(\d+)'', 1) as bigint) = tco.ticket_id; then raw.company_data comp on tco.company_id = comp.id. - Join raw.owner_data o on t.property_hubspot_owner_id = o.owner_id. - Left joins may introduce duplicate rows per ticket_id; no de-duplication is applied. - Derive SLA performance: - sla_status: ''Met SLA'' if resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours; ''Near Miss'' if <= 1.5 × sla_target_hours; else ''SLA Breach''. - sla_breach_hours: 0 if resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours; else resolution_time_hours − sla_target_hours. - Derive urgency_score as integer sum of three components: - Priority weight: High 40, Medium 20, else 10. - Revenue weight: ≥1,000,000 → 30; ≥100,000 → 20; >0 → 10; else 5. - Resolution-time weight: ≥72 → 30; ≥24 → 20; ≥4 → 10; else 0. - Derive resolution_efficiency: - If ticket_status=''Closed'' and resolution_time_hours <= 0.5 × sla_target_hours → ''Fast Resolution''. - Else if ''Closed'' and resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours → ''Standard Resolution''. - Else if ''Closed'' → ''Slow Resolution''. - Else → ''Unresolved''. - Final derivations: - customer_segment from company_annual_revenue: ≥1,000,000 → ''Enterprise Customer''; ≥100,000 → ''Mid-Market Customer''; >0 → ''SMB Customer''; else ''Unknown Size''. - escalation_recommendation from urgency_score: ≥80 → ''Critical - Immediate Escalation''; ≥60 → ''High - Manager Review''; ≥40 → ''Medium - Monitor Closely''; else ''Low - Standard Process''. - service_quality_rating: ''Excellent Service'' if resolution_efficiency=''Fast Resolution'' and sla_status=''Met SLA''; ''Good Service'' if resolution_efficiency∈{''Fast Resolution'',''Standard Resolution''} and sla_status=''Met SLA''; ''Adequate Service'' if sla_status=''Near Miss''; else ''Poor Service''. - days_open: if ticket_status!=''Closed'' then days between created_date and current_date; else NULL. - risk_level (only for non-closed): if urgency_score≥70 and days_open≥3 → ''High Risk''; else if urgency_score≥50 and days_open≥7 → ''Medium Risk''; else if days_open≥14 → ''Low Risk''; else ''No Risk''; closed tickets return ''No Risk''. - Output columns exactly as selected; results are ordered by urgency_score desc, then created_date desc.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: HubSpot ticket identifier from raw.ticket_data.id; may repeat due to left joins; non-null.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: ticket_subject
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Ticket subject from raw.ticket_data.property_subject; NULLs preserved.
      - name: ticket_pipeline
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pipeline name from raw.ticket_data.property_hs_pipeline; NULLs preserved.
      - name: ticket_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pipeline stage from raw.ticket_data.property_hs_pipeline_stage; NULLs preserved.
      - name: ticket_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Derived: ''Closed'' if source closed_date is not null; else ''Waiting for Customer'' if stage contains ''waiting''; ''In Progress'' if stage contains ''progress''; else ''Open''.'
      - name: priority_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Derived from property_hs_ticket_priority: 1→High, 2→Medium, 3→Low, others→Medium.'
      - name: created_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution-time timestamp set to current_timestamp; always non-null.
      - name: closed_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution-time timestamp set to current_timestamp only when source closed_date is present and not empty; else NULL.
      - name: days_open
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: For non-closed tickets, days from created_date to current_date at execution time; else NULL.
      - name: resolution_time_hours
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Fixed: 24 if source closed_date is present, else 8.'
      - name: sla_target_hours
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Target by priority: High 4, Medium 24, Low 48, default 24.'
      - name: sla_breach_hours
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 0 if resolution_time_hours ≤ sla_target_hours; otherwise the positive difference.
      - name: sla_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'SLA result: ''Met SLA'' if within target; ''Near Miss'' if within 1.5× target; else ''SLA Breach''.'
      - name: resolution_efficiency
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Closed & time ≤ 0.5× target → Fast; Closed & time ≤ target → Standard; Closed → Slow; otherwise Unresolved.
      - name: urgency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Sum of weights: priority (High 40/Medium 20/else 10) + revenue (≥1M 30/≥100k 20/>0 10/else 5) + time (≥72 30/≥24 20/≥4 10/else 0).'
      - name: risk_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'For non-closed: ≥70 urgency and ≥3 days → High; ≥50 and ≥7 days → Medium; ≥14 days → Low; else No Risk; closed return No Risk.'
      - name: service_quality_rating
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Excellent if Fast Resolution and Met SLA; Good if (Fast or Standard) and Met SLA; Adequate if Near Miss; else Poor.
      - name: escalation_recommendation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Based on urgency_score: ≥80 Critical; ≥60 High; ≥40 Medium; else Low.'
      - name: agent_first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Owner first name from raw.owner_data via owner_id; NULLs preserved.
      - name: agent_last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Owner last name from raw.owner_data via owner_id; NULLs preserved.
      - name: agent_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Owner email from raw.owner_data via owner_id; NULLs preserved.
      - name: contact_first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact first name from staging.stg_hubspot__contact via ticket_contact mapping; NULLs preserved.
      - name: contact_last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact last name from staging.stg_hubspot__contact via ticket_contact mapping; NULLs preserved.
      - name: contact_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact email from staging.stg_hubspot__contact via ticket_contact mapping; NULLs preserved.
      - name: contact_job_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Contact job title from staging.stg_hubspot__contact via ticket_contact mapping; NULLs preserved.
      - name: company_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Company name from raw.company_data via ticket_company mapping; NULLs preserved.
      - name: company_industry
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Company industry from raw.company_data via ticket_company mapping; NULLs preserved.
      - name: company_annual_revenue
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Company annual revenue from raw.company_data.property_annualrevenue; integer units; NULLs preserved.
      - name: customer_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'From company_annual_revenue: ≥1,000,000 Enterprise; ≥100,000 Mid-Market; >0 SMB; else Unknown Size.'

alternatives.expression_sql: CASE WHEN NOT t.property_closed_date IS NULL THEN 'Closed' WHEN LOWER(t.property_hs_pipeline_stage) LIKE '%waiting%' THEN 'Waiting for Customer' WHEN LOWER(t.property_hs_pipeline_stage) LIKE '%progress%' THEN 'In Progress' ELSE 'Open' END
CASE WHEN t.property_hs_ticket_priority = 1 THEN 'High' WHEN t.property_hs_ticket_priority = 3 THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Medium' END
CASE WHEN NOT t.property_closed_date IS NULL AND t.property_closed_date <> '' THEN CURRENT_TIMESTAMP END
CASE WHEN ticket_status <> 'Closed' THEN CAST(DATE_DIFF('DAY', CAST(created_date AS DATE), CURRENT_DATE) AS BIGINT) END
CASE WHEN NOT t.property_closed_date IS NULL THEN 24 ELSE 8 END
CASE WHEN priority_level = 'High' THEN 4 WHEN priority_level = 'Low' THEN 48 ELSE 24 END
CASE WHEN resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours THEN 0 ELSE resolution_time_hours - sla_target_hours END
CASE WHEN resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours THEN 'Met SLA' WHEN resolution_time_hours <= 1.5 * sla_target_hours THEN 'Near Miss' ELSE 'SLA Breach' END

CASE WHEN ticket_status = 'Closed' AND resolution_time_hours <= 0.5 * sla_target_hours THEN 'Fast Resolution' WHEN ticket_status = 'Closed' AND resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours THEN 'Standard Resolution' WHEN ticket_status = 'Closed' THEN 'Slow Resolution' ELSE 'Unresolved' END

(CASE WHEN priority_level = 'High' THEN 40 WHEN priority_level = 'Medium' THEN 20 ELSE 10 END) + (CASE WHEN revenue >= 1000000 THEN 30 WHEN revenue >= 100000 THEN 20 WHEN revenue > 0 THEN 10 ELSE 5 END) + (CASE WHEN resolution_time_hours >= 72 THEN 30 WHEN resolution_time_hours >= 24 THEN 20 WHEN resolution_time_hours >= 4 THEN 10 ELSE 0 END)

CASE WHEN ticket_status = 'Closed' THEN 'No Risk' WHEN urgency_score >= 70 AND days_open >= 3 THEN 'High Risk' WHEN urgency_score >= 50 AND days_open >= 7 THEN 'Medium Risk' WHEN days_open >= 14 THEN 'Low Risk' ELSE 'No Risk' END

CASE WHEN resolution_efficiency = 'Fast Resolution' AND sla_status = 'Met SLA' THEN 'Excellent Service' WHEN resolution_efficiency IN ('Fast Resolution', 'Standard Resolution') AND sla_status = 'Met SLA' THEN 'Good Service' WHEN sla_status = 'Near Miss' THEN 'Adequate Service' ELSE 'Poor Service' END

CASE WHEN urgency_score >= 80 THEN 'Critical - Immediate Escalation' WHEN urgency_score >= 60 THEN 'High - Manager Review' WHEN urgency_score >= 40 THEN 'Medium - Monitor Closely' ELSE 'Low - Standard Process' END
CASE WHEN revenue >= 1000000 THEN 'Enterprise Customer' WHEN revenue >= 100000 THEN 'Mid-Market Customer' WHEN revenue > 0 THEN 'SMB Customer' ELSE 'Unknown Size' END

-- Simplified date handling - use current timestamp as placeholder
current_timestamp as created_date,
then current_timestamp
count(case when spm.created_date >= current_date - interval '30 days' then 1 end) as tickets_last_30_days,
count(case when spm.created_date >= current_date - interval '7 days' then 1 end) as tickets_last_7_days
where spm.created_date >= current_date - interval '12 months'
then datediff('day', spm.created_date, current_date)
when spm.ticket_status != 'Closed' and spm.urgency_score >= 70 and datediff('day', spm.created_date, current_date) >= 3 then 'High Risk'
when spm.ticket_status != 'Closed' and spm.urgency_score >= 50 and datediff('day', spm.created_date, current_date) >= 7 then 'Medium Risk'
when spm.ticket_status != 'Closed' and datediff('day', spm.created_date, current_date) >= 14 then 'Low Risk'

business_logic: '- Start from raw.ticket_data t and keep tickets where t.is_deleted != ''true''. - Set created_date = current_timestamp (execution time); set closed_date = current_timestamp only if t.property_closed_date is not null and not empty, else NULL. - Derive resolution_time_hours: 24 if t.property_closed_date is not null, else 8. - Derive ticket_status: ''Closed'' if t.property_closed_date is not null; else if t.property_hs_pipeline_stage LIKE ''%waiting%'' then ''Waiting for Customer''; else if LIKE ''%progress%'' then ''In Progress''; else ''Open''. - Derive priority_level from t.property_hs_ticket_priority: 1→High, 2→Medium, 3→Low, others→Medium. - Derive sla_target_hours by priority_level: High→4, Medium→24, Low→48, default→24. - Enrich using left joins: - Join raw.ticket_contact_data tc on cast(regexp_extract(t.id, ''ID(\d+)'', 1) as bigint) = tc.ticket_id; then staging.stg_hubspot__contact c on cast(tc.contact_id as varchar) = c.contact_id. - Join raw.ticket_company_data tco on cast(regexp_extract(t.id, ''ID(\d+)'', 1) as bigint) = tco.ticket_id; then raw.company_data comp on tco.company_id = comp.id. - Join raw.owner_data o on t.property_hubspot_owner_id = o.owner_id. - Left joins may introduce duplicate rows per ticket_id; no de-duplication is applied. - Derive SLA performance: - sla_status: ''Met SLA'' if resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours; ''Near Miss'' if <= 1.5 × sla_target_hours; else ''SLA Breach''. - sla_breach_hours: 0 if resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours; else resolution_time_hours − sla_target_hours. - Derive urgency_score as integer sum of three components: - Priority weight: High 40, Medium 20, else 10. - Revenue weight: ≥1,000,000 → 30; ≥100,000 → 20; >0 → 10; else 5. - Resolution-time weight: ≥72 → 30; ≥24 → 20; ≥4 → 10; else 0. - Derive resolution_efficiency: - If ticket_status=''Closed'' and resolution_time_hours <= 0.5 × sla_target_hours → ''Fast Resolution''. - Else if ''Closed'' and resolution_time_hours <= sla_target_hours → ''Standard Resolution''. - Else if ''Closed'' → ''Slow Resolution''. - Else → ''Unresolved''. - Final derivations: - customer_segment from company_annual_revenue: ≥1,000,000 → ''Enterprise Customer''; ≥100,000 → ''Mid-Market Customer''; >0 → ''SMB Customer''; else ''Unknown Size''. - escalation_recommendation from urgency_score: ≥80 → ''Critical - Immediate Escalation''; ≥60 → ''High - Manager Review''; ≥40 → ''Medium - Monitor Closely''; else ''Low - Standard Process''. - service_quality_rating: ''Excellent Service'' if resolution_efficiency=''Fast Resolution'' and sla_status=''Met SLA''; ''Good Service'' if resolution_efficiency∈{''Fast Resolution'',''Standard Resolution''} and sla_status=''Met SLA''; ''Adequate Service'' if sla_status=''Near Miss''; else ''Poor Service''. - days_open: if ticket_status!=''Closed'' then days between created_date and current_date; else NULL. - risk_level (only for non-closed): if urgency_score≥70 and days_open≥3 → ''High Risk''; else if urgency_score≥50 and days_open≥7 → ''Medium Risk''; else if days_open≥14 → ''Low Risk''; else ''No Risk''; closed tickets return ''No Risk''. - Output columns exactly as selected; results are ordered by urgency_score desc, then created_date desc.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: hubspot__tickets
      schema: service
      description: Comprehensive HubSpot ticket facts enriched with pipeline/stage attributes, owner details, and aggregated company/contact associations
      grain: One row per ticket_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_hubspot__ticket
      - staging.stg_hubspot__ticket_pipeline
      - staging.stg_hubspot__ticket_pipeline_stage
      - staging.stg_hubspot__ticket_company
      - staging.stg_hubspot__company
      - staging.stg_hubspot__ticket_contact
      - staging.stg_hubspot__contact
      - intermediate.int_hubspot__owners_enhanced
      business_logic: '- Load all tickets; output grain is one row per ticket_id. - Left join pipeline attributes on ticket_pipeline_id. - Left join stage attributes on ticket_pipeline_stage_id, and require the stage’s pipeline_id to match the ticket’s pipeline_id. - Left join owner details on owner_id. - Company associations: - Left join ticket_company to company to bring company_name. - Per ticket_id, concatenate company_id values with "," and separately concatenate company_name values with ",". - NULL inputs become empty elements in the concatenation; duplicates are kept; no ordering is imposed; if no company rows exist, the concatenated fields are NULL. - Contact associations: - Left join ticket_contact to contact to bring email. - Per ticket_id, concatenate contact_id values with "," and separately concatenate email values with ",". - NULL inputs become empty elements in the concatenation; duplicates are kept; no ordering is imposed; if no contact rows exist, the concatenated fields are NULL. - Select all ticket fields plus joined attributes and aggregations; no additional filtering or de-duplication.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary key of the ticket; exactly one output row per ticket_id (from stg_hubspot__ticket)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: owner_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Owner identifier from stg_hubspot__ticket; used to join owner details; NULL preserved
      - name: ticket_subject
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Ticket subject/title from stg_hubspot__ticket; NULL preserved
      - name: ticket_content
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Ticket body/description from stg_hubspot__ticket; NULL preserved
      - name: ticket_category
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Ticket category from stg_hubspot__ticket; NULL preserved
      - name: ticket_priority
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Numeric priority value from stg_hubspot__ticket; NULL preserved
      - name: ticket_pipeline_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pipeline identifier from stg_hubspot__ticket; used to join pipeline metadata; NULL preserved
      - name: ticket_pipeline_stage_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stage identifier from stg_hubspot__ticket; used to join stage metadata; NULL preserved
      - name: created_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Ticket creation timestamp from stg_hubspot__ticket; timezone-naive; NULL preserved
      - name: closed_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Ticket closed timestamp from stg_hubspot__ticket; timezone-naive; NULL preserved
      - name: first_agent_reply_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: First agent reply timestamp from stg_hubspot__ticket; timezone-naive; NULL preserved
      - name: is_ticket_deleted
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Ticket deletion flag from stg_hubspot__ticket; NULL preserved
      - name: _fivetran_synced
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Last Fivetran sync timestamp from stg_hubspot__ticket; timezone-aware; NULL preserved
      - name: ticket_state
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stage state from stg_hubspot__ticket_pipeline_stage joined by stage_id and matching pipeline_id; NULL if no match
      - name: company_ids
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated company_id values per ticket; NULL inputs become empty elements; duplicates kept; order not guaranteed; NULL when no associated companies
      - name: contact_ids
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated contact_id values per ticket; NULL inputs become empty elements; duplicates kept; order not guaranteed; NULL when no associated contacts
      - name: contact_emails
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated contact emails per ticket; NULL inputs become empty elements; duplicates kept; order not guaranteed; NULL when no associated contacts
      - name: owner_active_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Active user identifier from int_hubspot__owners_enhanced joined by owner_id; NULL if no match
      - name: company_names
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated company names per ticket; NULL inputs become empty elements; duplicates kept; order not guaranteed; NULL when no associated companies
      - name: owner_email_address
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Owner email address from int_hubspot__owners_enhanced joined by owner_id; NULL if no match
      - name: pipeline_stage_label
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Stage label from stg_hubspot__ticket_pipeline_stage joined by stage_id and matching pipeline_id; NULL if no match
      - name: is_ticket_pipeline_deleted
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Pipeline deletion flag from stg_hubspot__ticket_pipeline joined by pipeline_id; NULL if no match
      - name: is_ticket_pipeline_stage_deleted
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Stage deletion flag from stg_hubspot__ticket_pipeline_stage joined by stage_id and matching pipeline_id; NULL if no match

- name: stg_hubspot__company
      description: "Cleaned company records with validated revenue data and standardized industry classifications"
      source_table: raw.company_data
      columns:
        - name: company_id
          data_type: VARCHAR
          constraints: [not_null]
        - name: company_name
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: description
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: industry
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "industry IS NULL OR industry IN ('Technology','Healthcare','Finance','Manufacturing','Retail','Education','Government','Other','Consulting','Real Estate','Hospitality')"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: address
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: address_2
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: city
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: state
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: country
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: annual_revenue
          data_type: DECIMAL(18,2)
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "annual_revenue IS NULL OR annual_revenue >= 0"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "annual_revenue IS NULL OR annual_revenue <= 9999999999999.99"
              on_failure: nullify_field
            - rule: "CASE WHEN annual_revenue IS NOT NULL AND annual_revenue > 0 THEN annual_revenue BETWEEN 1000 AND 9999999999999.99 ELSE TRUE END"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: created_date
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "created_date <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "created_date >= '2000-01-01'"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: is_company_deleted
          data_type: BOOLEAN
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "is_company_deleted IN (TRUE, FALSE)"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "is_company_deleted IS NOT NULL"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: _fivetran_synced
          data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__field_history_scd
      description: Slowly changing daily snapshots of Jira issue fields with forward-filled values
      grain: One row per issue_day_id (issue per day)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__pivot_daily_field_history (valid_starting_on, issue_id, issue_day_id, status, sprint, story_points, story_point_estimate)
      business_logic: 'Build a daily slowly changing snapshot from the pivoted field history: - Use all rows from intermediate.int_jira__pivot_daily_field_history. - For each issue_id, sort records by valid_starting_on ascending. - For each field in [status → status_id, sprint, story_points, story_point_estimate]: - Define update groups by maintaining a running count that increases by 1 on days when the field is non-NULL; on NULL days the count does not change. Each group starts on a non-NULL day and spans until (but not including) the next non-NULL day. - For every day within an update group, set the field’s value to the value from the first day of that group, carrying it forward across subsequent days. - Days before the first non-NULL remain NULL; later NULLs in the source are treated as no change and the prior value persists. - Output valid_starting_on, issue_id, issue_day_id, and the forward-filled fields, with status renamed to status_id. - No deduplication or final ordering is applied; the model assumes at most one row per (issue_id, valid_starting_on). Values are not transformed beyond forward-fill.'
      columns:
      - name: valid_starting_on
        data_type: DATE
        description: Snapshot date that orders updates and forward-fill
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier used to group and forward-fill field histories
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_day_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique key for the daily snapshot of an issue
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: status_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Forward-filled daily status (renamed from status); NULL until first non-NULL; later NULLs treated as no change
      - name: sprint
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Forward-filled daily sprint; NULL until first non-NULL; later NULLs treated as no change
      - name: story_points
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Forward-filled daily story points (string); NULL until first non-NULL; later NULLs treated as no change
      - name: story_point_estimate
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Forward-filled daily story point estimate (string); NULL until first non-NULL; later NULLs treated as no change

- name: int_jira__issue_calendar_spine
      description: Daily calendar spine of Jira issues with open-state window and derived week metrics
      grain: One row per issue_id per date_day
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue (issue_id, created_at, resolved_at)
      - intermediate.int_jira__field_history_scd (issue_id, valid_starting_on)
      business_logic: '- Build a daily date spine from 2016-01-01 through seven days after today. - For each issue, derive created_on as the calendar date of created_at. Set open_until to today if the issue is unresolved; otherwise to the calendar date of the field-history valid_starting_on. - Join issues to the date spine and include a row when date_day is on or after created_on and on or before one month after open_until. If multiple history records match, earliest_open_until_date is the minimum open_until for that issue_id and date_day. - Create issue_day_id as an MD5 hash of date_day and issue_id concatenated with no delimiter. - Derive earliest_open_until_week as the Monday start of the week containing earliest_open_until_date. - Limit the final output to date_day not later than today. - Determinism and null policy: - All timestamps are converted to calendar dates; comparisons are inclusive. - Only (issue_id, date_day) pairs that meet the window are emitted; earliest_open_until_date is non-null for all rows. - Grouping enforces one row per (issue_id, date_day); issue_day_id is unique.'

        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date in scope (2016-01-01 through today, inclusive) when the issue is within its open window

        tests:

      - name: issue_day_id

- name: int_jira__issue_comments
      description: Aggregates Jira comments per issue into a comment count and a newline-separated conversation string.
      grain: One row per issue_id with at least one comment whose author_user_id matches a user in staging.stg_jira__user
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__comment
      - staging.stg_jira__user
      business_logic: '- Read all rows from staging.stg_jira__comment; an initial sort by issue_id and created_at is applied in the source CTE but no ordering is enforced in the final aggregation. - Inner join to staging.stg_jira__user on author_user_id = user_id; comments without a matching user are excluded. - Group by issue_id and compute: - count_comments: count of non-NULL comment_id across the joined comments; duplicates are counted. - conversation: for each joined comment, create a line "<created_at as text> - <user_display_name>: <body>" and concatenate all lines using a single LF (newline) between lines; if any component needed for a line is NULL, that line is omitted; if all lines are omitted, the result is NULL; original casing and spacing are preserved; no trimming or normalization is applied. - Ordering: no explicit ordering is applied in the concatenation; the order of lines in the conversation is not guaranteed and may vary. - Only issue_id values with at least one joined comment appear in the output.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier; one row per issue_id with at least one joined comment.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: count_comments
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of joined comments per issue; counts non-NULL comment_id and excludes comments without a matching user.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: conversation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Newline-separated concatenation of lines formatted as ''<created_at as text> - <user_display_name>: <body>''; line order is not guaranteed; lines with any NULL component are omitted; casing and spacing are preserved.'

output.equality_policy: exact CAST AS VARCHAR per row; no trim/case/numeric/date normalization; both NULL ignored; at least one nonnull equal row; one-sided NULL differs

alternatives.expression_sql: LISTAGG(CAST(c.created_at AS TEXT) || ' - ' || u.user_display_name || ': ' || c.body, CHR(10)) FILTER(WHERE NOT c.created_at IS NULL AND NOT u.user_display_name IS NULL AND NOT c.body IS NULL)

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__issue_lifecycle_analysis
      description: Issue lifecycle metrics and activity-based classifications derived from non-null field history changes
      grain: One row per issue_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history
      business_logic: '- Build issue_activity_history from staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history: - Keep only records where field_value is present. - For each issue_id, sort changes by updated_at ascending and derive: - previous_change_time: the timestamp of the immediately prior change for the same issue; null for the first change. - change_sequence: the 1-based position of the change in the sorted list. - total_changes: the total number of non-null field_value changes for the issue (reference only). - If multiple changes share an identical updated_at within an issue, their tie-order is implementation-dependent (no secondary tiebreaker). - Build activity_patterns by retaining only changes with a previous_change_time and compute: - days_between_changes: elapsed time in days between change_time and previous_change_time. - hours_between_changes: elapsed time in hours between change_time and previous_change_time (intermediate only; not output). - Summarize per issue_id (issue_activity_summary): - total_field_changes: the count of retained changes (number of consecutive intervals). - avg_days_between_changes: average of days_between_changes. - max_days_between_changes: maximum of days_between_changes. - activity_variance: standard deviation of days_between_changes. - first_change_time: earliest change_time among retained changes. - last_change_time: latest change_time among retained changes. - When no retained changes exist, the summary has no row; downstream metrics remain null, with total_field_changes set to 0 in the final step. - Build issue_base_info from staging.stg_jira__issue and compute: - total_lifecycle_days: elapsed time in days from created_at to resolved_at; if unresolved, to the current timestamp at execution. - Final integration and classifications (left join summary to base on issue_id): - total_field_changes: set to 0 when summary is missing; other summary metrics remain null when missing. - activity_pattern: - If total_field_changes = 0 → "No Activity". - Otherwise by avg_days_between_changes: ≤1 → "High Activity"; ≤7 → "Regular Activity"; ≤30 → "Low Activity"; else → "Minimal Activity". - lifecycle_speed: - By total_lifecycle_days: ≤7 → "Fast"; ≤30 → "Normal"; ≤90 → "Slow"; else → "Very Slow". - risk_indicator (applied in order): - If total_lifecycle_days > 90 and total_field_changes < 5 → "Stagnant". - Else if max_days_between_changes > 30 → "Inactive Periods". - Else if total_field_changes > 50 → "Over Worked". - Else → "Normal". - Output one row per issue_id from staging.stg_jira__issue; the final result is ordered by issue_id ascending.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary grouping key from Jira; exactly one output row per issue_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: issue_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Human-readable Jira issue key (e.g., PROJ-123)
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_type_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue type identifier from Jira
      - name: priority_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Priority identifier from Jira
      - name: project_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Project identifier from Jira
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue creation timestamp from Jira
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue resolution timestamp; null if unresolved
      - name: assignee_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current assignee user identifier from Jira
      - name: reporter_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Reporter user identifier from Jira
      - name: total_lifecycle_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Fractional days from created_at to resolved_at; if unresolved, to current_timestamp at execution; no rounding
      - name: total_field_changes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of consecutive change intervals (rows with non-null previous_change_time) over non-null field_value changes; 0 when none
      - name: avg_days_between_changes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Average of days_between_changes across change intervals; unit: days; null when no intervals'
      - name: max_days_between_changes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Maximum of days_between_changes across change intervals; unit: days; null when no intervals'
      - name: activity_variance
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Standard deviation of days_between_changes across change intervals; null when no intervals
      - name: first_change_time
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest change_time among intervals (second or later change); null when no intervals
      - name: last_change_time
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Latest change_time among intervals; null when no intervals
      - name: activity_pattern
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Classification: No Activity if total_field_changes=0; else High/Regular/Low/Minimal based on avg_days_between_changes thresholds'
        tests:
        - activity_pattern IN ('No Activity', 'High Activity', 'Regular Activity', 'Low Activity', 'Minimal Activity')
      - name: lifecycle_speed
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Classification from total_lifecycle_days: Fast (≤7), Normal (≤30), Slow (≤90), else Very Slow'
        tests:
        - lifecycle_speed IN ('Fast', 'Normal', 'Slow', 'Very Slow')
      - name: risk_indicator
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk classification applied in order: Stagnant, then Inactive Periods, then Over Worked, else Normal'
        tests:
        - risk_indicator IN ('Normal', 'Stagnant', 'Inactive Periods', 'Over Worked')

CASE WHEN b.total_lifecycle_days <= 7 THEN 'Fast' WHEN b.total_lifecycle_days <= 30 THEN 'Normal' WHEN b.total_lifecycle_days <= 90 THEN 'Slow' ELSE 'Very Slow' END

- name: int_jira__issue_multiselect_history
      description: Multiselect field change history joined with lowercased field names via inner join on field_id
      grain: One row per stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history row that successfully joins to stg_jira__field on field_id (duplicates preserved)
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history
      - staging.stg_jira__field
      business_logic: '- Use staging.stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history as the base; carry forward all its columns for rows that have a matching field in staging.stg_jira__field. - Inner join to staging.stg_jira__field on equality of field_id; history rows without a match are excluded; if multiple field rows share the same field_id, output includes one row per match (no deduplication). - Add field_name by converting the matched field''s name to lowercase; NULL remains NULL; spacing and characters are otherwise unchanged. - No sorting, aggregation, or type casting is performed; column order is the original history columns followed by the derived field_name.'
      columns:
      - name: field_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Field identifier from stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history; join key to stg_jira__field.field_id
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier from stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp of the multiselect change from stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: field_value
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Multiselect option value carried through from stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history (may be NULL)

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__issue_sprint
      description: Synthetic issue-to-sprint mapping using a deterministic hash-based assignment; about one-third of issues are included.
      grain: One row per issue whose deterministic hash of issue_id has remainder 0 when divided by 3.
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__sprint
      business_logic: '- Build sprint_data from staging.stg_jira__sprint with fields (sprint_id, sprint_name, board_id, started_at, ended_at, completed_at) and assign sprint_sequence by ordering sprints ascending by started_at; ties and NULL ordering follow the database default. - Build issue_base from staging.stg_jira__issue with fields (issue_id, issue_key, created_at, resolved_at, project_id) and compute assigned_sprint_sequence by: taking a deterministic hash of issue_id, taking the remainder when divided by the number of sprints, converting to a non-negative value, then adding 1 to map to the 1-based sprint_sequence. At least one sprint is required; if there are no sprints, this model will error. - Join issues to sprints on assigned_sprint_sequence = sprint_sequence (left join). When at least one sprint exists, each included issue maps to exactly one sprint; sprint attributes reflect the matched sprint and may be NULL only if the source sprint fields are NULL. - Filter to include only issues where the deterministic hash of issue_id yields a remainder of 0 when divided by 3; issues with NULL issue_id are excluded by this filter. This selects roughly one-third of issues and is deterministic for a given issue_id and sprint set. - Output selected issue and sprint fields and set count_sprint_changes to 1 for all rows (no history modeled). Assignments depend on the set of sprints and their ordering by started_at; changes to sprint count or ordering will change assignments.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier; row included only when the hash-based 3-way filter selects it; NULL issue_id are excluded.
      - name: issue_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Human-readable issue key from the issue source.
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue creation timestamp from the issue source; may be NULL.
      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue resolution timestamp from the issue source; may be NULL.
      - name: project_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Project identifier from the issue source; may be NULL.
      - name: current_sprint_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Identifier of the assigned sprint determined by the sequence mapping; NULL only if the source sprint field is NULL.
      - name: current_sprint_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Name of the assigned sprint; NULL only if the source sprint field is NULL.
      - name: board_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Board identifier of the assigned sprint; NULL only if the source sprint field is NULL.
      - name: sprint_started_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Start timestamp of the assigned sprint (used for sprint ordering); may be NULL.
      - name: sprint_ended_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: End timestamp of the assigned sprint; may be NULL.
      - name: sprint_completed_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Completion timestamp of the assigned sprint; may be NULL.
      - name: count_sprint_changes
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Always 1 to represent a single synthetic assignment without history.

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__issue_type_parents
      description: Issues enriched with type name, revised parent linkage, and parent issue details
      grain: One row per issue_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_type
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_epic
      business_logic: '- Start with all issues from staging.stg_jira__issue (one row per issue_id; no aggregation or ordering). - Left join intermediate.int_jira__issue_epic on issue_id to bring in epic linkage. - Set revised_parent_issue_id by using parent_issue_id when present; otherwise use epic_issue_id; treat identifiers as text; set to NULL when neither exists. - Left join staging.stg_jira__issue_type on issue_type_id to add issue_type (the type name); keep issues even when no type is found. - Left self-join using revised_parent_issue_id matched to issue_id (compared as text) to add parent_issue_type, parent_issue_name, and parent_issue_key. - Set is_parent_epic to true when the joined parent issue type equals "Epic" ignoring case; otherwise false, including when no parent exists. - All other fields are direct pass-through from staging.stg_jira__issue without transformation.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique issue ID; one row per value
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Human-readable issue key
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue title; may be NULL
      - name: issue_description
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue description text; may be NULL
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue creation timestamp
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Resolution timestamp; NULL if unresolved
      - name: updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Last update timestamp
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: project_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Project identifier
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: assignee_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Assignee user ID; may be NULL
      - name: reporter_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Reporter user ID; may be NULL
      - name: creator_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Creator user ID; may be NULL
      - name: status_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Status ID; may be NULL
      - name: priority_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Priority ID; may be NULL
      - name: issue_type_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue type ID; may be NULL
      - name: resolution_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Resolution ID; may be NULL
      - name: parent_issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Original parent issue ID from the source; may be NULL; replaced by revised_parent_issue_id when an epic link provides a parent
      - name: due_date
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Due date string; may be NULL
      - name: environment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Environment value; may be NULL
      - name: status_changed_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp of the last status change; may be NULL
      - name: original_estimate_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Original time estimate in seconds; may be NULL
        tests:
        - original_estimate_seconds IS NULL OR original_estimate_seconds >= 0
      - name: remaining_estimate_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Remaining time estimate in seconds; may be NULL
        tests:
        - remaining_estimate_seconds IS NULL OR remaining_estimate_seconds >= 0
      - name: time_spent_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Time spent in seconds; may be NULL
        tests:
        - time_spent_seconds IS NULL OR time_spent_seconds >= 0
      - name: work_ratio
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Work completion ratio; may be NULL
        tests:
        - work_ratio IS NULL OR work_ratio >= 0
      - name: revised_parent_issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Derived parent issue ID: use parent_issue_id when present; otherwise epic_issue_id; treated as text; NULL when neither exists'
      - name: issue_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue type name joined via issue_type_id; NULL when no match
      - name: parent_issue_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Parent issue type from the self-join; NULL when no parent
      - name: parent_issue_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Parent issue title from the self-join; NULL when no parent
      - name: parent_issue_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Parent issue key from the self-join; NULL when no parent
      - name: is_parent_epic
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True when the parent issue type equals 'Epic' ignoring case; false when absent or not Epic

      grain: One row per issue; may produce multiple rows per issue if the user table has duplicate user_id entries
      source_models:

- name: int_jira__issue_versions
      description: Aggregates the most recent affected and fix version names per issue into comma-separated strings.
      grain: One row per issue_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__version
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_multiselect_history
      business_logic: '- Filter issue multiselect history to records where field_id is ''versions'' or ''fixVersions''. - For each (issue_id, field_id), identify the most recent updated_at; if multiple rows share the most recent timestamp, keep all of them. - Convert field_value to an integer version_id and join to the version table to retrieve version_name; only matching version_ids contribute. - For each (issue_id, field_id), concatenate version_name values into a single string using ", ": - No specific ordering is applied. - Duplicates are kept. - NULL names are ignored; if none remain, the result is NULL. - Map the concatenated string to: - affects_versions when field_id = ''versions'' - fixes_versions when field_id = ''fixVersions'' - Produce a single row per issue_id by carrying forward the non-null value for each version column.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique Jira issue identifier
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: affects_versions
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated version_name list from the most recent 'versions' update; no ordering; duplicates kept; NULL names ignored; NULL if none
      - name: fixes_versions
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated version_name list from the most recent 'fixVersions' update; no ordering; duplicates kept; NULL names ignored; NULL if none

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__pivot_daily_field_history
      description: Daily pivot of latest status, sprint, story points, and story point estimate per issue on days with changes
      grain: One row per issue_id per valid_starting_on (only days with a change in any pivoted field)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_field_history
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_multiselect_history
      business_logic: '- Read single-value field changes from intermediate.int_jira__issue_field_history and multiselect field changes from intermediate.int_jira__issue_multiselect_history. - For multiselect changes, aggregate all values per (field_id, field_name, issue_id, updated_at) into one string joined by ", "; duplicates are preserved; NULL inputs are excluded; no ordering is enforced in the concatenation. - Union the aggregated multiselect changes with the single-value changes. - For each issue and field, each change timestamp starts a validity period that lasts until the next change; also derive the calendar date of the start. - Keep only relevant fields: status by field_id (case-insensitive), and sprint, story points, story point estimate by field_name (case-insensitive). - For each issue, field, and calendar date, retain the last change of that day (the highest change timestamp for that day; no tie-breaker beyond timestamp). - Replace a NULL field value with the literal "is_null"; otherwise keep the original text (including any comma-joined multiselect values). - Pivot to columns: status from field_id; sprint, story points, and story point estimate from field_name. Group by issue and date, and carry the week-start of the selected change timestamp. Use max as a pass-through since there is at most one selected value per field per day. - Output includes only dates where at least one relevant field changed for the issue. Unchanged fields on that date remain NULL; fields changed to true NULL appear as "is_null". - Compute issue_day_id as the MD5 of valid_starting_on concatenated with issue_id, with no delimiter.'
      columns:
      - name: valid_starting_on
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date on which the day's selected field updates became valid
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Jira issue identifier for the daily pivot row
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: valid_starting_at_week
        data_type: DATE
        description: Week start date based on the selected change timestamp for the day
      - name: status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest status recorded that day; 'is_null' if the latest status was NULL; otherwise NULL when status did not change that day
      - name: sprint
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest sprint value(s) recorded that day as a comma-separated list; 'is_null' if the latest sprint was NULL; otherwise NULL when sprint did not change that day
      - name: story_points
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest 'story points' recorded that day; 'is_null' if the latest value was NULL; otherwise NULL when it did not change that day
      - name: story_point_estimate
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest 'story point estimate' recorded that day; 'is_null' if the latest value was NULL; otherwise NULL when it did not change that day
      - name: issue_day_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: MD5 hash of valid_starting_on and issue_id concatenated with no delimiter
        tests:
        - not_null
