alternatives.expression_sql: CASE WHEN position_age_days < 90 THEN 'New Position (<3 months)' WHEN position_age_days < 365 THEN 'Recent Position (3-12 months)' WHEN position_age_days < 730 THEN 'Established Position (1-2 years)' WHEN position_age_days < 1825 THEN 'Mature Position (2-5 years)' ELSE 'Legacy Position (5+ years)' END
CASE WHEN current_workers_assigned > 0 THEN 'Occupied' WHEN total_workers_ever_assigned > 0 THEN 'Vacant (Previously Occupied)' ELSE 'Vacant (Never Occupied)' END
CAST(CASE WHEN total_workers_ever_assigned = 0 THEN 0 ELSE ROUND(departures_last_year * 100.0 / total_workers_ever_assigned, 2) END AS DOUBLE)

CASE WHEN REGEXP_EXTRACT(compensation_grade_id, '([0-9]+)', 1) = '' THEN 'Ungraded' WHEN TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(compensation_grade_id, '([0-9]+)', 1) AS INT) <= 5 THEN 'Entry Level' WHEN TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(compensation_grade_id, '([0-9]+)', 1) AS INT) <= 10 THEN 'Mid Level' WHEN TRY_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(compensation_grade_id, '([0-9]+)', 1) AS INT) <= 15 THEN 'Senior Level' ELSE 'Executive Level' END
CAST((CASE WHEN is_work_shift_required THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN is_union_eligible THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN default_weekly_hours > 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS INT)
CAST(CASE management_level WHEN 'Director' THEN 4 WHEN 'Senior Manager' THEN 3 WHEN 'Manager' THEN 2 WHEN 'Individual Contributor' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS INT)

CAST(ROUND((CASE WHEN current_workers_assigned > 0 THEN 25 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN avg_tenure_days >= 730 THEN 25 WHEN avg_tenure_days >= 365 THEN 20 WHEN avg_tenure_days >= 180 THEN 15 ELSE 10 END + LEAST(30, avg_employee_performance_score * 0.3) + LEAST(20, department_health_score * 0.2)), 2) AS DOUBLE)

CASE WHEN current_workers_assigned = 0 THEN 'Vacant Position' WHEN avg_employee_performance_score >= 80 AND avg_tenure_days >= 730 THEN 'High-Performance Stable Position' WHEN avg_employee_performance_score >= 70 THEN 'High-Performance Position' WHEN avg_tenure_days >= 730 THEN 'Stable Position' WHEN departures_last_year > 1 THEN 'High-Turnover Position' ELSE 'Standard Position' END

CASE WHEN current_workers_assigned = 0 AND position_age_days > 180 THEN 'Review Position Necessity' WHEN high_risk_employees_count > 0 THEN 'Focus on Retention' WHEN avg_employee_performance_score < 50 THEN 'Performance Improvement Needed' WHEN department_health_score < 50 THEN 'Department Support Needed' WHEN avg_employee_performance_score >= 80 THEN 'Maintain Excellence' ELSE 'Standard Management' END

CASE WHEN current_workers_assigned = 0 THEN 'No Current Cost' WHEN default_weekly_hours > 40 AND avg_employee_performance_score < 60 THEN 'High Cost - Low Performance' WHEN default_weekly_hours > 40 AND avg_employee_performance_score >= 80 THEN 'High Cost - High Performance' WHEN default_weekly_hours <= 40 AND avg_employee_performance_score >= 80 THEN 'Optimal Cost-Performance' ELSE 'Standard Cost-Performance' END

CASE WHEN current_workers_assigned = 0 AND position_age_days > 365 THEN 'Consider Position Elimination' WHEN similar_positions_in_department > 5 THEN 'Consider Position Consolidation' WHEN flight_risk_employees_count > 0 THEN 'Develop Succession Plan' WHEN avg_employee_performance_score >= 90 THEN 'Consider Position Expansion' ELSE 'Maintain Current Structure' END

CASE WHEN business_title IS NULL OR TRIM(business_title) = '' THEN 'ERROR: Missing title' WHEN default_weekly_hours <= 0 THEN 'ERROR: Invalid weekly hours' WHEN position_age_days < 0 THEN 'ERROR: Future position date' WHEN default_weekly_hours > 80 OR current_workers_assigned > 3 THEN 'WARNING: Position anomaly' ELSE 'VALID' END

business_logic: '- Base: Start from positions. Compute position_age_days as the days from effective_start to today. Bucket position_age_category by age: <90 days "New Position (<3 months)"; <365 days "Recent Position (3-12 months)"; <2 years "Established Position (1-2 years)"; <5 years "Mature Position (2-5 years)"; otherwise "Legacy Position (5+ years)". - Utilization history: Join worker-position assignments by position and source. Count distinct workers ever assigned (total), with open end date (current), and with closed end date (former). Set position_occupancy_status to "Occupied" if current>0; else "Vacant (Previously Occupied)" if total>0; else "Vacant (Never Occupied)". Average tenure days uses assignment start-to-end when ended, or start-to-today when still open. Take the most recent assignment start as last_assignment_date and most recent end as last_departure_date. New assignments last year count distinct workers with assignment start within the past 12 months; departures last year count distinct workers with assignment end within the past 12 months. - Organizational context: Link positions to organizations and organization metrics. Also link to job profile. similar_positions_in_department is the count of positions sharing the same organization_id and job_profile_id across the dataset. - Compensation and job profile: Derive compensation_tier from the first number found in compensation_grade_id: missing or not numeric → "Ungraded"; ≤5 → "Entry Level"; ≤10 → "Mid Level"; ≤15 → "Senior Level"; >15 → "Executive Level". challenging_work_conditions_score is the sum of three indicators (shift required, union eligible, weekly hours>40), range 0–3. Map management_level to a numeric scale: Director 4, Senior Manager 3, Manager 2, Individual Contributor 1, otherwise 0. - Current employee metrics: From employee overview by position and source. Averages (overall performance, career development, retention stability) are computed only for currently employed workers. Risk counts (High/Medium/Low Risk) are distinct worker counts by risk level without restricting to current employment. Value segments (High Value - High Retention, High Value - Flight Risk) are distinct worker counts by segment. New and veteran counts include only currently employed workers with maturity containing "New Hire" or "Veteran". Average age and ethnic diversity use only currently employed workers; military_veterans_count counts currently employed workers with military service. - Final projection and defaults: If any numeric metric is missing, default to 0; booleans default to false; text dimensions default to "Unknown"; compensation grade/tier default to "Ungraded". last_assignment_date falls back to position_created_date when no assignments; last_departure_date remains null when none. - Rounding: avg_tenure_years_in_position is average tenure days divided by 365, rounded to two decimals. Average employee scores are rounded to two decimals. Average employee age is rounded to one decimal. position_turnover_rate and position_efficiency_score are rounded to two decimals. - Derived metrics: position_turnover_rate is 0 if total ever assigned is 0; otherwise departures in the last year divided by total ever assigned, expressed as a percentage. position_efficiency_score (0–100) is the sum of: 25 if occupied; a tenure bucket (25 if tenure≥2 years, 20 if ≥1 year, 15 if ≥180 days, else 10); up to 30 points from employee performance (performance score × 0.3, capped at 30); up to 20 points from department health (health score × 0.2, capped at 20); then rounded. - Categorization rules (first-match wins): position_performance_category: Vacant Position; High-Performance Stable Position (performance≥80 and tenure≥2 years); High-Performance Position (performance≥70); Stable Position (tenure≥2 years); High-Turnover Position (departures_last_year>1); else Standard Position. management_priority: Review Position Necessity (vacant and age>180 days); Focus on Retention (any high risk employees); Performance Improvement Needed (performance<50); Department Support Needed (department health<50); Maintain Excellence (performance≥80); else Standard Management. cost_performance_analysis: No Current Cost (vacant); High Cost - Low Performance (weekly hours>40 and performance<60); High Cost - High Performance (weekly hours>40 and performance≥80); Optimal Cost-Performance (weekly hours≤40 and performance≥80); else Standard Cost-Performance. strategic_recommendation: Consider Position Elimination (vacant and age>365 days); Consider Position Consolidation (similar positions>5); Develop Succession Plan (any flight risk employees); Consider Position Expansion (performance≥90); else Maintain Current Structure. - Data quality: Mark as ERROR when title is missing/blank, weekly hours≤0, or position_age_days<0; mark as WARNING when weekly hours>80 or current assignments>3; otherwise VALID. - Output ordering: Sort rows by current_workers_assigned descending, then average employee performance descending, then position_age_days descending. - Analysis timestamp: Set to the current timestamp at query execution (time zone aware).'

blocks.original_text:
- name: workday__workforce_analytics
      description: Enterprise workforce KPI snapshot from employee overview with distinct counts, filtered averages and sums, and 2-decimal rounded percentages; uses the current date and timestamp at execution
      grain: One row per analysis_date (current_date) for the entire organization
      source_models:
      - mart.workday__employee_overview
      business_logic: 'Build three metric sets from mart.workday__employee_overview and cross join them to produce a single enterprise snapshot: - workforce_base_metrics: - Set source_relation to ''workday'' and analysis_date to the execution date. - Employee counts use distinct worker_id; position count uses distinct position_id. - Active vs former employees are split by the employment status flag. - Employee type counts (Regular, Contingent, Intern) are limited to active employees. - Weekly hours: - Average weekly hours are computed over active employees, excluding NULL values. - Total weekly hours are the sum over active employees, excluding NULL values. - Part-time counts include active employees with weekly hours below 40; full-time counts include active employees with weekly hours at or above 40; rows with NULL hours do not meet either predicate. - Diversity: - Ethnic diversity counts the distinct ethnicity code values among active employees; NULL codes are ignored. - Military veterans count distinct active workers with the military service flag true. - Age and generation groups among active employees: - Average age excludes NULL values. - Generation bands: 18–25 (Gen Z), 26–41 (Millennials), 42–57 (Gen X), and 58+ (Boomers). - retention_turnover_analysis: - Retention rates at 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, and 3 years are the mean of the corresponding retained flags among active employees, expressed as percentages and rounded to two decimals; if there are no active rows or all flags are NULL, the rate is NULL. - Churn risk distribution counts (High Risk, Medium Risk, Low Risk, Stable) use distinct worker_id across all rows without an employment filter. - Departure counts use distinct worker_id by departure_category (Early Termination, Short-term Departure, Mid-term Departure, Long-term Departure). - Annual turnover rate is the percentage of distinct workers who are no longer employed and departed in the past 12 months divided by distinct workers hired on or before one year ago, rounded to two decimals; if the denominator is zero, the value is NULL. - Tenure: - Average tenure for active employees converts average days as worker to years and rounds to two decimals; excludes NULL days. - Average tenure for departed employees applies the same conversion and rounding; excludes NULL days. - career_performance_metrics (filtered to active employees): - Average career development score is rounded to two decimals; NULL scores are excluded. - High achievers have at least two total promotions; fast track employees have one or more fast promotions. - Management levels: directors and above (level ≥ 4), senior managers (level = 3), managers (level = 2), individual contributors (level = 1). - Career phases use exact matches: Early Career, Mid Career, Senior Career. - Employee value segments use exact matches: High Value - High Retention, High Value - Flight Risk, Stable - Development Needed, Development Required. - Final computations: - Percentages divide the numerator by the stated denominator, multiply by 100, and round to two decimals; if the denominator is zero, the result is NULL. Specifically: - Position utilization = active employees over total positions. - Regular employee share = regular employees over active employees. - Full-time share = full-time employees over active employees. - Veteran share = military veterans over active employees. - High-risk share = high-risk employees over active employees. - High achiever share = high achievers over active employees. - Management share = (directors and above + senior managers + managers) over active employees. - Workforce health score (0–100) is the rounded sum of: - Retention component: 25 if the 1-year retention rate is at least 80; otherwise the rate is scaled by 0.3125. - Turnover component: 25 if the annual turnover rate is at most 15; otherwise subtract (annual turnover rate minus 15) × 1.67 from 25, floored at 0. - Career development component: 25 if the average career development score is at least 70; otherwise the score is scaled by 0.357. - Plus a fixed baseline of 25. - If any component is NULL, the overall score is NULL. - Workforce status flag precedence: 1) If there are no active employees, set to "ERROR: No active employees". 2) Else if annual turnover exceeds 50, set to "WARNING: High turnover rate". 3) Else if average career development score is below 30, set to "WARNING: Low career development". 4) Else set to "HEALTHY". - Analysis timestamp is captured at execution.'
      columns:
      - name: source_relation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Constant string 'workday' identifying the source system for this snapshot
      - name: analysis_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Date of the snapshot set to the execution day

references.name: mart.workday__employee_overview
references.line_text: business_logic: 'Build three metric sets from mart.workday__employee_overview and cross join them to produce a single enterprise snapshot: - workforce_base_metrics: - Set source_relation to ''workday'' and analysis_date to the execution date. - Employee counts use distinct worker_id; position count uses distinct position_id. - Active vs former employees are split by the employment status flag. - Employee type counts (Regular, Contingent, Intern) are limited to active employees. - Weekly hours: - Average weekly hours are computed over active employees, excluding NULL values. - Total weekly hours are the sum over active employees, excluding NULL values. - Part-time counts include active employees with weekly hours below 40; full-time counts include active employees with weekly hours at or above 40; rows with NULL hours do not meet either predicate. - Diversity: - Ethnic diversity counts the distinct ethnicity code values among active employees; NULL codes are ignored. - Military veterans count distinct active workers with the military service flag true. - Age and generation groups among active employees: - Average age excludes NULL values. - Generation bands: 18–25 (Gen Z), 26–41 (Millennials), 42–57 (Gen X), and 58+ (Boomers). - retention_turnover_analysis: - Retention rates at 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, and 3 years are the mean of the corresponding retained flags among active employees, expressed as percentages and rounded to two decimals; if there are no active rows or all flags are NULL, the rate is NULL. - Churn risk distribution counts (High Risk, Medium Risk, Low Risk, Stable) use distinct worker_id across all rows without an employment filter. - Departure counts use distinct worker_id by departure_category (Early Termination, Short-term Departure, Mid-term Departure, Long-term Departure). - Annual turnover rate is the percentage of distinct workers who are no longer employed and departed in the past 12 months divided by distinct workers hired on or before one year ago, rounded to two decimals; if the denominator is zero, the value is NULL. - Tenure: - Average tenure for active employees converts average days as worker to years and rounds to two decimals; excludes NULL days. - Average tenure for departed employees applies the same conversion and rounding; excludes NULL days. - career_performance_metrics (filtered to active employees): - Average career development score is rounded to two decimals; NULL scores are excluded. - High achievers have at least two total promotions; fast track employees have one or more fast promotions. - Management levels: directors and above (level ≥ 4), senior managers (level = 3), managers (level = 2), individual contributors (level = 1). - Career phases use exact matches: Early Career, Mid Career, Senior Career. - Employee value segments use exact matches: High Value - High Retention, High Value - Flight Risk, Stable - Development Needed, Development Required. - Final computations: - Percentages divide the numerator by the stated denominator, multiply by 100, and round to two decimals; if the denominator is zero, the result is NULL. Specifically: - Position utilization = active employees over total positions. - Regular employee share = regular employees over active employees. - Full-time share = full-time employees over active employees. - Veteran share = military veterans over active employees. - High-risk share = high-risk employees over active employees. - High achiever share = high achievers over active employees. - Management share = (directors and above + senior managers + managers) over active employees. - Workforce health score (0–100) is the rounded sum of: - Retention component: 25 if the 1-year retention rate is at least 80; otherwise the rate is scaled by 0.3125. - Turnover component: 25 if the annual turnover rate is at most 15; otherwise subtract (annual turnover rate minus 15) × 1.67 from 25, floored at 0. - Career development component: 25 if the average career development score is at least 70; otherwise the score is scaled by 0.357. - Plus a fixed baseline of 25. - If any component is NULL, the overall score is NULL. - Workforce status flag precedence: 1) If there are no active employees, set to "ERROR: No active employees". 2) Else if annual turnover exceeds 50, set to "WARNING: High turnover rate". 3) Else if average career development score is below 30, set to "WARNING: Low career development". 4) Else set to "HEALTHY". - Analysis timestamp is captured at execution.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_greenhouse__application_info
      description: Integrated application snapshot with joins to candidate, job, activity, source, stage, and EEOC datasets
      grain: One row per application_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_greenhouse__application_users
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application
      - intermediate.int_greenhouse__candidate_users
      - intermediate.int_greenhouse__candidate_tags
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__source
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__activity
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__job_application
      - intermediate.int_greenhouse__job_info
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__eeoc
      business_logic: '- Start with intermediate.int_greenhouse__application_users (application) selecting all columns. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__application (staging_application) on application_id to add applied_at, current_stage_id, last_activity_at, prospect, and source_id from staging; because these names already exist in application.*, DuckDB emits the staging versions as applied_at_1, current_stage_id_2, last_activity_at_3, prospect_4, source_id_5; these staging-sourced fields are NULL if the staging row is missing. - Left join intermediate.int_greenhouse__candidate_users (candidate) on candidate_id to add current_title, current_company, first_contact_date, last_contact_date; also set primary_email = ''Unknown'', website = ''Unknown'', linkedin_url = ''Unknown'' for all rows; set candidate_created_at equal to staging_application.applied_at (NULL if staging_application is missing). - Left join intermediate.int_greenhouse__candidate_tags (candidate_tag) on candidate_id to bring in the pre-aggregated tag string as candidate_tags; NULL if no tag record. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage (job_stage) on staging_application.current_stage_id = job_stage.job_stage_id to add current_job_stage = job_stage.name; NULL if no stage match. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__source (source) on staging_application.source_id = source.source_id to add sourced_from = source.name and sourced_from_type = source.source_type_name; NULL if no source match. - Summarize staging.stg_greenhouse__activity by candidate_id as the total number of activity rows per candidate (count_activities); left join on candidate_id so it is NULL if the candidate has no activity rows. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__job_application (job_application) on application_id, then left join intermediate.int_greenhouse__job_info (job) on job_application.job_id = job.job_id to add job-related fields (title, status, managers, recruiters, requisition_id, sourcers, offices, departments, parent_departments); these are NULL when no matching job_application or job exists. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__eeoc (eeoc) on application_id to add candidate_gender, candidate_disability_status, candidate_race, and candidate_veteran_status; NULL if no EEOC record. - Set prospect_pool = ''Unknown'' and prospect_stage = ''Unknown'' constants for all rows. - Build application_job_key by concatenating application_id, a hyphen, and job_id rendered as text; when job_id is NULL, use the lowercase string "null" in place of job_id.'
      columns:
      - name: application_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique application identifier from application.*; one output row per application_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: candidate_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Candidate identifier from application.* used to join candidate, tags, and activity
      - name: applied_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Applied timestamp from application.*
      - name: current_stage_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Current stage ID from application.*
      - name: status

        description: Application status from application.*
      - name: last_activity_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Last activity timestamp from application.*
      - name: rejected_at

        description: Rejection timestamp from application.*
      - name: source_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Source ID from application.*
      - name: prospect
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Prospect flag from application.*
      - name: candidate_full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name from application.*
      - name: candidate_company
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Company from application.*
      - name: referrer_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Referrer name from application.*
      - name: prospect_owner_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Prospect owner name from application.*
      - name: applied_at_1

        description: Applied timestamp from staging_application; NULL if no staging match
      - name: current_stage_id_2
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Current stage ID from staging_application; NULL if no staging match
      - name: last_activity_at_3
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Last activity timestamp from staging_application; NULL if no staging match
      - name: prospect_4

        description: Prospect flag from staging_application; NULL if no staging match
      - name: source_id_5

        description: Source ID from staging_application; NULL if no staging match
      - name: current_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current title from candidate users; NULL if no candidate match
      - name: current_company
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current company from candidate users; NULL if no candidate match
      - name: first_contact_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: First contact date from candidate users; NULL if no candidate match
      - name: last_contact_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Last contact date from candidate users; NULL if no candidate match
      - name: primary_email

references.name: intermediate.int_greenhouse__application_users
references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start with intermediate.int_greenhouse__application_users (application) selecting all columns. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__application (staging_application) on application_id to add applied_at, current_stage_id, last_activity_at, prospect, and source_id from staging; because these names already exist in application.*, DuckDB emits the staging versions as applied_at_1, current_stage_id_2, last_activity_at_3, prospect_4, source_id_5; these staging-sourced fields are NULL if the staging row is missing. - Left join intermediate.int_greenhouse__candidate_users (candidate) on candidate_id to add current_title, current_company, first_contact_date, last_contact_date; also set primary_email = ''Unknown'', website = ''Unknown'', linkedin_url = ''Unknown'' for all rows; set candidate_created_at equal to staging_application.applied_at (NULL if staging_application is missing). - Left join intermediate.int_greenhouse__candidate_tags (candidate_tag) on candidate_id to bring in the pre-aggregated tag string as candidate_tags; NULL if no tag record. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage (job_stage) on staging_application.current_stage_id = job_stage.job_stage_id to add current_job_stage = job_stage.name; NULL if no stage match. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__source (source) on staging_application.source_id = source.source_id to add sourced_from = source.name and sourced_from_type = source.source_type_name; NULL if no source match. - Summarize staging.stg_greenhouse__activity by candidate_id as the total number of activity rows per candidate (count_activities); left join on candidate_id so it is NULL if the candidate has no activity rows. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__job_application (job_application) on application_id, then left join intermediate.int_greenhouse__job_info (job) on job_application.job_id = job.job_id to add job-related fields (title, status, managers, recruiters, requisition_id, sourcers, offices, departments, parent_departments); these are NULL when no matching job_application or job exists. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__eeoc (eeoc) on application_id to add candidate_gender, candidate_disability_status, candidate_race, and candidate_veteran_status; NULL if no EEOC record. - Set prospect_pool = ''Unknown'' and prospect_stage = ''Unknown'' constants for all rows. - Build application_job_key by concatenating application_id, a hyphen, and job_id rendered as text; when job_id is NULL, use the lowercase string "null" in place of job_id.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_greenhouse__application_users
      description: Application records joined to candidate details, with referrer and prospect owner set to 'Unknown'; the user email CTE is unused.
      grain: One row per application with a matching candidate_id (inner join; duplicates propagate if multiple candidate rows match).
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__candidate
      business_logic: '- Read all columns from staging.stg_greenhouse__application (CTE application). - Read staging.stg_greenhouse__candidate (CTE candidate) and use only full_name and current_company. - Inner join application to candidate on candidate_id; applications without a match are excluded. - Output all application columns unchanged; NULLs are preserved. - Add candidate_full_name from candidate.full_name and candidate_company from candidate.current_company; values are passed through as-is and may be NULL. - Set referrer_name and prospect_owner_name to the constant ''Unknown'' for all rows (non-NULL, exact casing). - The intermediate.int_greenhouse__user_emails CTE is not used in the final output. - No aggregation, filtering, or de-duplication; if multiple candidate rows share the same candidate_id, application rows are duplicated. - No ordering is applied; row order is unspecified.'
      columns:
      - name: application_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Application identifier from application; duplicates can occur if multiple candidate rows match.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: candidate_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Candidate identifier from application used for the inner join to candidate.candidate_id; may duplicate across rows.
      - name: applied_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Applied-at timestamp from application; passed through as-is; NULLs preserved.
      - name: current_stage_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Current stage ID from application; passed through as-is; NULLs preserved.
      - name: status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Application status from application; passed through as-is; NULLs preserved.
      - name: last_activity_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Last activity timestamp from application; passed through as-is; NULLs preserved.
      - name: rejected_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Rejection timestamp from application; passed through as-is; NULLs preserved.
      - name: source_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Source identifier from application; passed through as-is; NULLs preserved.
      - name: prospect
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Prospect flag from application; passed through as-is; NULLs preserved.
      - name: candidate_full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate full name from candidate.full_name after the join; may be NULL.
      - name: candidate_company
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate current company from candidate.current_company after the join; may be NULL.
      - name: referrer_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Constant value 'Unknown' for all rows; non-NULL with exact casing.
      - name: prospect_owner_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Constant value 'Unknown' for all rows; non-NULL with exact casing.

- name: int_greenhouse__candidate_tags
      description: Aggregates candidate tags into a single string, counts tag associations, and flags presence of technical or experience tags.
      grain: One row per candidate_id with at least one joined tag association
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__candidate_tag
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__candidate
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__tag
      business_logic: '- Start from candidate-tag associations and inner join to candidate on candidate_id and to tag on tag_id. - Group by candidate_id and full_name. - tags: concatenate all non-null tag names separated by ", "; duplicates are kept; original casing and spacing are preserved; ordering is unspecified; if no non-null tag names exist in the group, the result is NULL. - tag_count: total number of joined tag associations per candidate, including rows where the tag name is NULL. - has_technical_tag: TRUE if any tag name contains "technical" when compared case-insensitively; otherwise FALSE. - has_experience_tag: TRUE if any tag name contains "experience" when compared case-insensitively; otherwise FALSE. - Due to inner joins, only candidates present in all three sources with at least one matching tag are included.'
      columns:
      - name: candidate_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Candidate identifier; one output row per candidate_id present after the inner joins.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name from the candidate source paired with candidate_id; may be NULL.
      - name: tags
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Concatenated tag names separated by ', '; duplicates kept; NULL tag names skipped; ordering unspecified; NULL if no non-null tag names.
      - name: tag_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total tag associations per candidate after joins, including rows where the tag name is NULL.
      - name: has_technical_tag
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: TRUE if any tag name includes 'technical' ignoring case; otherwise FALSE; never NULL.
      - name: has_experience_tag
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: TRUE if any tag name includes 'experience' ignoring case; otherwise FALSE; never NULL.

- name: int_greenhouse__candidate_users
      description: Candidate profile with first and last application interaction timestamps
      grain: One row per candidate_id with at least one application
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__candidate
      business_logic: '- Join applications to candidates on candidate_id using an inner join, so only candidates with applications are included. - For each candidate_id, carry through full_name, current_company, and current_title from the candidate record without modification. - Summarize the candidate''s application records: - first_contact_date is the earliest applied_at across that candidate''s applications. - last_contact_date is the latest last_activity_at across that candidate''s applications. - Null handling: when determining earliest/latest, NULL values are ignored; if all values for a candidate are NULL, the summary date is NULL. - Duplicate application rows do not change earliest/latest results. - No normalization of string fields; original casing and spacing are preserved. - Timestamps are preserved as in the source; no timezone conversion.'
      columns:
      - name: candidate_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Primary candidate identifier; appears once for candidates with at least one application
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate full name from the candidate record; passed through unmodified
      - name: current_company
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current company from the candidate record; passed through unmodified; may be NULL
      - name: current_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current title from the candidate record; passed through unmodified; may be NULL
      - name: first_contact_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest applied_at among the candidate's application records; NULL if all applied_at values are NULL; no timezone conversion
      - name: last_contact_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Latest last_activity_at among the candidate's application records; NULL if all last_activity_at values are NULL; no timezone conversion

- name: int_greenhouse__hiring_team
      description: Aggregates user full names into role-based lists per job by joining hiring_team to user_emails and grouping by job_id.
      grain: One row per job_id with at least one matched user_id in intermediate.int_greenhouse__user_emails
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__hiring_team
      - intermediate.int_greenhouse__user_emails
      business_logic: '- Read staging.stg_greenhouse__hiring_team (job_id, user_id, hiring_team_role) and intermediate.int_greenhouse__user_emails (user_id, full_name). - Perform an inner join on user_id; rows without a matching user are removed. - For each joined row, derive four role-category name fields based on a case-insensitive substring check of hiring_team_role: * Recruiter: role contains "recruiter" * Hiring manager: role contains "hiring" followed later by "manager" * Coordinator: role contains "coordinator" * Sourcer: role contains "sourcer" A single row can contribute to multiple categories; if a category does not match, that row’s value for the category is NULL. - Group by job_id. For each category, concatenate all non-NULL full_name values using ", ": * Only non-NULL names are included; duplicates are kept; no ordering is enforced before concatenation. * If a job_id has no names for a category, the result for that category is NULL. - Output one row per job_id present after the inner join.'
      columns:
      - name: job_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Job identifier; exactly one row per job_id present after the inner join on user_id.
        tests:
        - unique
      - name: hiring_managers
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated user full_name values for roles containing both 'hiring' then 'manager' (case-insensitive); delimiter ', '; order unspecified; duplicates kept; NULL names excluded; NULL if none; original name formatting preserved.
      - name: sourcers
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated user full_name values for roles containing 'sourcer' (case-insensitive); delimiter ', '; order unspecified; duplicates kept; NULL names excluded; NULL if none; original name formatting preserved.
      - name: recruiters
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated user full_name values for roles containing 'recruiter' (case-insensitive); delimiter ', '; order unspecified; duplicates kept; NULL names excluded; NULL if none; original name formatting preserved.
      - name: coordinators

- name: int_greenhouse__job_offices
      description: Job-to-office aggregation producing semicolon-separated office and location names per job_id
      grain: One row per job_id with at least one matching office_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__job_office
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__office
      primary_key:
      - job_id
      business_logic: '- Read job-office links from staging.stg_greenhouse__job_office (uses job_id, office_id). - Read office attributes from staging.stg_greenhouse__office (uses office_id, office_name, location_name). - Inner join on office_id; only job_office rows with a matching office record are retained. - Group by job_id to produce one output row per job_id. - offices: concatenate office_name values with delimiter "; ". - locations: concatenate location_name values with delimiter "; ". - Determinism for both aggregations: - Delimiter: "; " inserted between consecutive non-NULL items; no leading/trailing delimiter. - Ordering: no explicit ordering specified; concatenation order is not guaranteed. - Duplicates: preserved; identical names appear multiple times if present in joined rows. - NULL policy: NULL values are excluded; if all aggregated values are NULL, the result is NULL. - Casing/whitespace: preserved as stored (no trimming or normalization). - Jobs without any joined office rows are excluded from the output.'
      columns:
      - name: job_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Job identifier; exactly one output row per job_id with at least one matched office
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: offices
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Semicolon-separated office_name values for the job_id; order unspecified; duplicates preserved; NULLs excluded; NULL when all values are NULL; casing/whitespace preserved
      - name: locations
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Semicolon-separated location_name values for the job_id; order unspecified; duplicates preserved; NULLs excluded; NULL when all values are NULL; casing/whitespace preserved

      description: User details combined with aggregated email information
      grain: One row per user_id from staging.stg_greenhouse__user
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__user
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__user_email
      business_logic: '- Begin with all users from staging.stg_greenhouse__user (one row per user_id). - From staging.stg_greenhouse__user_email, take user_id and email_address as email; retain all rows and duplicates; no filtering or ordering is applied. - For each user_id: - primary_email: pick the lexicographically smallest non-NULL email; if there are no non-NULL emails, treat as missing. - all_emails: concatenate all non-NULL emails using ", "; preserve duplicates, original casing, and spacing; no specific ordering is guaranteed; if no non-NULL emails exist, treat as missing. - email_count: count the number of email records for the user, including records where email is NULL; if there are no records, the count is zero. - Left join these email aggregates to the user base on user_id so every user is present regardless of email availability. - Final defaults: replace missing primary_email and all_emails with an empty string, and missing email_count with 0. - Pass through user attributes unchanged from staging.stg_greenhouse__user.'

        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique user identifier; one output row per user_id

        data_type: VARCHAR

blocks.original_text:
- name: greenhouse__application_history
      description: Application status-change intervals enriched with candidate/job attributes and per-interval activity counts
      grain: One row per application_id per status-change interval (valid_from→valid_until)
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application_history
      - mart.greenhouse__application_enhanced
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__activity
      business_logic: '- Build status-change intervals from staging.stg_greenhouse__application_history: - For each application_id, order records by updated_at ascending. - Set valid_from to updated_at of the record. - Set valid_until to the next updated_at for the same application_id; if none, use the current timestamp at query time. - Intervals are half-open: include valid_from, exclude valid_until. - Enrich each interval: - Inner join mart.greenhouse__application_enhanced on application_id to add candidate and job attributes. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage on new_stage_id = job_stage_id to add the stage name; if no match, the name is NULL. - Compute days_in_stage as the exact seconds between valid_until and valid_from divided by 86,400; fractional days with no rounding. - Count activities per interval: - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__activity on candidate_id only; counts include all activities for the candidate across applications. - For each interval, count activity rows where created_at (as a timestamp) is on or after valid_from and before valid_until. - Duplicates are counted; rows with NULL created_at do not count; if a candidate has no matching activities, the count is 0. - One row is produced per application_id per interval with all selected attributes; the last open interval is time-variant because valid_until uses the current timestamp.'
      columns:
      - name: application_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Application identifier; multiple intervals may exist per application_id

references.line_text: business_logic: '- Build status-change intervals from staging.stg_greenhouse__application_history: - For each application_id, order records by updated_at ascending. - Set valid_from to updated_at of the record. - Set valid_until to the next updated_at for the same application_id; if none, use the current timestamp at query time. - Intervals are half-open: include valid_from, exclude valid_until. - Enrich each interval: - Inner join mart.greenhouse__application_enhanced on application_id to add candidate and job attributes. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage on new_stage_id = job_stage_id to add the stage name; if no match, the name is NULL. - Compute days_in_stage as the exact seconds between valid_until and valid_from divided by 86,400; fractional days with no rounding. - Count activities per interval: - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__activity on candidate_id only; counts include all activities for the candidate across applications. - For each interval, count activity rows where created_at (as a timestamp) is on or after valid_from and before valid_until. - Duplicates are counted; rows with NULL created_at do not count; if a candidate has no matching activities, the count is 0. - One row is produced per application_id per interval with all selected attributes; the last open interval is time-variant because valid_until uses the current timestamp.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: greenhouse__candidate_summary
      description: Candidate-level aggregates of applications, interviews, and derived quality metrics
      grain: One row per candidate_id with total_applications > 0 or total_interviews > 0
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__candidate (candidate_id, first_name, last_name, full_name, current_company, current_title, created_at)
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application (application_id, candidate_id, status, rejected_at, applied_at)
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__scheduled_interview (scheduled_interview_id, application_id)
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__scorecard (application_id, overall_recommendation)
      business_logic: '1) Build application aggregates: left join candidates (c) to applications (a) by candidate_id, keeping rows where c.candidate_id is not null. Per candidate_id compute: total_applications as the count of application rows; hired_count as the count where status is "hired"; active_count where status is "active"; rejected_count where rejected_at is present; first_application_date as the earliest applied_at; last_application_date as the latest applied_at. Assign candidate_status as: "Hired" if hired_count > 0; else "Active" if active_count > 0; else "Persistent" if total_applications > 2; else "Standard". 2) Build interview metrics: from applications (a) where a.candidate_id is not null, left join scheduled_interviews (si) and scorecards (sc), grouped by candidate_id. Compute total_interviews as the count of distinct scheduled_interview_id (ignores nulls). Compute positive_interviews as the count of scorecards where overall_recommendation is "strong_yes" or "yes" (counts all qualifying scorecards). Compute avg_interview_score as the average of mapped recommendations: strong_yes=4, yes=3, no=2, definitely_not=1; other or missing values are excluded from the average. 3) Join interview metrics to application aggregates on candidate_id; missing totals for interviews and positive_interviews are treated as 0; avg_interview_score remains null if no mapped scorecards exist. 4) Derive metrics: personal_hire_rate = hired_count × 100 / total_applications when total_applications > 0, else 0. Interview_success_rate = positive_interviews × 100 / total_interviews when total_interviews > 0, else 0. Candidate_quality_score is set to 85 if hired_count > 0 and avg_interview_score ≥ 3.5; 70 if hired_count > 0; 60 if active_count > 0 and avg_interview_score ≥ 3.0; 50 if active_count > 0; 30 if total_applications > 2; otherwise 20. 5) Keep candidates with total_applications > 0 or total_interviews > 0. Sort by candidate_quality_score descending, then hired_count descending.'
      columns:
      - name: candidate_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique candidate key; one output row per candidate_id that meets the final filter
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: first_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Direct pass-through of the candidate’s first name; may be null
      - name: last_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Direct pass-through of the candidate’s last name; may be null
      - name: full_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Direct pass-through of the candidate’s full name; not constructed here; may be null
      - name: current_company
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Direct pass-through of the candidate’s current company; may be null
      - name: current_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Direct pass-through of the candidate’s current title; may be null
      - name: candidate_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp when the candidate record was created in the source
      - name: total_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of non-null application rows linked to the candidate; duplicates counted
      - name: hired_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of the candidate’s applications with status equal to 'hired'
      - name: active_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of the candidate’s applications with status equal to 'active'
      - name: rejected_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of the candidate’s applications where rejected_at is present, regardless of status
      - name: first_application_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest applied_at across the candidate’s applications; null if none available
      - name: last_application_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Latest applied_at across the candidate’s applications; null if none available
      - name: candidate_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Classification: Hired if hired_count>0; else Active if active_count>0; else Persistent if total_applications>2; else Standard'
      - name: total_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of distinct scheduled_interview_id across the candidate’s applications; returned as 0 when not available
      - name: positive_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of scorecards with a 'strong_yes' or 'yes' recommendation; counts all qualifying scorecards; returned as 0 when not available
      - name: avg_interview_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average mapped score from scorecards (strong_yes=4, yes=3, no=2, definitely_not=1); excludes unmapped or null values; may be null
      - name: personal_hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent as hired_count*100/total_applications when total_applications>0, otherwise 0; not rounded
      - name: interview_success_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent as positive_interviews*100/total_interviews when total_interviews>0, otherwise 0; numerator counts scorecards and denominator counts distinct interviews
      - name: candidate_quality_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Score set to 85 if hired_count>0 and avg_interview_score≥3.5; 70 if hired_count>0; 60 if active_count>0 and avg_interview_score≥3.0; 50 if active_count>0; 30 if total_applications>2; else 20

- name: greenhouse__diversity_metrics
      description: Quarterly DEI metrics aggregated from applications and EEOC data (one row per year-quarter with at least 5 applications)
      grain: One row per application_year and application_quarter where total_applications >= 5
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__eeoc
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_greenhouse__application and keep only rows with applied_at present. - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__eeoc on application_id; no de-duplication is applied, so multiple EEOC rows per application will inflate counts. - Derived fields per application: - application_year and application_quarter taken from applied_at (quarters 1–4). - is_hired = 1 when status equals ''hired'' exactly, else 0. - Dimension text filled with defaults: gender, race, veteran_status, disability_status are set to ''Unknown'' when the EEOC value is NULL. - Flags using exact string matches (case and spacing preserved; NULLs do not match): - is_female = 1 when EEOC gender_description is ''Female'' or ''Woman''. - Male counts use the gender dimension (with ''Unknown'' for NULL) equal to ''Male''. - is_non_white = 1 when EEOC race_description is present and not in {''White'',''Caucasian'',''Unknown'',''''}. - White counts use the race dimension (with ''Unknown'' for NULL) equal to ''White'' or ''Caucasian''. - is_veteran = 1 when EEOC veteran_status_description is ''Yes''. - has_disability = 1 when EEOC disability_status_description is ''Yes''. - Aggregate by application_year and application_quarter: - total_applications is the number of joined rows. - total_hires is the number of rows with is_hired = 1. - Group applications are the number of rows meeting each group condition; blocks.original_text:
- name: greenhouse__interview_enhanced
      description: Enhanced interview dataset enriched with job stage, application, and candidate/job context
      grain: One row per row in intermediate.int_greenhouse__interview_users
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_greenhouse__interview_users
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage
      - intermediate.int_greenhouse__application_info
      business_logic: '- Start from all rows in intermediate.int_greenhouse__interview_users (no filtering, no aggregation, duplicates preserved). - Left join staging.stg_greenhouse__job_stage on job_stage_id. - Left join intermediate.int_greenhouse__application_info on application_id. - Select all interview fields and enrich with: - job_stage set to the job stage name; NULL if no job_stage match. - candidate_name from application.candidate_full_name; NULL if no application match. - application_current_job_stage from application.current_job_stage; NULL if no application match. - current_application_status from application.status; NULL if no application match. - job_title and job_id from application; NULL if no application match. - interviewer_is_hiring_manager: TRUE when hiring_managers contains interviewer_name, FALSE when it does not, and NULL when either value is NULL; matching is a case-sensitive substring check with original casing and whitespace preserved. - Additional application context: hiring_managers, recruiter_name, job_offices, job_departments, job_parent_departments, candidate_gender, candidate_disability_status, candidate_race, candidate_veteran_status. - Determinism and NULL policy: - No deduplication, ordering, or aggregation; values are direct passthroughs unless noted. - Left joins produce NULLs for unmatched rows. - Strings preserve original casing and whitespace; no trimming or normalization. - Timestamps are passed through without conversion or rounding. - duration_interview_minutes is passed through without rounding; unit is minutes and may be fractional.'
      columns:
      - name: application_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Application identifier from interview source; join key to application context
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Interview record creation timestamp
      - name: end_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Scheduled interview end timestamp
      - name: scheduled_interview_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Scheduled interview instance identifier
      - name: interview_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Interview identifier
      - name: location
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview location
      - name: organizer_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Interview organizer user ID
      - name: start_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Scheduled interview start timestamp
      - name: status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview status
      - name: last_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Interview record last update timestamp
      - name: job_stage_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Job stage identifier used to join to job stage name
      - name: interview_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interview name or title
      - name: duration_interview_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Interview duration in minutes; may be fractional
      - name: scorecard_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Scorecard identifier associated with the interview
      - name: candidate_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Candidate identifier
      - name: overall_recommendation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Overall recommendation from the interview record
      - name: scorecard_submitted_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Scorecard submission timestamp
      - name: scorecard_submitted_by_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Scorecard submitter user ID
      - name: scorecard_last_updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Scorecard last update timestamp
      - name: interviewer_user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Interviewer user ID
      - name: interview_scorecard_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: String key linking interview and scorecard
      - name: interviewer_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interviewer full name
      - name: scorecard_submitter_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name of the scorecard submitter
      - name: organizer_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name of the interview organizer
      - name: interviewer_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Interviewer email
      - name: candidate_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Candidate full name from application via left join; NULL if no match
      - name: job_stage

blocks.original_text:
- name: greenhouse__recruitment_performance
      description: Job- and quarter-level recruitment performance metrics with counts, rates, interview quality, tiers, and flags
      grain: One row per (job_id, application_year, application_quarter) with at least one application
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__job
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__job_application
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__scheduled_interview
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__scorecard
      business_logic: '- Build job_applications: - Join job to job_application to application; include only applications where applied_at is populated. - Group by job_id, job_title, job_status, job_created_at, and applied_at year and quarter (quarter 1–4). - Compute: - total_applications: count of application rows. - unique_candidates: count of distinct candidate_id. - hired_count: count of applications with status "hired". - active_count: count of applications with status "active". - rejected_count: count of applications with a rejection timestamp present. - avg_process_days: average days from applied_at to rejected_at if present, otherwise to last_activity_at; exclude non-computable durations; no rounding. - Build interview_metrics: - From job_application joined to application (applied_at populated), left join scheduled_interview and scorecard. - Group by job_id and applied_at year and quarter. - Compute: - total_interviews: distinct count of scheduled_interview_id. - completed_interviews: count of scheduled interviews with status "completed" (not distinct). - total_scorecards: distinct count of scorecard_id. - avg_interview_score: average of mapped recommendations across scorecards (strong_yes=4, yes=3, no=2, definitely_not=1); exclude other values and nulls; no rounding. - Join metrics: - Left join interview_metrics to job_applications on job_id, application_year, and application_quarter. - If interview_metrics is missing, set total_interviews, completed_interviews, and total_scorecards to 0; keep avg_interview_score as NULL. - Derive rates (percentages 0–100, double precision, no rounding): - hire_rate: hired_count divided by total_applications times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - interview_rate: total_interviews divided by total_applications times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - interview_to_hire_rate: hired_count divided by total_interviews times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - interview_completion_rate: completed_interviews divided by total_interviews times 100; return 0 if the denominator is 0. - Assign performance_tier (first matching rule applies): - "Excellent" if hired_count >= 3 and hire_rate >= 20. - "Good" if hired_count >= 2 and hire_rate >= 15. - "Average" if hired_count >= 1 and hire_rate >= 10. - "Needs Improvement" if total_applications >= 10. - Else "Low Activity". - Flags: - is_fast_process: 1 if avg_process_days <= 30 else 0; NULL avg_process_days yields 0. - has_good_interview_quality: 1 if avg_interview_score >= 3.0 else 0; NULL avg_interview_score yields 0. - Final filter and ordering: - Keep only rows where total_applications >= 1. - Order rows by application_year descending, application_quarter descending, then hire_rate descending.'
      columns:
      - name: job_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Greenhouse job identifier; groups all metrics for the job within the year-quarter
      - name: job_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Job name as stored in Greenhouse at the time of extraction
      - name: job_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Job status from Greenhouse (e.g., open/closed)
      - name: job_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp the job record was created in Greenhouse
      - name: application_year
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Calendar year extracted from application.applied_at (non-null)
      - name: application_quarter
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Calendar quarter number (1–4) extracted from application.applied_at (non-null)
      - name: total_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of application rows with non-null applied_at for the job-year-quarter (>=1 due to filter)
      - name: unique_candidates
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of candidate_id among applications in the job-year-quarter
      - name: hired_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of applications with status 'hired' in the job-year-quarter
      - name: active_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of applications with status 'active' in the job-year-quarter
      - name: rejected_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of applications with a rejection timestamp present in the job-year-quarter
      - name: avg_process_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from applied_at to rejected_at if present, otherwise to last_activity_at; excludes non-computable durations; double precision; no rounding
      - name: total_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of scheduled_interview_id for the job-year-quarter; 0 if none
      - name: completed_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of scheduled interviews with status 'completed' (not distinct); 0 if none
      - name: total_scorecards
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of scorecard_id for the job-year-quarter; 0 if none
      - name: avg_interview_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average mapped score across scorecards (strong_yes=4, yes=3, no=2, definitely_not=1); NULL if no mappable scorecards; no rounding
      - name: hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: hired_count divided by total_applications times 100; returns 0 when denominator is 0; double precision; no rounding
      - name: interview_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: total_interviews divided by total_applications times 100; returns 0 when denominator is 0; double precision; no rounding
      - name: interview_to_hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: hired_count divided by total_interviews times 100; returns 0 when denominator is 0; double precision; no rounding
      - name: interview_completion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: completed_interviews divided by total_interviews times 100; returns 0 when denominator is 0; double precision; no rounding
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Categorical tier per thresholds: Excellent, Good, Average, Needs Improvement, or Low Activity'
      - name: is_fast_process
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if avg_process_days <= 30 else 0; NULL avg_process_days yields 0
      - name: has_good_interview_quality
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if avg_interview_score >= 3.0 else 0; NULL avg_interview_score yields 0

blocks.original_text:
- name: greenhouse__talent_pipeline_simplified
      description: Simplified talent pipeline and source effectiveness by source and year-quarter; rows require at least one application
      grain: One row per source_id, source_name, source_type, application_year, application_quarter with total_applications >= 1
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__application
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__source
      - staging.stg_greenhouse__scheduled_interview
      business_logic: '- Keep applications where applied_at and source_id are present. - Enrich with source_name and source_type via a left join on source_id; if no source match, name/type are NULL. - Derive application_year and application_quarter from applied_at. - Group by source_id, source_name, source_type, application_year, application_quarter. - Aggregations per group: * total_applications: number of application rows. * unique_candidates: count of distinct non-null candidate_id values. * total_hires: applications with status exactly "hired" (string match is exact and case-sensitive). * active_applications: applications with status exactly "active". * rejected_applications: applications where rejected_at is present. * applications_with_interviews: applications that have at least one scheduled interview linked by application_id; each application counted once regardless of interview count. * avg_process_days: for each application, compute days from applied_at to rejected_at if present, otherwise to last_activity_at; average these durations; applications lacking both end timestamps do not contribute. - Metrics (expressed as percentages from 0 to 100, no rounding): * hire_rate: total_hires divided by total_applications; 0 if total_applications is 0. * interview_rate: applications_with_interviews divided by total_applications; 0 if total_applications is 0. * interview_to_hire_rate: total_hires divided by applications_with_interviews; 0 if no interviewed applications. * rejection_rate: rejected_applications divided by total_applications; 0 if total_applications is 0. - Rankings per year-quarter: * hire_rate_rank: rank by hire_rate descending (ties share rank; gaps allowed). * volume_rank: rank by total_applications descending (ties share rank; gaps allowed). - performance_tier: assign in order—High Performer (hire_rate ≥ 20 and total_applications ≥ 10), Good Performer (hire_rate ≥ 10 and total_applications ≥ 5), High Volume (total_applications ≥ 10), Medium Volume (total_applications ≥ 5), else Low Volume. - efficiency_score: if total_applications > 0, hire_rate + (total_applications ÷ 10); otherwise 0; no rounding. - Exclude groups with total_applications < 1. - Order rows by application_year descending, application_quarter descending, then efficiency_score descending.'
      columns:
      - name: source_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Application source identifier; part of the grouping key; may repeat across year-quarter groups
      - name: source_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source name from the source table; NULL if no match; grouped using exact text
      - name: source_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source type name; NULL allowed; grouped using exact text
      - name: application_year
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Calendar year derived from applied_at; non-NULL
      - name: application_quarter
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Quarter number (1–4) derived from applied_at; non-NULL
      - name: total_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of applications in the group; final result includes only groups with at least one
      - name: unique_candidates
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of distinct non-null candidate_id values in the group
      - name: total_hires
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Applications whose status equals 'hired' (exact match; NULL or other statuses not counted)
      - name: active_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Applications whose status equals 'active' (exact match)
      - name: rejected_applications
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Applications with a non-null rejected_at timestamp
      - name: applications_with_interviews
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Applications with at least one scheduled interview; each application counted once regardless of interview count
      - name: avg_process_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from applied_at to rejected_at if present, otherwise to last_activity_at; applications missing both end timestamps are excluded
      - name: hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of applications hired (0–100); set to 0 when total_applications is 0; unrounded
      - name: interview_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of applications with interviews (0–100); set to 0 when total_applications is 0; unrounded
      - name: interview_to_hire_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of interviewed applications that were hired (0–100); set to 0 when no interviewed applications; unrounded
      - name: rejection_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent of applications rejected (0–100); set to 0 when total_applications is 0; unrounded
      - name: hire_rate_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank within the same year-quarter by hire_rate descending; ties share rank; gaps allowed
      - name: volume_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank within the same year-quarter by total_applications descending; ties share rank; gaps allowed
      - name: performance_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier label based on thresholds for hire_rate and total_applications: High Performer, Good Performer, High Volume, Medium Volume, or Low Volume'
      - name: efficiency_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Score equal to hire_rate plus total_applications divided by 10; 0 when total_applications is 0; unrounded

blocks.original_text:
- name: stg_greenhouse__application
      description: "Cleaned application records with status validation and temporal consistency checks"
      source_table: "raw.application"
      primary_key: ["application_id"]
      columns:
        - name: application_id
          data_type: BIGINT
          constraints: [not_null, unique]
        - name: candidate_id
          data_type: BIGINT
          constraints: [not_null]
        - name: applied_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
          constraints: [not_null]
        - name: current_stage_id
          data_type: BIGINT
        - name: status
          data_type: VARCHAR(50)
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "status = LOWER(TRIM(status))"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "status IN ('active', 'hired', 'rejected', 'withdrawn')"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: last_activity_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
        - name: rejected_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "rejected_at >= applied_at OR rejected_at IS NULL"
              on_failure: nullify_field
            - rule: "(status = 'rejected' AND rejected_at IS NOT NULL) OR (status != 'rejected')"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: source_id
          data_type: BIGINT
        - name: prospect
          data_type: BOOLEAN

      description: "Cleaned and standardized candidate profile information with basic validation and formatting rules applied"
      source_table: "raw.candidate"
      primary_key: ["candidate_id"]
      columns:
        - name: candidate_id
          data_type: BIGINT
          constraints: [not_null, unique]
        - name: first_name
          data_type: VARCHAR(100)
          constraints: [not_null]
        - name: last_name
          data_type: VARCHAR(100)
          constraints: [not_null]
        - name: full_name
          data_type: VARCHAR(201)
        - name: current_company
          data_type: VARCHAR(255)
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "current_company = TRIM(current_company)"
              on_failure: correct
            - rule: "current_company = CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(current_company)) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE current_company END"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: current_title
          data_type: VARCHAR(255)
        - name: coordinator_user_id
          data_type: BIGINT
        - name: recruiter_user_id
          data_type: BIGINT
        - name: created_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
          constraints: [not_null]
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"
              on_failure: delete_row
            - rule: "created_at >= '2000-01-01'"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: last_updated_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
        - name: last_activity_at
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
        - name: is_private
          data_type: BOOLEAN
        - name: new_candidate_id
          data_type: BIGINT
