- name: youtube__age_demographics_pivot
      description: Age-demographic view percentages per video and country, left joined with video title and published date.
      grain: One row per age_pivot row per matching video row (left join on video_id).
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_youtube__age_pivot
      - intermediate.int_youtube__video
      business_logic: '- Read age demographics from intermediate.int_youtube__age_pivot (fields: date_day, video_id, country_code, and age group columns "13-17", "18-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65-"). - Read video attributes from intermediate.int_youtube__video (fields: video_id, video_title, published_at_date). - Left join on video_id: - If multiple video rows exist for a video_id, the output contains one row per matching pair (duplicates propagate). - If no video match exists, video_title and video_published_date are NULL and the age_pivot row is retained. - Select pass-through fields and rename age group columns: - "13-17" → 13-17_view_percentage - "18-24" → 18-24_view_percentage - "25-34" → 25-34_view_percentage - "35-44" → 35-44_view_percentage - "45-54" → 45-54_view_percentage - "55-64" → 55-64_view_percentage - "65-" → 65-_view_percentage - Select video_title and published_at_date as video_published_date. - No filtering, aggregation, deduplication, normalization, rounding, or sorting is applied; values are passed through as-is and NULLs are preserved.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date from age_pivot; pass-through; NULLs preserved.
      - name: video_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Video identifier from age_pivot used for the left join to video; pass-through; NULLs preserved.
      - name: country_code
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Country code from age_pivot (e.g., ISO alpha-2); casing preserved; NULLs preserved.
      - name: 13-17_view_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: View percentage for age 13–17 from age_pivot; passed through without scaling or rounding.
      - name: 18-24_view_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: View percentage for age 18–24 from age_pivot; passed through without scaling or rounding.
      - name: 25-34_view_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: View percentage for age 25–34 from age_pivot; passed through without scaling or rounding.
      - name: 35-44_view_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: View percentage for age 35–44 from age_pivot; passed through without scaling or rounding.
      - name: 45-54_view_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: View percentage for age 45–54 from age_pivot; passed through without scaling or rounding.
      - name: 55-64_view_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: View percentage for age 55–64 from age_pivot; passed through without scaling or rounding.
      - name: 65-_view_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: View percentage for age 65+ from age_pivot; passed through without scaling or rounding.
      - name: video_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Video title from the video table for the matching video_id; NULL if no match; pass-through.
      - name: video_published_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Published date from the video table (published_at_date) for the matching video_id; NULL if no match; pass-through.

blocks.original_text:
- name: youtube__demographics_report
      description: Daily demographics summary by date, video, and country with distinct coverage counts, clipped total views percentage, and joined video attributes.
      grain: One row per (date_day, video_id, country_code); if multiple video rows exist for a video_id, the aggregated row is duplicated per matching video row.
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_youtube__channel_demographics
      - intermediate.int_youtube__video
      business_logic: '- Read all rows from intermediate.int_youtube__channel_demographics. - Aggregate by (date_day, video_id, country_code): - total_views_percentage: sum views_percentage over the group; after summing, force the value to be at least 0.0 and at most 1.0; if the sum is NULL, the final value remains NULL; no rounding is applied. - age_groups_count: count of distinct age_group values; NULLs are excluded by distinct counting. - genders_count: count of distinct gender values; NULLs are excluded by distinct counting. - records_count: count of all rows in the group; NULL attributes do not affect this count. - Left join the aggregated result to intermediate.int_youtube__video on video_id: - video_title - published_at_date mapped to video_published_date - Join semantics: - If no matching video_id exists, video_title and video_published_date are NULL. - If multiple video rows match the same video_id, the aggregated row is returned once per matching video row. - Final ordering: sort by date_day descending, then by total_views_percentage descending.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date from demographics; nullable and used as a grouping key.
      - name: video_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Video identifier from demographics; grouping key and left-join key to video metadata.
      - name: country_code
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Country code from demographics; used as a grouping key.
      - name: total_views_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Sum of views_percentage per group, then clipped to [0.0, 1.0]; remains NULL if the sum is NULL; expressed as a fraction with no rounding.
        tests:
        - total_views_percentage IS NULL OR total_views_percentage BETWEEN 0 AND 1
      - name: age_groups_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of distinct non-NULL age_group values in the group.
        tests:
        - age_groups_count >= 0
      - name: genders_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of distinct non-NULL gender values in the group.
        tests:
        - genders_count >= 0
      - name: records_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total number of demographics rows in the group, including rows with NULL attributes.
        tests:
        - records_count >= 1
      - name: video_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Title from the joined video row; NULL if no match; duplicates if multiple video rows match.
      - name: video_published_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Published date from the joined video row; NULL if no match; duplicates if multiple video rows match.

blocks.original_text:
- name: youtube__video_report
      description: Daily per-video performance fact with weighted averages and conversion KPIs
      grain: One row per video_id, channel_id, date_day
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_youtube__channel_basic
      - intermediate.int_youtube__video
      business_logic: '- Aggregate intermediate.int_youtube__channel_basic by date_day, video_id, and channel_id: - Sum views, likes, dislikes, shares, subscribers gained, subscribers lost, watch time minutes, and red watch time minutes. - Compute views-weighted averages: - avg_view_duration_seconds: weight each row’s average_view_duration_seconds by its views and divide by total views; return NULL when total views is 0 or when all contributing values are missing. - avg_view_duration_percentage: treat missing percentages as 0 before weighting; return NULL when total views is 0. - records_count equals the number of channel_basic rows in the group. - Derive KPIs: - like_rate, dislike_rate, and share_rate equal the respective totals divided by total views when total views > 0; otherwise NULL. - net_subscribers equals subscribers gained minus subscribers lost. - Left join intermediate.int_youtube__video on video_id to add video_title and video_published_date; unmatched videos yield NULLs. - Exclude groups with negative total views; keep zero and positive. - Create video_report_id as the MD5 of the string formed by converting date_day to text and appending video_id with no delimiter. - Query output is ordered by date_day descending and total_views descending; ordering does not affect table contents.'
      columns:
      - name: video_report_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: MD5 of date_day (as text) concatenated with video_id without a delimiter; stable key per video/day
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date of aggregation
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: video_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: YouTube video identifier
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: channel_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Channel identifier sourced from aggregated rows
        tests: []
      - name: video_title
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Video title from int_youtube__video; NULL if no match
        tests: []
      - name: video_published_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Publication date from int_youtube__video; NULL if no match
        tests: []
      - name: total_views
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of views across channel_basic rows for the group; non-negative due to final filter
        tests:
        - total_views >= 0
      - name: total_likes
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of likes across channel_basic rows for the group
        tests: []
      - name: total_dislikes
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of dislikes across channel_basic rows for the group
        tests: []
      - name: total_shares
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of shares across channel_basic rows for the group
        tests: []
      - name: total_subscribers_gained
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of subscribers_gained across channel_basic rows for the group
        tests: []
      - name: total_subscribers_lost
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of subscribers_lost across channel_basic rows for the group
        tests: []
      - name: total_watch_time_minutes
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,1)
        description: Sum of watch_time_minutes across channel_basic rows (precision 0.1 minute)
        tests: []
      - name: total_red_watch_time_minutes
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,1)
        description: Sum of red_watch_time_minutes across channel_basic rows (precision 0.1 minute)
        tests: []
      - name: avg_view_duration_seconds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Views-weighted average over non-missing average_view_duration_seconds; NULL when total_views is 0 or all values are missing; no rounding
        tests: []
      - name: avg_view_duration_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Views-weighted average of average_view_duration_percentage with missing values treated as 0; NULL when total_views <= 0
        tests: []
      - name: like_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Computed as total_likes divided by total_views when total_views > 0; otherwise NULL; not clamped
        tests: []
      - name: dislike_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Computed as total_dislikes divided by total_views when total_views > 0; otherwise NULL; not clamped
        tests: []
      - name: share_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Computed as total_shares divided by total_views when total_views > 0; otherwise NULL; not clamped
        tests: []
      - name: net_subscribers
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: total_subscribers_gained minus total_subscribers_lost
        tests: []
      - name: records_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of channel_basic records aggregated into the group
        tests:
        - records_count >= 1

- name: stg_youtube__channel_basic
      description: "Cleaned daily per-video channel performance metrics (views, engagement, subscribers, annotations). Percentages are normalized to [0,1]."
      source_table: raw.channel_basic_a_2
      columns:
        - name: date_day
          data_type: DATE
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "date_day IS NOT NULL AND date_day <= CURRENT_DATE AND date_day >= '2020-01-01'"
              on_failure: delete_row
        - name: channel_id
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "channel_id IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(channel_id)) = 24"
              on_failure: nullify_field
            - rule: "channel_id = TRIM(channel_id)"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: video_id
          data_type: VARCHAR
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "video_id IS NULL OR LENGTH(TRIM(video_id)) = 11"
              on_failure: nullify_field
            - rule: "video_id = TRIM(video_id)"
              on_failure: correct
        - name: channel_title
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: video_title
          data_type: VARCHAR
        - name: deleted
          data_type: BOOLEAN
        - name: _fivetran_synced
          data_type: TIMESTAMP
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "_fivetran_synced IS NULL OR _fivetran_synced <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: average_view_duration_seconds
          data_type: BIGINT
        - name: average_view_duration_percentage
          data_type: DECIMAL(5,4)
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "average_view_duration_percentage BETWEEN 0 AND 1"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: views
          data_type: BIGINT
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "views BETWEEN 0 AND 1000000000"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: likes
          data_type: BIGINT
          validation_rules:
            - rule: "likes BETWEEN 0 AND 10000000"
              on_failure: nullify_field
        - name: dislikes

          validation_rules:
            - rule: "dislikes BETWEEN 0 AND 1000000"
              on_failure: nullify_field

- name: int_zendesk__assignee_updates
      description: Assignee change intervals per ticket from assignee_id history; each row begins at an update and ends at the next update.
      grain: One row per ticket_id per assignee update event
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history
      business_logic: '- Filter to history rows where field_name equals "assignee_id" ignoring case (exact match; whitespace or extra characters do not match). - Cast and rename: ticket_id→BIGINT, value→assignee_id (BIGINT), user_id→BIGINT, updated→valid_starting_at (TIMESTAMP). - For each ticket_id, order events by the source updated value ascending; no secondary tie-breaker is applied, so identical timestamps retain input order. - Set valid_ending_at to the timestamp of the next event in this ordered sequence for the same ticket; the final event has valid_ending_at = NULL. - Emit one row per filtered event; no validation that the assignee changed, no deduplication; source NULLs are preserved; no timezone conversion.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Ticket identifier used to group and sequence updates; cast from source.
      - name: assignee_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Assignee user ID at the start of the interval; cast from source value; may be NULL; identical consecutive values are not merged.
      - name: user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: User who performed the update; cast from source; may be NULL.
      - name: valid_starting_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp the assignee update occurred; cast from source updated; used to order events and mark interval start.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: valid_ending_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp of the next assignee update for the same ticket based on ordering by the source updated value; NULL for the last event.

- name: int_zendesk__latest_ticket_form
      description: Keeps the most recently updated record per ticket_form_id based on updated_at descending; ties are unresolved and NULL ordering follows engine defaults.
      grain: One row per ticket_form_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_form_history
      business_logic: '- Read ticket_form_id, created_at, updated_at, display_name, active, and name from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_form_history. - For each ticket_form_id, order records by updated_at in descending time order. - Assign a rank starting at 1 within each ticket_form_id based on that order and keep only the rank 1 record. - If multiple records share the same updated_at for a ticket_form_id, the kept row is chosen by the engine’s default tie-breaking (not deterministic). - Placement of NULL updated_at values in the ordering follows engine defaults. - Output the fields from the kept row and include the rank as latest_form_index; no additional transformations are applied.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_form_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique form identifier; exactly one output row per value.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Creation timestamp from the kept record; NULLs are preserved.
        tests: []
      - name: updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Sort key used to select the kept record; value from that record; may be NULL and its ordering follows engine defaults.
        tests: []
      - name: display_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Display name from the kept record; casing and whitespace preserved; may be NULL.
        tests: []
      - name: active
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: Active status from the kept record; TRUE/FALSE preserved as in source; may be NULL.
        tests: []
      - name: name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Form name from the kept record; casing and whitespace preserved; may be NULL.
        tests: []
      - name: latest_form_index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank within ticket_form_id when ordered by updated_at descending; always 1 in this table; ties follow engine defaults.

        - not_null

references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket, selecting the listed columns; output grain is one row per ticket_id. - Build ticket_tags by grouping staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_tag by ticket_id and concatenating all non-null tag values with ", " as the separator: - Duplicates are preserved, original text is retained, and ordering is not guaranteed. - If a ticket has no non-null tags or no tag rows, set ticket_tags to an empty string. - Build latest_form from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_form_history: - For each ticket_form_id, choose the record with the greatest updated_at; if multiple records share the latest timestamp, selection among them is arbitrary. - Map display_name to ticket_form_name and active to ticket_form_active. - Left join ticket_tags on ticket_id and latest_form on ticket_form_id to the ticket base; retain all ticket rows. - Emit all base ticket columns plus ticket_tags, ticket_form_name, and ticket_form_active without further transformation.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zendesk__ticket_comment_stats
      description: Per-ticket comment totals by visibility and the earliest public reply timestamp from an agent/admin
      grain: One row per ticket_id with at least one comment in staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_comment
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_comment
      - staging.stg_zendesk__user
      business_logic: '- Use comments: ticket_id, created_at, user_id, is_public. - From users: user_id and role; mark a user as internal when role (case-insensitive) is agent or admin. - Left join users to comments on user_id; if the user is missing or role is NULL, treat the author as not internal. - For each ticket_id: - comment_count: count all comment rows (every row counts once; visibility and user match do not affect inclusion). - public_comment_count: count rows where is_public is true; rows with is_public NULL do not contribute. - private_comment_count: count rows where is_public is false; rows with is_public NULL do not contribute. - first_agent_public_reply_at: earliest created_at among rows where the comment is public and the author is internal; NULL if none qualify. - Only tickets with at least one comment are included; duplicate rows are counted separately; timestamps are not transformed or rounded; ties at the earliest timestamp return that timestamp.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Ticket identifier; exactly one output row per ticket with comments.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: comment_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total number of comment rows for the ticket; includes all comments regardless of visibility or author; never NULL.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: public_comment_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of comments marked public; rows with NULL visibility do not contribute; independent of author role; never NULL.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: private_comment_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of comments marked private; rows with NULL visibility do not contribute; independent of author role; never NULL.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: first_agent_public_reply_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest timestamp of a public comment authored by an internal user (agent or admin); NULL if none; missing users are treated as not internal.
        tests: []

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zendesk__ticket_historical_satisfaction
      description: History of satisfaction-prefixed ticket field changes with per-ticket validity windows derived from change timestamps.
      grain: One row per satisfaction-prefixed ticket field change
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history. - Keep only rows where the field name starts with "satisfaction" ignoring case; rows with NULL field_name are excluded. - For each row: cast ticket_id to BIGINT; pass through field_name and value; set valid_starting_at to the updated timestamp cast to TIMESTAMP. - Within each ticket_id, sort changes by updated ascending and set valid_ending_at to the start timestamp of the next change for that ticket; if none exists, valid_ending_at is NULL. - The next change may be for any satisfaction-prefixed field on the ticket and is not limited to the same field_name. - If multiple rows share the same updated timestamp within a ticket, the relative order among them is not explicitly defined; duplicates are preserved; no de-duplication. - Output one row per qualifying change record.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Ticket identifier cast to BIGINT; used to group changes when deriving validity windows.
        tests: []
      - name: field_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Field name included only when it starts with 'satisfaction' (case-insensitive); original casing and content preserved.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: value
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Field value at the change time; passed through as-is and may be NULL.
        tests: []
      - name: valid_starting_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Start timestamp of the change (from updated) cast to TIMESTAMP.
        tests: []
      - name: valid_ending_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Start timestamp of the next change within the same ticket based on updated ascending; spans any satisfaction-prefixed field; NULL when no later change; tie order for equal timestamps is undefined.
        tests: []

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zendesk__ticket_metrics
      description: Per-ticket metrics with comment counts, first agent public reply, resolution timestamp, and elapsed minutes/days.
      grain: One row per ticket_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_comment
      - staging.stg_zendesk__user
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history
      business_logic: '- Tickets: one row per ticket_id from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket with created_at, updated_at, and status. - Comment aggregates (grouped by ticket_id) from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_comment joined to staging.stg_zendesk__user on user_id: - comment_count counts all comment rows; no de-duplication. - public_comment_count counts comments flagged public; comments with is_public NULL do not contribute. - private_comment_count counts comments flagged non-public; comments with is_public NULL do not contribute. - first_agent_public_reply_at is the earliest comment.created_at where the comment is public and the author’s role is agent or admin (role comparison is case-insensitive); comments without a matching user or with NULL role do not qualify; earliest time is chosen, and absence yields NULL. - Resolution timestamp from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history: - Restrict to field_name equal to status (case-insensitive) and, per ticket_id, take the earliest updated timestamp where the status value is solved or closed (case-insensitive); ticket_id is treated as BIGINT for joining. - Final assembly: left join the comment aggregates and resolution timestamp to tickets by ticket_id. - first_response_minutes is the whole-minute difference between created_at and first_agent_public_reply_at; NULL if no qualifying reply. - resolution_minutes is the whole-minute difference between created_at and resolved_at; NULL if unresolved. - age_days is the whole-day difference between created_at and resolved_at if present, otherwise updated_at; NULL only if both are NULL. - Null handling and determinism: - If a ticket has no comment rows, all comment aggregates and any derived metrics depending on them are NULL. - Earliest timestamps are chosen deterministically; ties at identical times simply return that time. - Comparisons for role, field_name, and status values are case-insensitive. - Differences are integer units; negative values are possible if source timestamps are inconsistent. - No explicit ordering is applied in the final output.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique ticket identifier; one row per ticket.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Ticket creation timestamp from the ticket source.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Most recent ticket update timestamp from the ticket source; may be NULL.
        tests: []
      - name: status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current ticket status from the ticket source; original casing preserved.
        tests: []
      - name: comment_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total comments on the ticket; NULL if the ticket has no comment rows.
        tests: []
      - name: public_comment_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of comments marked public; NULL if the ticket has no comment rows; comments with is_public NULL are not counted.
        tests: []
      - name: private_comment_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of comments marked non-public; NULL if the ticket has no comment rows; comments with is_public NULL are not counted.
        tests: []
      - name: first_agent_public_reply_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest time a public comment was posted by a user with role agent or admin; NULL if none qualify.
        tests: []
      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest time the ticket’s status changed to solved or closed based on status history; NULL if never reached.
        tests: []
      - name: first_response_minutes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Whole minutes between ticket creation and the first qualifying agent public reply; NULL if none.
        tests: []
      - name: resolution_minutes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Whole minutes between ticket creation and resolution; NULL if unresolved.
        tests: []
      - name: age_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Whole days between ticket creation and resolution if present, otherwise latest update; NULL only if both are NULL.
        tests: []

comments without a matching user or with NULL role do not qualify; earliest time is chosen, and absence yields NULL. - Resolution timestamp from staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history: - Restrict to field_name equal to status (case-insensitive) and, per ticket_id, take the earliest updated timestamp where the status value is solved or closed (case-insensitive); ticket_id is treated as BIGINT for joining. - Final assembly: left join the comment aggregates and resolution timestamp to tickets by ticket_id. - first_response_minutes is the whole-minute difference between created_at and first_agent_public_reply_at; NULL if no qualifying reply. - resolution_minutes is the whole-minute difference between created_at and resolved_at; NULL if unresolved. - age_days is the whole-day difference between created_at and resolved_at if present, otherwise updated_at; NULL only if both are NULL. - Null handling and determinism: - If a ticket has no comment rows, all comment aggregates and any derived metrics depending on them are NULL. - Earliest timestamps are chosen deterministically; ties at identical times simply return that time. - Comparisons for role, field_name, and status values are case-insensitive. - Differences are integer units; negative values are possible if source timestamps are inconsistent. - No explicit ordering is applied in the final output.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zendesk__ticket_status_transitions
      description: Earliest timestamp a ticket first reached status 'solved' or 'closed' based on Zendesk status change history.
      grain: One row per ticket_id present in the filtered status history
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history
      business_logic: '- Keep only rows where field_name equals "status" when compared in lowercase; no trimming is applied. - For each kept row: set status to the lowercase of value; set valid_starting_at to the timestamp parsed from updated. - For each ticket_id, resolved_at is the earliest valid_starting_at among rows where status equals "solved" or "closed" when compared in lowercase. - If a ticket_id never has status "solved" or "closed", resolved_at is null. - Exact text matching is used after lowercasing; spaces or other characters are not trimmed. - All rows are considered; duplicates are not removed. - Output one row per ticket_id present in the filtered dataset.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Ticket identifier from the status history; one row per ticket_id in the filtered dataset.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest timestamp when the ticket first had status 'solved' or 'closed' (case-insensitive); null if never reached; duplicates are allowed and not de-duplicated.
        tests: []

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zendesk__updates
      description: Unified stream of ticket field-change and comment events with per-branch next-event end timestamps
      grain: One row per ticket change or comment event
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_field_history
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket
      - staging.stg_zendesk__ticket_comment
      business_logic: 'Build a unified event stream per ticket_id by combining field-change history with comments: - Field-change events: - From ticket field history, use ticket_id and user_id as BIGINT, field_name, value, and the field’s updated timestamp as TIMESTAMP. - Within each ticket, order field-change events by their updated timestamp; the starting time is the event’s updated timestamp, and the ending time is the updated timestamp of the next field-change event for the same ticket. If there is no later field-change event, the ending time is NULL. - The comment visibility flag is not applicable and is set to NULL. - If two field-change events share the same updated timestamp, which one is considered “next” is not specified. - Comment events: - From ticket comments, use ticket_id and user_id as BIGINT, body as value, is_public, and the comment’s created timestamp as TIMESTAMP. - Within each ticket, order comments by their created timestamp; the starting time is the comment’s created timestamp, and the ending time is the created timestamp of the next comment for the same ticket. If there is no later comment, the ending time is NULL. - The field_name is the literal value "comment". - If two comments share the same created timestamp, which one is considered “next” is not specified. - Combine the two event sets into a single table; all records are retained, duplicates are preserved, and the final output is not sorted. - Enrich each record with the ticket’s creation timestamp by matching on ticket_id; if the ticket does not exist, the creation timestamp is NULL. - Text values are preserved as stored; NULLs are carried through without substitution. Validity intervals are derived independently for field-change events and for comment events; field changes do not consider comment timestamps and vice versa.'
      columns:
      - name: ticket_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Ticket identifier (cast to BIGINT); grouping key for events
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: field_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Changed field name for history events; literal 'comment' for comment events
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: value
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'For field changes: the new value; for comments: the comment body; text preserved as stored and may be NULL'
        tests: []
      - name: is_public
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: 'For comments: comment visibility flag; for field-change events: always NULL'
        tests: []
      - name: user_id
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Actor who performed the change or authored the comment (cast to BIGINT); may be NULL
        tests: []
      - name: valid_starting_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Event timestamp: field changes use updated; comments use created_at; cast to TIMESTAMP'
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: valid_ending_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: 'Next event timestamp within the same branch and ticket: next field-change time for history, next comment time for comments; NULL if none; ties on equal timestamps are unordered'
        tests: []
      - name: ticket_created_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Ticket creation timestamp from tickets.created_at; NULL if the ticket row is missing
        tests: []

- name: int_zendesk__user_aggregates
      description: Combines Zendesk user attributes with per-user tag concatenation and a case-insensitive internal-role flag
      grain: One row per user_id from staging.stg_zendesk__user
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zendesk__user
      - staging.stg_zendesk__user_tag

- name: zendesk__ticket_enriched
      description: Ticket records enriched with requester, assignee, and organization attributes via left joins to user and organization aggregates.
      grain: One row per ticket_id from tickets; rows may duplicate if joined sources have multiple matches per key.
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_zendesk__ticket_aggregates
      - intermediate.int_zendesk__user_aggregates
      - intermediate.int_zendesk__organization_aggregates
      business_logic: '- Use intermediate.int_zendesk__ticket_aggregates as the base (alias t); emit one row per t.ticket_id from the base. - Build requester (alias r) from intermediate.int_zendesk__user_aggregates selecting: user_id → requester_id, name → requester_name, email → requester_email, is_internal_role → requester_is_internal, user_tags → requester_tags. - Build assignee (alias a) from intermediate.int_zendesk__user_aggregates selecting: user_id → assignee_id, name → assignee_name, email → assignee_email, is_internal_role → assignee_is_internal, user_tags → assignee_tags. - Build organization (alias o) from intermediate.int_zendesk__organization_aggregates selecting: organization_id, name → organization_name, organization_tags. - Perform LEFT JOINs: r on r.requester_id = t.requester_id; a on a.assignee_id = t.assignee_id; o on o.organization_id = t.organization_id. Equality joins use the raw values; no casting, trimming, case changes, filtering, or deduplication are applied. - Select the columns exactly as listed; values are passed through unchanged from their sources. - Null policy: - Joined columns are NULL when no matching row exists in the corresponding aggregate. - Base ticket columns retain any NULLs present in t. - Tag columns (requester_tags, assignee_tags, organization_tags, ticket_tags) are pre-aggregated strings from source; delimiter, ordering, duplicates, casing, and whitespace are preserved as provided. - No DISTINCT or ORDER BY is applied. If any joined source has multiple rows per join key, the LEFT JOIN produces multiple output rows for that ticket_id.'

      description: Pass-through per-ticket operational metrics selected directly from intermediate.int_zendesk__ticket_metrics
      grain: One row per source row from intermediate.int_zendesk__ticket_metrics
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_zendesk__ticket_metrics
      business_logic: '- Select all columns from intermediate.int_zendesk__ticket_metrics exactly as stored; no filters, joins, renames, casts, or transformations. - Grain: one row per source row; any uniqueness by ticket_id is inherited from the source and not enforced here. - Null policy: preserve source NULLs; no imputation or substitution. - Timestamps: passed through unchanged; timezone/offset preserved from source; no conversion applied. - Units: first_response_minutes and resolution_minutes are whole minutes; age_days is whole days; values are upstream-derived and not recomputed here. - Ordering: no ORDER BY applied; row order is unspecified and should not be relied upon. - Data types: mirror source types (DuckDB) for deterministic reproduction (BIGINT/HUGEINT/VARCHAR/TIMESTAMP).'

        description: Unique ticket identifier passed through from source; intended grouping key
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Ticket creation timestamp passed through; timezone/offset preserved; NULLs preserved
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: updated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Latest ticket update timestamp passed through; timezone/offset preserved; NULLs preserved
        tests: []
      - name: status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest ticket status string passed through; casing and whitespace preserved; NULLs preserved
        tests: []
      - name: comment_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total comments count passed through as-is; NULLs preserved
        tests:
        - comment_count >= 0
      - name: public_comment_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Public comments count passed through as-is; NULLs preserved
        tests:
        - public_comment_count >= 0
      - name: private_comment_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Private comments count passed through as-is; NULLs preserved
        tests:
        - private_comment_count >= 0
      - name: first_agent_public_reply_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp of the first public agent reply passed through; NULL if none; timezone/offset preserved

      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp when the ticket reached a terminal status passed through; NULL if unresolved; timezone/offset preserved

        description: Whole days from created_at to updated_at passed through; NULLs preserved

        - age_days IS NULL OR age_days >= 0

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zuora__billing_enriched
      description: Per-invoice aggregates from most-recent invoice items, taxes, payments, and credit balance adjustments
      grain: One row per invoice_id present in most-recent invoice items
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice_item
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice_payment
      - staging.stg_zuora__payment
      - staging.stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment
      - staging.stg_zuora__taxation_item
      business_logic: '- Keep only rows marked as most recent in each staging source. - Aggregate invoice items by invoice_id: - invoice_items: number of unique invoice_item_id; NULLs ignored. - products: number of unique product_id; NULLs ignored. - subscriptions: number of unique subscription_id; NULLs ignored. - discount_charges: total charge_amount for items where processing_type equals ''1'' (string compare); items not matching contribute 0; result is NULL if all qualifying amounts are NULL. - discount_charges_home_currency: same logic using charge_amount_home_currency. - units: total of quantity; NULLs ignored; NULL if all quantities are NULL. - first_charge_date: earliest charge_date; NULLs ignored. - most_recent_charge_date: latest charge_date; NULLs ignored. - invoice_service_start_date: earliest service_start_date; NULLs ignored. - invoice_service_end_date: latest service_end_date; NULLs ignored. - Taxes: per invoice_id, total tax_amount_home_currency across taxation items; NULLs ignored; NULL if no taxation items or all amounts are NULL. - Payments: join invoice_payment to payment on payment_id, then aggregate per invoice_id: - payments: number of unique payment_id; NULLs ignored. - invoice_amount_paid_home_currency: total of amount_home_currency with NULL or non-numeric treated as 0; NULL if no matched payments exist. - first_payment_date: earliest effective_date string (by string order); NULLs ignored; NULL if none. - most_recent_payment_date: latest effective_date string (by string order); NULLs ignored; NULL if none. - payment_methods: number of unique payment_method_id; NULLs ignored; 0 if all method IDs are NULL; NULL if no matched payments exist. - Credit balance adjustments: per invoice_id aggregate: - credit_balance_adjustments: number of unique credit_balance_adjustment_id; NULLs ignored. - credit_balance_adjustment_amount_home_currency: total of amount_home_currency; NULLs ignored; NULL if none or all amounts are NULL. - first_credit_balance_adjustment_date: earliest adjustment_date; NULLs ignored; NULL if none. - most_recent_credit_balance_adjustment_date: latest adjustment_date; NULLs ignored; NULL if none. - Final output starts from invoices with at least one most-recent invoice item and left joins taxes, payments, and credit aggregates on invoice_id; unmatched joins produce NULLs.'
      columns:
      - name: invoice_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Invoice identifier; one row per invoice_id from most-recent invoice items
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: invoice_items
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique invoice_item_id count from most-recent invoice items; NULLs ignored
        tests: []
      - name: products
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique product_id count from most-recent invoice items; NULLs ignored
        tests: []
      - name: subscriptions
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique subscription_id count from most-recent invoice items; NULLs ignored
        tests: []
      - name: discount_charges
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total charge_amount for items where processing_type='1'; non-matching items add 0; NULL if all qualifying amounts are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: discount_charges_home_currency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total charge_amount_home_currency for items where processing_type='1'; non-matching items add 0; NULL if all qualifying amounts are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: units
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total quantity across items; NULLs ignored; NULL if all quantities are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: first_charge_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest non-null charge_date across items; NULL if all are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: most_recent_charge_date
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Latest non-null charge_date across items; NULL if all are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_service_start_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Earliest non-null service_start_date across items; NULL if all are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_service_end_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Latest non-null service_end_date across items; NULL if all are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: tax_amount_home_currency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total tax_amount_home_currency from taxation items; NULL if none or all amounts are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: payments
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique payment_id count from payments linked via invoice_payment; NULL if none
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_amount_paid_home_currency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total of payment amounts in home currency with NULL or non-numeric treated as 0; NULL if no linked payments
        tests: []
      - name: first_payment_date
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Earliest effective_date string among linked payments (string order); NULL if none
        tests: []
      - name: most_recent_payment_date
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest effective_date string among linked payments (string order); NULL if none
        tests: []
      - name: payment_methods
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique payment_method_id count across linked payments; 0 if all method IDs are NULL; NULL if none
        tests: []
      - name: credit_balance_adjustments
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Unique credit_balance_adjustment_id count for the invoice_id; NULL if none
        tests: []
      - name: credit_balance_adjustment_amount_home_currency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total amount_home_currency across credit balance adjustments; NULL if none or all amounts are NULL
        tests: []
      - name: first_credit_balance_adjustment_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Earliest non-null adjustment_date across credit balance adjustments; NULL if none
        tests: []
      - name: most_recent_credit_balance_adjustment_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Latest non-null adjustment_date across credit balance adjustments; NULL if none
        tests: []

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zuora__invoice_base
      description: Invoice headers from the latest Zuora records with type casts and explicit past-due logic
      grain: One row per invoice_id from stg_zuora__invoice where is_most_recent_record = true
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice
      business_logic: '- Filter to rows where is_most_recent_record is true. - Cast created_date to TIMESTAMP as created_at; cast due_date to DATE; invoice_date is passed through. - Map fields: invoice_amount = amount; invoice_amount_home_currency = amount_home_currency; invoice_amount_paid = payment_amount; purchase_type = source_type. - Compute invoice_amount_unpaid as amount minus payment_amount; if either input is NULL, the result is NULL; can be negative if payments exceed the amount. - Pass through tax_amount, refund_amount, transaction_currency, home_currency, exchange_rate_date, status, account_id, invoice_number. - Compute total_amount_past_due using today''s calendar date (time ignored): - If today is strictly after due_date and amount differs from payment_amount, set total_amount_past_due to balance; otherwise set to 0.0. - If due_date is NULL, or amount or payment_amount is NULL, treat as not past due → 0.0. - If past due and balance is NULL, total_amount_past_due is NULL. - No aggregation or sorting; output is a direct row-wise transform of the filtered source.'
      columns:
      - name: invoice_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique invoice identifier; one row per latest invoice_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account linked to the invoice
        tests: []
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Timestamp derived from created_date
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_number
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Human-readable invoice number
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Invoice date from source
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_amount
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total invoice amount in transaction currency
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_amount_home_currency
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total invoice amount in home currency
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_amount_paid
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Amount paid to date in transaction currency
        tests: []
      - name: invoice_amount_unpaid
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Amount minus payment_amount; NULL if either is NULL; may be negative
        tests: []
      - name: tax_amount
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Tax amount in transaction currency
        tests: []
      - name: refund_amount
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Refund amount in transaction currency
        tests: []
      - name: transaction_currency
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: ISO currency of transaction amounts
        tests: []
      - name: home_currency
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: ISO home/reporting currency
        tests: []
      - name: exchange_rate_date
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Exchange rate date from source as text
        tests: []
      - name: due_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Invoice due date cast to DATE
        tests: []
      - name: status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Invoice status from source
        tests: []
      - name: purchase_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Purchase type from source_type
        tests: []
      - name: total_amount_past_due
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 0.0 unless today is after due_date and amount differs from payment_amount, then equals balance; NULL if balance is NULL when past due
        tests: []

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zuora__invoice_item_base
      description: Invoice line items filtered to latest records, with charge/service date buckets and discount amounts derived when processing_type='1'.
      grain: One row per source record where is_most_recent_record = TRUE
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice_item
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_zuora__invoice_item and keep only rows where is_most_recent_record is true. - Pass through all source fields unchanged. - Derive charge_day, charge_week, charge_month from charge_date: - charge_day is the calendar day; charge_week is the start date of the ISO week (Monday); charge_month is the first day of the calendar month. - If charge_date is null, all charge buckets are null. - Derive service_start_day, service_start_week, service_start_month from service_start_date with the same rules and null handling. - Compute discounts: - When processing_type equals the string ''1'', discount_amount_home_currency is the numeric value of charge_amount_home_currency and discount_amount is the numeric value of charge_amount. - When processing_type is not ''1'', both discount fields are set to 0.0. - If processing_type is ''1'' and the source amount is null, the corresponding discount field is null. No rounding or sign changes are applied. - No aggregation, deduplication, or ordering is performed; one output row per filtered source row.'

references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_zuora__invoice_item and keep only rows where is_most_recent_record is true. - Pass through all source fields unchanged. - Derive charge_day, charge_week, charge_month from charge_date: - charge_day is the calendar day; charge_week is the start date of the ISO week (Monday); charge_month is the first day of the calendar month. - If charge_date is null, all charge buckets are null. - Derive service_start_day, service_start_week, service_start_month from service_start_date with the same rules and null handling. - Compute discounts: - When processing_type equals the string ''1'', discount_amount_home_currency is the numeric value of charge_amount_home_currency and discount_amount is the numeric value of charge_amount. - When processing_type is not ''1'', both discount fields are set to 0.0. - If processing_type is ''1'' and the source amount is null, the corresponding discount field is null. No rounding or sign changes are applied. - No aggregation, deduplication, or ordering is performed; one output row per filtered source row.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zuora__mrr_date_spine
      description: Continuous daily spine from the minimum to maximum day-level service_start_date among most recent Zuora invoice items.
      grain: One row per date_day
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice_item (service_start_date, is_most_recent_record)
      business_logic: '- Filter the invoice items to rows marked as the most recent record. - Determine the earliest and latest service_start_date after truncating to the day. - Generate a consecutive daily series from the earliest to the latest day, inclusive. - For each day in the series: - date_day: the calendar day (date only). - date_week: the first day of that week, with weeks starting on Monday (DuckDB default). - date_month: the first day of that month. - date_year: the first day of that year. - date_index: assign 1 to the earliest day and increment by 1 for each subsequent day in ascending order, with no gaps. - The output has one unique row per date_day, ordered ascending. - Null policy: - Null service_start_date values are ignored when determining bounds. - If no non-null service_start_date exists after filtering, the result contains no rows.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar day from the generated spine; unique and ascending.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: date_week
        data_type: DATE
        description: Start date of the week (Monday) for the given date_day.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: date_month
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the month corresponding to date_day.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: date_year
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the year corresponding to date_day.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: date_index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Sequential 1-based index by ascending date_day; strictly consecutive without gaps.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zuora__transaction_date_spine
      description: Continuous daily date spine from Zuora invoices with week/month/year buckets and a sequential index.
      grain: One row per calendar day between min and max invoice_date (inclusive)
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice (invoice_date, is_most_recent_record)
      business_logic: '- Start from staging.stg_zuora__invoice and keep only rows where is_most_recent_record is true. - Determine bounds: - min_date = the minimum invoice_date truncated to the calendar day. - max_date = the maximum invoice_date truncated to the calendar day. - Null invoice_date values do not affect these bounds; if no qualifying rows exist, both bounds are null. - Generate a continuous daily series from min_date to max_date inclusive with a 1-day step; if either bound is null, return no rows. - For each generated day: - date_day = that calendar day. - date_week = the start of the week for date_day (Monday). - date_month = the first day of the month for date_day. - date_year = the first day of the year for date_day. - date_index = a 1-based sequential counter ordered by date_day ascending, contiguous with no gaps.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar day generated from the inclusive min and max invoice_date bounds.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: date_week
        data_type: DATE
        description: Start of the week (Monday) for date_day.
        tests: []
      - name: date_month
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the month for date_day.
        tests: []
      - name: date_year
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the year for date_day.
        tests: []
      - name: date_index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: 1-based sequential index by date_day ascending; strictly increasing and unique.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_zuora__transactions_grouped
      description: Daily Zuora invoice-based transaction aggregates per account with day/week/month/year buckets.
      grain: One row per account_id per date_day
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice
      - staging.stg_zuora__invoice_item
      business_logic: '- Keep only records flagged as most recent from both invoices and invoice items. - Invoices use: invoice_id, account_id, invoice_date, amount, payment_amount, refund_amount. - Invoice items use: invoice_id, invoice_item_id. - For each invoice, count unique invoice_item_id values to get its item count; null item IDs do not contribute. - Left join per-invoice item counts to invoices by invoice_id so invoices without items are retained. - Derive calendar buckets from invoice_date: - date_day: the calendar date (time removed). - date_week: Monday of the week containing the date. - date_month: first day of the calendar month. - date_year: first day of the calendar year. - Group by account_id and the four time buckets (equivalent to account_id by date_day) and compute: - daily_invoices: number of unique invoices in the group; missing invoice IDs do not count. - daily_invoice_items: sum of each invoice’s unique item count; invoices with no items contribute 0; if none have items the result is 0. - daily_invoice_amount: total of invoice amounts; null amounts are ignored; result is null if no non-null amounts exist in the group. - daily_invoice_amount_paid: total of payment amounts; nulls are ignored; result is null if all are null. - daily_invoice_amount_unpaid: for each invoice take amount minus payment amount, then total; if either value is null for an invoice it contributes nothing; result is null if all are null. - daily_refunds: total of refund amounts; nulls are ignored; result is null if all are null. - Output one row per account_id and date_day; other date buckets are deterministic functions of invoice_date for that row.'
      columns:
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Zuora account identifier used to group aggregates.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date from invoice_date with time removed.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: date_week
        data_type: DATE
        description: Monday of the week containing invoice_date.
      - name: date_month
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the month containing invoice_date.
      - name: date_year
        data_type: DATE
        description: First day of the year containing invoice_date.
      - name: daily_invoices
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct invoice count for the account and date_day; missing invoice IDs do not count.
      - name: daily_invoice_items
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of per-invoice unique item counts; invoices with no items contribute 0 and result is 0 if none have items.
      - name: daily_invoice_amount
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total invoice amounts for the group; null amounts are ignored and result is null if all are null.
      - name: daily_invoice_amount_paid
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total payment amounts for the group; nulls are ignored and result is null if all are null.
      - name: daily_invoice_amount_unpaid
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total of per-invoice (amount minus payment); invoices with null in either value contribute nothing; result is null if all are null.
      - name: daily_refunds
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total refund amounts for the group; nulls are ignored and result is null if all are null.

blocks.original_text:
- name: zuora__account_overview
      description: Account-level overview combining current account fields, current contact fields, invoice aggregates, and invoice item counts
      grain: One row per account_id present in int_zuora__account_current
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_zuora__account_current
      - intermediate.int_zuora__contact_current
      - intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base
      - intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_item_base
      - intermediate.int_zuora__billing_enriched
      business_logic: '- Base: Start from intermediate.int_zuora__account_current (assumed one current row per account_id). - Contact: Left join intermediate.int_zuora__contact_current on account_id; if no contact row, all contact fields are NULL. - Invoice item count: - Build items_by_account by joining intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base to intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_item_base on invoice_id, then counting distinct invoice_item_id per account_id. - Left join items_by_account to accounts. The count reflects distinct item IDs across all invoices of the account. If an account has invoices but none have items, the count is 0. If an account has no invoices, there is no items_by_account row and the joined count is NULL. - Invoice aggregates: - Build per_invoice by left joining intermediate.int_zuora__billing_enriched to intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base on invoice_id, then grouping by account_id to compute: - first_charge_date: earliest non-NULL first_charge_date across the account’s invoices. - total_amount_paid: sum of invoice_amount_paid. - total_amount_not_paid: sum of invoice_amount_unpaid. - total_taxes: sum of tax_amount. - total_invoice_amount: sum of invoice_amount. - Summations skip NULL inputs per row; if an account has invoices but all values for a summed field are NULL, the result is NULL. If an account has no invoices, no per_invoice row exists and all joined aggregates are NULL. - Invoice count: - Compute per account_id using a correlated subquery over intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base that counts distinct invoices; returns 0 when no invoices exist. - Output: - Select pass-through account fields, joined contact fields, per_invoice.first_charge_date as first_charge_processed_at, items_by_account.invoice_item_count, the scalar invoice_count, and the per_invoice totals. No zero-coalescing, rounding, or casting; all joins from accounts are left joins.'
      columns:
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account identifier from int_zuora__account_current; exactly one output row per account_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: account_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Account created_date from int_zuora__account_current
      - name: account_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account name from int_zuora__account_current
      - name: account_number
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account number from int_zuora__account_current
      - name: account_credit_balance

references.name: intermediate.int_zuora__account_current
references.line_text: business_logic: '- Base: Start from intermediate.int_zuora__account_current (assumed one current row per account_id). - Contact: Left join intermediate.int_zuora__contact_current on account_id; if no contact row, all contact fields are NULL. - Invoice item count: - Build items_by_account by joining intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base to intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_item_base on invoice_id, then counting distinct invoice_item_id per account_id. - Left join items_by_account to accounts. The count reflects distinct item IDs across all invoices of the account. If an account has invoices but none have items, the count is 0. If an account has no invoices, there is no items_by_account row and the joined count is NULL. - Invoice aggregates: - Build per_invoice by left joining intermediate.int_zuora__billing_enriched to intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base on invoice_id, then grouping by account_id to compute: - first_charge_date: earliest non-NULL first_charge_date across the account’s invoices. - total_amount_paid: sum of invoice_amount_paid. - total_amount_not_paid: sum of invoice_amount_unpaid. - total_taxes: sum of tax_amount. - total_invoice_amount: sum of invoice_amount. - Summations skip NULL inputs per row; if an account has invoices but all values for a summed field are NULL, the result is NULL. If an account has no invoices, no per_invoice row exists and all joined aggregates are NULL. - Invoice count: - Compute per account_id using a correlated subquery over intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base that counts distinct invoices; returns 0 when no invoices exist. - Output: - Select pass-through account fields, joined contact fields, per_invoice.first_charge_date as first_charge_processed_at, items_by_account.invoice_item_count, the scalar invoice_count, and the per_invoice totals. No zero-coalescing, rounding, or casting; all joins from accounts are left joins.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: zuora__billing_history
      description: Invoice-level snapshot joining invoice_base with billing_enriched; includes invoice attributes plus item, tax, payment, and credit metrics.
      grain: One row per invoice_id from intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base
      - intermediate.int_zuora__billing_enriched
      business_logic: '- Load invoices from intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_base and billing metrics from intermediate.int_zuora__billing_enriched. - Left join on invoice_id, retaining all invoices; if no billing match exists, all billing-derived fields are NULL. - Project all selected invoice_base fields unchanged. - Project all selected billing_enriched fields unchanged. - Compute invoice_amount_unpaid_home_currency as the invoice home-currency amount minus the paid amount in home currency; if either input is NULL, the result is NULL; no rounding or currency conversion is applied. - No explicit row ordering is applied.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: zuora__line_item_enhanced
      description: Zuora invoice line items enriched with invoice, payment, product, subscription, and customer attributes; duplicates can occur from one-to-many joins
      grain: One row per joined combination of a line item with matching invoice_payment, contact, and rate_plan rows for its invoice/account/subscription
      source_models:
      - int_zuora__invoice_item_base
      - int_zuora__account_current
      - int_zuora__contact_current
      - int_zuora__invoice_base
      - int_zuora__invoice_payment_current
      - int_zuora__payment_current
      - int_zuora__payment_method_current
      - int_zuora__product_current
      - int_zuora__subscription_current
      - int_zuora__rate_plan_current
      business_logic: 'Start from invoice line items. Enrich via LEFT JOINs: - Invoices by invoice_id to bring created_at, status, purchase_type, refund_amount. - Invoice payments by invoice_id to bring payment_id and payment_method_id. - Payments by payment_id to bring effective_date and the related payment_method_id. - Payment methods by the payment''s payment_method_id to bring payment_method_name. - Accounts by account_id to bring account created_date and name. - Contacts by account_id to bring first_name, last_name, work_email, city, country; all matching contacts are retained (no primary-contact filter). - Products by product_id to bring product name and category. - Subscriptions by subscription_id to bring start/end dates (converted to timestamp) and status. - Rate plans by subscription_id to bring rate_plan name. Multiplicity and duplicates: - Multiple rows can result per line item when an invoice has multiple payments, an account has multiple contacts, and/or a subscription has multiple rate plans; these multiplicities combine across those dimensions. Derived/transform rules: - line_item_index: assign a 1-based sequence within each invoice, ordered by line_item_id ascending across the final result; order among identical line_item_id values is non-deterministic. - transaction_type: interpret processing_type as a string where ''0''→charge, ''1''→discount, ''2''→prepayment, ''3''→tax; otherwise NULL. - discount_amount: for discount rows (processing_type=''1''), set to charge_amount converted to double; otherwise 0.0; if charge_amount is NULL on a discount row, the result is NULL. - customer_level: constant value ''customer''. - customer_name: concatenate contact first name, a single space, and last name; if either name part is NULL, the result is NULL; no trimming or case changes. - Subscription period fields: convert subscription start and end dates to timestamp. Pass-through fields (carried as stored, no normalization): quantity, unit_amount (unit_price), tax_amount, total_amount (charge_amount), currency, payment_at (payments.effective_date). Null policy: - All joins are LEFT joins from line items; unmatched enrichments yield NULLs. - Pass-through fields preserve NULLs from the source.'
      columns:
      - name: header_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Invoice header id from line_items.invoice_id
      - name: line_item_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Invoice item id from line_items.invoice_item_id
      - name: line_item_index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: 1-based sequence within each header_id ordered by line_item_id ascending across the final result; order among identical line_item_id values is non-deterministic
      - name: line_item_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Creation timestamp from line_items.created_date
      - name: invoice_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Invoice creation timestamp from invoices.created_at
      - name: header_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Invoice status from invoices.status
      - name: billing_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Invoice purchase type from invoices.purchase_type
      - name: currency
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Transaction currency from line_items.transaction_currency (verbatim)
      - name: product_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Product id from line_items.product_id
      - name: product_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Product name from products.name; NULL if no product match
      - name: product_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Product category from products.category; NULL if no product match
      - name: transaction_type
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Processing type mapped to charge, discount, prepayment, or tax; NULL if unmapped
      - name: quantity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Quantity from line_items.quantity (verbatim string; NULLs preserved)
      - name: unit_amount
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unit price from line_items.unit_price (verbatim string; NULLs preserved)
      - name: discount_amount
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: For discount rows set to charge_amount as DOUBLE, otherwise 0.0; NULL if charge_amount is NULL on a discount row
      - name: tax_amount
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Tax amount from line_items.tax_amount (verbatim string; NULLs preserved)
      - name: total_amount
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Total/charge amount from line_items.charge_amount (verbatim string; NULLs preserved)
      - name: payment_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Payment id from invoice_payments.payment_id; NULL if no related invoice_payment
      - name: payment_method_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Payment method id from invoice_payments.payment_method_id; NULL if no related invoice_payment
      - name: payment_method
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Payment method name from payment_methods.payment_method_name via the joined payment; NULL if no related payment or method
      - name: payment_at
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Payment effective date/time from payments.effective_date (verbatim string; NULL if no related payment)
      - name: refund_amount
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Refund amount from invoices.refund_amount; NULL if no invoice match
      - name: subscription_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Subscription id from line_items.subscription_id
      - name: subscription_plan
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Rate plan name from rate_plan.name; duplicates occur if multiple rate plans per subscription
      - name: subscription_period_started_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Subscription start timestamp converted from subscriptions.subscription_start_date
      - name: subscription_period_ended_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Subscription end timestamp converted from subscriptions.subscription_end_date
      - name: subscription_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Subscription status from subscriptions.status; NULL if no subscription match
      - name: customer_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer account id from line_items.account_id
      - name: customer_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Constant 'customer'
      - name: customer_created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Customer account creation timestamp from accounts.created_date
      - name: customer_company
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer company/account name from accounts.name
      - name: customer_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Full name from contact first and last name separated by a space; NULL if either name part is NULL; no trimming
      - name: customer_email
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer email from contacts.work_email; NULL if no contact match
      - name: customer_city
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer city from contacts.city; NULL if no contact match
      - name: customer_country
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Customer country from contacts.country; NULL if no contact match
